summary: PANDA was trained on non-contrast abdominal CT scans from 3,208 patients at a high-volume pancreatic cancer centre in Shanghai. In a retrospective evaluation of 20,530 consecutive patients across four clinical settings, the paper reports 92.9% sensitivity and 99.9% specificity for pancreatic lesion detection. The study also reports five cancers and 26 other pancreatic lesions missed by the initial standard of care. These results do not establish population-screening benefit; the authors call for prospective risk-benefit and cost-effectiveness studies and broader international validation.
ai_technology: PANDA (three-stage deep learning cascade on non-contrast CT)
organization: DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group; Shanghai Institute of Pancreatic Diseases; First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University

title: Virchow: pan-cancer detection using a pathology foundation model
summary: Using Virchow pathology-model embeddings, a pan-cancer detector achieved a specimen-level AUC of 0.95 across nine common and seven rare cancer types. The held-out evaluation included 6,142 specimens from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and external institutions. Separate comparisons approached the performance of tissue-specific clinical products and exceeded them on some rare variants. This is diagnostic validation on existing specimens, not evidence that the Virchow detector itself was deployed or improved patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Virchow (vision transformer foundation model for pathology)
organization: Paige; Microsoft Research; Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

title: PI-CAI: AI matches or beats radiologists in prostate cancer detection on MRI
summary: In a reader study with 62 radiologists on 400 cases, the AI detected about 6.8% more clinically significant cancers at the same specificity and produced about 50% fewer false positives. On 1,000 routine-practice cases, however, non-inferiority was not confirmed (specificity 68.9% vs 69.0% at 96.1% sensitivity). The authors call for prospective validation, and the system is not available for clinical use.
ai_technology: PI-CAI challenge super-algorithm (ensemble of top five submitted deep learning models)
organization: PI-CAI consortium; Radboud University Medical Center

title: EchoNext: detecting structural heart disease from ECGs with AI
summary: EchoNext was trained on more than one million heart-rhythm and imaging records to detect structural heart disease. The journal abstract reports internal and external validation, a controlled comparison outperforming cardiologists, and prospective clinical-trial evaluation in patients without previous cardiac imaging that identified undiagnosed disease. This supports a screening study, not proof that deployment improves patient outcomes. The authors also released model weights and an annotated dataset.
ai_technology: EchoNext (deep learning model on 12-lead ECG)
organization: Columbia University; NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital

title: Conversations with an AI chatbot durably reduce conspiracy beliefs
summary: Across experiments with more than 2,000 participants, three dialogues with GPT-4 reduced belief in the targeted conspiracy theory by about 20%, and the effect persisted for two months and spilled over to unrelated conspiracies. A professional fact-checker rated 99.2% of 128 sampled chatbot claims as true. Caveats: lab setting, the chatbot did not reduce belief in true conspiracies, and most participants still held the hoax belief.
ai_technology: GPT-4 (DebunkBot dialogue system)
organization: MIT Sloan School of Management; Cornell University; American University

title: Instantaneous voice-synthesis neuroprosthesis for a man with ALS
summary: A brain-computer interface decoding 256 microelectrodes in the ventral precentral gyrus synthesized the participant's intended voice causally, with a reported latency of about 10 ms per decoding step. Listeners understood almost 60% of synthesized words, compared with 4% when he was not using the device, and he could modulate intonation and sing short melodies. Caveat: a single participant with ALS, within the BrainGate2 trial, and the authors describe the technology as early stage.
ai_technology: Deep neural network speech decoder for intracortical recordings
organization: UC Davis; Stanford University; BrainGate consortium

title: Centaur: a foundation model that predicts human behaviour across psychology experiments
summary: Fine-tuning Llama 3.1 70B on Psych-101, a dataset of about 10 million human choices from 160 psychology experiments, produced a model that predicts and simulates human behaviour in experiments expressed in natural language, including tasks it had not seen. The authors report that its internal representations align better with human neural activity after fine-tuning. Caveat: a 2025 critique argues that its language comprehension is limited and that it fails to follow altered instructions.
ai_technology: Centaur (Llama 3.1 70B fine-tuned on Psych-101)
organization: Helmholtz Munich; Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics; University of Tübingen

title: Generative agents built from interview transcripts simulate 1,000 people
summary: LLM agents built from participants' full interview transcripts reproduced their General Social Survey answers at about 85% of the rate at which participants reproduced their own answers two weeks later, a normalized score. They also matched personality and economic-game results (normalized correlations of about 0.80 and 0.66) and replicated four of five behavioural experiments. Caveat: arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed, and the results are normalized rather than raw accuracy.
ai_technology: Generative agent architecture with LLM and full interview transcripts
organization: Stanford University; Google DeepMind; Northwestern University; University of Washington

title: Deep learning maps Angkorian-period reservoirs beyond Greater Angkor
summary: A DeepLabV3+ segmentation model trained on about 3,600 high-quality samples from over 11,000 candidates mapped Angkor-period reservoirs in satellite imagery across the wider Angkorian realm. The best F1 score reached 45% in favourable regions, comparable to a trained human interpreter. The authors present the model as a second opinion for landscape archaeologists that requires human validation.
ai_technology: DeepLabV3+ semantic segmentation
organization: Leiden University; University of Toronto; University of Colorado Boulder

title: Mind captioning: text descriptions of viewed videos decoded from fMRI
summary: In six participants, a language-model pipeline translated fMRI responses to viewed videos into descriptions of their semantic content. Video identification reached about 50% among 100 candidates, compared with 1% chance. Results also extended to instructed video recall and persisted when the canonical language network was excluded, supporting a shared semantic representation beyond that network. The experiment used extensive participant-specific training; it was not unrestricted reading of private thoughts or a clinical aphasia trial.
ai_technology: Deep language model semantic-feature decoder with text generation search
organization: NTT Communication Science Laboratories

title: The levers of political persuasion with conversational AI
summary: In three large experiments with 76,977 participants, 19 LLMs argued 707 British political positions in dialogue. Persuasiveness was driven mainly by information density, while tailoring to user traits added little, and post-training for persuasion raised effectiveness by up to 50%. The most persuasive models also produced the most inaccurate claims. Caveat: the persuasion effects are measured in survey experiments, and accuracy was tested on a subset of claims.
ai_technology: 19 open and closed LLMs (including GPT-4.5, GPT-4o, Grok-3)
organization: University of Oxford; UK AI Security Institute; London School of Economics; Stanford University; MIT

title: RAVEN pipeline validates 118 new TESS planets and vets over 2,000 candidates
summary: A pipeline combining box least squares detection with machine-learning classifiers, trained on realistic simulations, searched 2.2 million TESS main-sequence stars in full-frame images (sectors 1 to 55). It newly validates 118 planets, 31 of them newly detected, and vets over 2,000 candidates, about 1,000 of them new. The machine-learning classifier is a validation tool rather than the detection method, and the paper is a preprint accepted for MNRAS; the peer-reviewed publication date was not confirmed.
ai_technology: RAVEN: box least squares detection with machine-learning vetting classifiers trained on simulations
organization: Warwick University; and collaborators

title: Physics-tailored machine learning reveals unexpected non-reciprocal forces in dusty plasmas
summary: A neural network built with physical constraints was trained on 3D particle-tracking data from a laboratory dusty plasma to infer the interaction forces between particles. The method describes the non-reciprocal forces more precisely than before and shows that some common theoretical assumptions about them are inaccurate. The authors checked their inferred force laws against laboratory experiments, which strengthens the claim, though the result comes from a single experimental system.
ai_technology: Physics-tailored neural network for inferring force laws from particle trajectories
organization: Emory University

title: Machine-learning alert flags supernova 2023zkd as a black hole and star binary merger
summary: The LAISS machine-learning alert system flagged the transient SN 2023zkd months before its most unusual behaviour, and the team then analysed its four-year optical precursor. The authors conclude that a massive, partly stripped helium star merged with a black hole companion, with the second light peak explained by a collision with a dense disk-like cloud. The ML step only prioritised the event; the physical interpretation is model-based, and outlets give conflicting accounts of who first detected it.
ai_technology: LAISS machine-learning anomaly alert for transient detection
organization: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian; MIT; University of California Santa Cruz; Young Supernova Experiment

title: First-principles neural network finds crystallization of fractional quantum Hall liquids
summary: A self-attention neural-network wavefunction (MagNet), trained only by minimising the microscopic Hamiltonian of interacting electrons in a magnetic field, finds both topological liquid and electron-crystal ground states across a range of Landau-level mixing. The authors present it as a method that discovers correlated phases without assumptions. This is an arXiv preprint with computational results only, not yet checked experimentally or peer reviewed.
ai_technology: MagNet: self-attention neural-network variational wavefunction
organization: MIT

title: Deep-learning CADe colonoscopy raises adenoma detection in a double-blind trial
summary: In a double-blind randomised trial of 962 patients in China (484 analysed with CADe, 478 with a sham system), the deep-learning system raised adenoma detection to 34% (165/484) from 28% (132/478), OR 1.36 (95% CI 1.03-1.79). The primary analysis was per protocol, the trial was single-centre, and the abstract reports no ITT analysis.
ai_technology: Deep-learning computer-aided detection (CADe) system for polyps during colonoscopy
organization: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences and Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital; Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center

title: COMPOSER sepsis model flags unfamiliar cases instead of guessing
summary: COMPOSER, a deep-learning early sepsis predictor, reached AUCs of 0.925-0.953 in ICU and 0.938-0.945 in ED across six cohorts (515,720 patients) from two US health systems. About 20% of non-septic and 8% of septic prediction windows were marked indeterminate, and the model gave a median early warning of 12.2 hours in ICU and 2.1 hours in ED before the first antibiotics order. The abstract reports no prospective deployment or patient-outcome results.
ai_technology: COMPOSER deep-learning model with uncertainty-based indeterminate output
organization: University of California San Diego

title: Combining AI algorithms with radiologists improves mammography specificity
summary: An international crowdsourced challenge (over 1,100 participants, 126 teams, 44 countries) tested AI on screening mammograms from 144,231 US and 166,578 Swedish examinations. The best single algorithm did not beat radiologists (US AUC 0.858), but an ensemble of top algorithms combined with US radiologists' recall decisions reached AUC 0.942 and 92.0% specificity at the same sensitivity. The study is retrospective, uses challenge data and does not report recall rates.
ai_technology: Ensemble of crowdsourced deep-learning mammography algorithms combined with radiologist recall
organization: Sage Bionetworks; and DREAM challenge collaborators, with US and Swedish screening programmes

title: Deep learning detects pancreatic cancer on CT in a nationwide study
summary: A deep-learning tool for contrast-enhanced CT reached 89.9% sensitivity and 95.9% specificity in an internal test set (not significantly different from the original radiologist reports, 96.1%). On 1,473 real-world Taiwanese CT studies it reached 89.7% sensitivity and 92.8% specificity, but sensitivity for cancers under 2 cm was 74.7%. The study is retrospective, with no prospective reader comparison in the abstract.
ai_technology: Segmentation CNN with an ensemble of five CNN classifiers for pancreatic cancer on CT
organization: National Taiwan University Hospital; National Taiwan University

title: CNN distinguishes pancreatic cancer on contrast CT with cross-racial validation
summary: A CNN trained on contrast-enhanced CT from a Taiwanese centre reached 98.3% sensitivity on combined local test sets versus 92.9% for radiologists (difference 5.4 points, p=0.014). On a US external test set, sensitivity fell to 79.0% with specificity 97.6% (AUC 0.920), and sensitivity for tumours under 2 cm was 63.1% in that set. The study is retrospective and the authors describe it as supplementary to radiologists.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network applied to CT image patches
organization: National Taiwan University; National Taiwan University Hospital

title: Med-BERT pretrained on structured health records improves disease prediction
summary: Med-BERT, a transformer pretrained on structured EHR data from 28,490,650 patients, improved AUC by 1.21% to 6.14% across two disease-prediction tasks compared with prior baselines. The gains are reported on retrospective structured-data tasks, and the abstract gives no clinical deployment or outcome results.
ai_technology: Med-BERT, BERT-style transformer pretrained on structured electronic health records
organization: University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

title: Self-reported symptom app predicts likely COVID-19 infection in real time
summary: A COVID Symptom Study app with 2,618,862 participants and 18,401 tested users found loss of smell or taste in 65.03% of positives versus 21.71% of negatives (OR 6.74). A machine-learning model applied to 805,753 users predicted 140,312 (17.42%) as likely infected. The inputs are self-reported and the test-verified subset is small relative to the user base, so the prediction is not a clinical diagnosis.
ai_technology: Machine-learning symptom model on self-reported app data
organization: King's College London; Massachusetts General Hospital

title: COVNet deep learning separates COVID-19 from other pneumonia on chest CT
summary: The COVNet 3D deep-learning model, trained on 4,352 CT scans from 3,322 patients, reached per-scan sensitivity 90% and specificity 96% (AUC 0.96) for COVID-19, and AUC 0.95 for community-acquired pneumonia. The study is retrospective and evaluated on Chinese cohorts, so performance in other populations is not established.
ai_technology: COVNet, a 3D convolutional neural network on chest CT
organization: Wuhan Huangpi People's Hospital; Wuhan Pulmonary Hospital; Liaocheng People's Hospital

title: AI augmentation lifts radiologists in telling COVID-19 from other pneumonia
summary: A CT model trained on 1,186 patients (521 COVID-19, 665 other pneumonia) reached 95% sensitivity and 96% specificity internally, and AUC 0.90 on an independent test set. Radiologist accuracy rose from 85% to 90% with AI assistance. The study is retrospective and the independent-test performance is lower than the internal result.
ai_technology: Deep-learning CT classifier used as an assistant for radiologists
organization: Xiangya Hospital, Central South University; Rhode Island Hospital; University of Pennsylvania

title: PENet detects pulmonary embolism on volumetric CT angiography
summary: PENet, a 3D deep-learning model for pulmonary embolism on CT angiography, reached AUROC 0.84 on an internal hold-out test and 0.85 on data from one unnamed external institution. The abstract does not report sensitivity, specificity or study size, and the external validation is limited to a single site.
ai_technology: PENet, 3D deep convolutional network on volumetric CT
organization: Stanford University

title: Deep neural networks diagnose brain tumours in minutes from stimulated Raman histology
summary: CNNs trained on over 2.5 million stimulated Raman histology images produced intraoperative brain tumour diagnoses in under 150 seconds, with 94.6% accuracy versus 93.9% for pathologists. The accuracy comparison comes from a prospective multicentre trial with 278 patients, but the abstract does not report sensitivity or specificity separately.
ai_technology: Deep neural networks on stimulated Raman histology images
organization: University of Michigan; Columbia University; University of Miami

title: Fusing CT images and EHR data with deep learning improves pulmonary embolism detection
summary: A deep multimodal network combining CT imaging with electronic health record data reached AUROC 0.947 (95% CI 0.946-0.948) on a held-out test set for pulmonary embolism. The abstract reports no sensitivity, specificity, study size or external validation sites, so the evidence is limited to retrospective internal testing.
ai_technology: Multimodal deep neural network fusing CT and EHR data
organization: Stanford University

title: Satellite model maps collapse and surviving Acropora corals in Belize
summary: A supervised Random Tree classifier on satellite images predicted a drop of over 90% in live Acropora cover at Belize from 2011 to 2023 across 25 km². Field searches in June 2025 found live or recently dead colonies at 28 of 42 predicted sites and live colonies at 16 previously undocumented locations. The field check was a search for survivors at sites the model flagged, not a blind test.
ai_technology: Random Tree supervised classification of satellite imagery (machine learning)
organization: Washington and Lee University; Macalester College

title: YOLO detector tracks endangered European hamster activity in camera traps
summary: A YOLO object-detection model trained on 2023 camera-trap videos detected European hamsters with an F1-score of 0.93 and accuracy of 0.93. Its activity profile matched human annotation and showed peak activity at dusk and a secondary peak before sunrise. The evidence covers one season at one monitoring setup, so generalization to other sites is untested.
ai_technology: YOLO object detection (deep learning)
organization: Goethe University Frankfurt

title: BirdNET embeddings distinguish individual North Atlantic right whales
summary: Audio embeddings from the BirdNET model robustly distinguished individual North Atlantic right whales in upcall recordings from 234 samples across 11 individuals at 3 sites. Simulations showed that an extra 7 dB or more of signal excess is needed to identify individuals under ambient noise. The study uses on-animal archival tags on an endangered species, but the sample is small and the model was not trained for whales.
ai_technology: BirdNET audio embeddings (deep learning)
organization: Cornell K. Lisa Yang Center for Conservation Bioacoustics; Oregon State University; Syracuse University

title: FluEmbed predicts H3N2 antigenic drift from sequence alone
summary: FluEmbed, a protein language model framework, predicted influenza A (H3N2) antigenicity from RNA sequence with Spearman correlations of 0.67 to 0.80 against hemagglutination inhibition titers. It outperformed Hamming, BLOSUM62 and phylogenetic baselines, and in-silico mutagenesis showed unconstrained mutations carry greater escape potential outside dominant lineages. Validation uses existing HI assay data and retrospective sequences; no new wet-lab tests were run.
ai_technology: FluEmbed (protein language model embeddings)
organization: University of Georgia

title: Unsupervised machine learning identifies palladium catalysts that form dinuclear complexes
summary: A workflow built on only five experimental data points screened 348 phosphine ligands and predicted ligands that favour dinuclear Pd(I) complexes over Pd(0) and Pd(II) species. The authors experimentally verified the predictions, including ligands that had never been synthesized before. The evidence is limited to the Pd speciation system studied, not a general catalyst performance gain.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine learning workflow with clustering on generalized parameter databases and in silico data
organization: RWTH Aachen University; University of Jyväskylä

title: Autonomous robotic system maps Bi2O3 synthesis phase diagram with active learning
summary: The SARA agent combined robotic laser spike annealing, optical characterization and nested active learning to map synthesis phase boundaries of Bi2O3. It reached orders-of-magnitude faster establishment of the phase diagram and identified conditions that stabilize metastable delta-Bi2O3. Validation is experimental but restricted to one oxide system.
ai_technology: Scientific Autonomous Reasoning Agent (SARA) with hierarchical active learning and uncertainty quantification
organization: Cornell University; University of Bern; California Institute of Technology

title: Retrosynthetic software finds experimentally validated supply routes for umifenovir
summary: Retrosynthesis software proposed alternative chemical supply routes for the antiviral umifenovir and eleven other antiviral and anti-inflammatory drugs. The authors experimentally validated four routes to umifenovir and one route to bromhexine, one of which converts six C-H bonds. The work is a proof of route feasibility for supply-chain resilience, not a new therapeutic claim.
ai_technology: Computer-aided retrosynthesis software with exclusion of known starting materials
organization: University of Michigan; MilliporeSigma; Entos, Inc.

title: Machine-learned design of CuPd nanocubes for electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia
summary: Interpretable machine learning identified ordered B2 CuPd intermetallics whose adsorption energies break the usual scaling relations. The team synthesized monodisperse CuPd nanocubes that reached a 92.5% Faradaic efficiency at -0.5 V RHE for nitrate reduction to ammonia, with a yield of 6.25 mol h-1 g-1 at -0.6 V. Performance was measured in the authors' own electrochemical tests, and the design rules come from a limited set of predicted intermetallics.
ai_technology: Interpretable machine learning on d-state Pauli repulsion descriptors (DFT-based)
organization: Virginia Tech; National University of Singapore; Argonne National Laboratory

title: Earth-abundant Ni3Mo alloy outperforms platinum for ethane dehydrogenation
summary: A microkinetic and high-throughput screen of 1,998 bimetallic alloys, combined with machine-learning concepts, shortlisted noble-metal-free catalysts for selective ethane dehydrogenation. The predicted Ni3Mo alloy was synthesized and experimentally shown to outperform Pt in selective ethylene production. The machine-learning role is secondary to the descriptor-based workflow, and the evidence is a single catalyst test.
ai_technology: Descriptor-based microkinetic modeling with high-throughput DFT and machine learning
organization: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory (SUNCAT); Westlake University; Lanzhou Institute of Chemical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: COVID Moonshot uses synthesis-directed de novo design for SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors
summary: A machine-learning de novo design model was coupled with synthesis route prediction in the COVID Moonshot campaign against the SARS-CoV-2 main protease. The authors report novel chemical scaffolds that are active in biochemical and live-virus assays and were synthesized along model-generated routes. The abstract gives no potency figures, so the strength of the result should be checked in the full text.
ai_technology: Synthesis-directed de novo design model with synthesis route prediction
organization: PostEra Inc.; University of Cambridge; The COVID Moonshot Consortium; University of Chicago; Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; Weizmann Institute of Science

title: Machine learning guides automated synthesis of 19F MRI copolymer agents
summary: An automated continuous-flow polymer platform synthesized 397 copolymer compositions in a six-variable space, in iterative cycles guided by machine learning. Exploring under 0.9% of the compositional space, the models identified more than ten copolymers that outperformed state-of-the-art 19F MRI agents. Validation is experimental across hundreds of real syntheses, but the imaging performance claims are limited to the compositions tested.
ai_technology: Machine learning models guiding automated flow copolymer synthesis
organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Carnegie Mellon University

title: Interpretable machine learning discovers ultrapermeable polymer membranes for gas separation
summary: Multitask machine-learning models trained on experimental gas permeability data screened over 9 million hypothetical polymers. They identified hundreds of never-before-seen ultrapermeable membranes, with molecular dynamics simulations confirming the predicted permeabilities of the top candidates. The validation is computational rather than fabricated membranes, so the candidates remain unproven experimentally.
ai_technology: Multitask machine learning with model interpretation, plus molecular dynamics
organization: California Institute of Technology; University of Connecticut

title: Global methane point sources mapped from EMIT imaging spectroscopy with a vision transformer
summary: MAPL-EMIT used a vision transformer trained on 3.6 million synthetic plumes embedded in EMIT radiance data to map methane sources. Beyond synthetic tests, the paper abstract reports recovery of 84% of known annotated plume complexes across 1,084 EMIT granules. Comparisons with airborne data, landfills and controlled releases supported previously uncaptured sources. This is source-reported validation, not an independent emissions audit.
ai_technology: MAPL-EMIT (end-to-end vision transformer on EMIT hyperspectral radiance)
organization: Google Research; Carnegie Institution for Science; Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology

title: Vision transformer detects methane point-source plumes in Sentinel-2 imagery at global scale
summary: A vision transformer applied to multispectral Sentinel-2 data detects methane plumes as small as 0.01 km2, corresponding to sources of about 200 to 300 kg CH4 per hour, and is reported to improve on the prior state of the art by an order of magnitude. Detections were compared with airborne methane measurement campaigns; the claims rest on that comparison and the abstract gives no formal detection-rate metrics.
ai_technology: Vision transformer for multispectral methane plume detection (Sentinel-2)
organization: Kyoto University (Disaster Prevention Research Institute)

title: Quake Neural Operator builds microseismic catalogues without phase picking
summary: The Quake Neural Operator detects and locates microseismic events directly from continuous data without explicit phase picking. Applied to the Geysers geothermal field, it finds nearly an order of magnitude more seismic detections than routine catalogues, checked against the Phase Neural Operator and visual inspection rather than an independent ground-truth catalogue.
ai_technology: Quake Neural Operator (QNO), multi-task neural operator for classification and regression
organization: University of Texas at El Paso, Department of Earth, Environmental and Resource Sciences

title: Simulated training data locates archaeological tar-kiln-like sites in Louisiana, field check finds WWII features
summary: Machine learning models trained on simulated landscape data flagged 9 of 12 known targets (model 1) and all 12 (model 2, with 686 false positives among 709 remaining predictions) in Kisatchie National Forest, Louisiana; a model trained on real South Carolina tar kilns found 11 of 12. Field visits to 11 targets and augering of 2 found none of the expected tar-kiln features, and the authors concluded the structures more likely relate to a WWII military training site. Evidence caveat: only 12 known targets, and field validation is qualitative.
ai_technology: Machine learning classifiers trained on simulated archaeological sites (with a real tar-kiln-trained comparison model)
organization: University of New Mexico; New Mexico Consortium; Utah State University; Louisiana State University

title: Empirical Research Assistance writes expert-level scientific code across six domains
summary: Google's Empirical Research Assistance (ERA), a Gemini-based tree-search system, reaches expert-level performance on six benchmarks spanning genomics, public health, satellite imagery, neuroscience, time-series forecasting and mathematics. Its state-level U.S. hospital admission forecasts for flu, COVID-19 and RSV rank at or near the top of CDC leaderboards. Results are computational and checked against public benchmarks and leaderboards, with no wet-lab validation; exact benchmark scores were not visible in the sources read.
ai_technology: Empirical Research Assistance (ERA), Gemini-based tree search
organization: Google Research

title: Quine ranks compounds that shift pancreatic cancer cells toward a basal state
summary: Microsoft's Quine, a multimodal biology world model, prioritized thousands of compounds for shifting tumor cell states, and a handful were tested in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell lines. The top-ranked compounds produced the largest classical-to-basal shifts, as validated by wet-lab experiments, and some moved cells toward a distinct third phenotype. The post gives no quantitative wet-lab figures and links no paper, and it measures cell-state changes rather than clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Quine, multimodal biology world model with interactive harness
organization: Microsoft Research; Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT

title: Claude's Cycles: a Hamiltonian cycle decomposition found by Claude
summary: Knuth's note reports that Claude Opus 4.6 found an explicit decomposition of the arcs of the m^3-vertex digraph into three directed Hamiltonian cycles for odd m, an open problem Knuth posed. Knuth's proof of the construction was reportedly formally verified in Lean by Kim Morrison. Caveat: sources disagree on the even case, which an independent arXiv paper (2603.24708) and a GPT-5.4 Pro proof treat differently.
ai_technology: Claude Opus 4.6
organization: Stanford University; Anthropic

title: New Zarankiewicz numbers and bounds from OpenEvolve search
summary: Using the open-source OpenEvolve LLM-driven evolutionary framework with a custom reward, the authors find exact values Z(11,21,3,3)=116, Z(11,22,3,3)=121 and Z(12,22,3,3)=132, and lower bounds for 41 further parameter sets, at under $30 per case. Caveats: arXiv preprint not peer reviewed; a separate NeurIPS 2026 listing by overlapping authors reports different counts.
ai_technology: OpenEvolve (LLM-guided evolutionary search, AlphaEvolve-style)
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; ETH Zurich; Stanford University

title: Co-FunSearch finds adversarial instances raising the Best-Fit bin packing bound
summary: A human-LLM pipeline (Co-FunSearch) finds adversarial instances for heuristics, raising the lower bound for Best-Fit bin packing in the random-order model from 1.3 to 1.5. The authors prove the 3/2 ratio analytically and report a search-found instance scoring 1.497 over 10,000 random shuffles against Packingsolver optima. Caveat: arXiv preprint; human analysis supplies the final proofs.
ai_technology: Co-FunSearch (FunSearch-based LLM program search)
organization: University of Bonn; Google DeepMind; University of Manitoba

title: Anderson's 2014 commutative algebra problem resolved by Rethlas and Archon
summary: An informal reasoning agent (Rethlas) and a formal verification agent (Archon) resolve an open problem in commutative algebra posed by D. D. Anderson in 2014, as a counterexample. The Lean 4 formalization has about 19,450 lines and was produced in roughly 80 agent hours, with the code public on GitHub. Caveat: arXiv preprint; the Lean check covers the formal statement as written.
ai_technology: Rethlas (informal agent) with Archon (formal Lean agent)
organization: Peking University; Westlake University; Kyoto University; Tianjin University

title: Erdős Problem #650 solved with ChatGPT strategy and Aristotle Lean proof
summary: The authors prove f(m) = min(m, ceil(2 sqrt(m))) for all m, resolving Erdős Problem #650 on Bloom's site, where f(m) counts disjoint divisibility pairs in an interval for an m-element set. The detailed argument was formally verified in Lean by Harmonic's Aristotle, following a strategy proposed by ChatGPT. Caveat: arXiv preprint; the AI contribution is the strategy and formalization, not an independently checked autonomous solution.
ai_technology: ChatGPT (strategy) and Aristotle (Lean formalization)
organization: Southeast University; Xi'an Jiaotong University

title: EchoNet-Dynamic: video-based AI for left ventricular ejection fraction
summary: A deep learning model trained on echocardiogram videos segmented the left ventricle with a Dice coefficient of 0.92 and estimated ejection fraction with a mean absolute error of 4.1% (6.0% on an external dataset from another health system). Prospective evaluation with repeated human measurements found its variance comparable to or lower than that of human experts. Caveat: training data come from one institution's echocardiograms, with external testing on a single additional system.
ai_technology: EchoNet-Dynamic (video deep learning model)
organization: Stanford University; Cedars-Sinai Medical Center

title: Neural network ensemble for prenatal detection of complex congenital heart disease
summary: An ensemble of neural networks trained on 107,823 fetal ultrasound images reached an AUC of 0.99, 95% sensitivity and 96% specificity in an internal test set of 4,108 fetal surveys with 0.9% CHD. Its sensitivity was comparable to that of clinicians and it stayed robust on outside-hospital and lower-quality images. Caveat: retrospective study with a low-prevalence internal test set.
ai_technology: Ensemble of convolutional neural networks with segmentation models
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Harvard Medical School

title: Federated learning model predicts oxygen needs in COVID-19 patients
summary: The EXAM federated model, trained on data from 20 institutes without sharing patient data, achieved an average AUC above 0.92 for predicting oxygen requirements at 24 and 72 hours. At the largest independent test site it reached sensitivity 0.950 and specificity 0.882, with a 16% average AUC gain over single-site models. Caveat: retrospective data from the pandemic period and unharmonized sites.
ai_technology: EXAM federated learning model (EMR data and chest X-rays)
organization: University of Toronto; NVIDIA; Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; NYU Grossman School of Medicine

title: Deep learning reads HIV rapid tests photographed in rural South Africa
summary: Deep learning models trained on 11,374 smartphone-tablet images of HIV lateral-flow tests, captured by 60 fieldworkers, classified results with 97.8% sensitivity and 100% specificity in a pilot field study compared with human visual reading. The approach also reduced false positives and false negatives relative to human readers. Caveat: a pilot deployment in one rural setting, so wider field validation is still needed.
ai_technology: Deep learning image classifier on mobile-captured rapid test images
organization: Africa Health Research Institute; University College London

title: Deep learning assesses heart allograft rejection from biopsy whole-slide images
summary: A deep learning system analysing gigapixel endomyocardial biopsy slides detected allograft rejection with an AUC of 0.962, distinguished cellular and antibody-mediated rejection (AUCs 0.958 and 0.874) and graded rejection with an AUC of 0.833. In a human reader study it was non-inferior to conventional assessment and reduced interobserver variability and assessment time. Caveat: test cohorts from the US, Turkey and Switzerland are retrospective and the authors call for clinical trials.
ai_technology: Deep learning on whole-slide images for endomyocardial biopsies
organization: Harvard Medical School; Ege University; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; University of California San Diego

title: Swarm learning predicts colorectal cancer mutations from histopathology slides
summary: Swarm learning, which trains models across partner sites without moving patient data, was applied to over 5,000 patients to predict BRAF status and microsatellite instability from H&E colorectal cancer slides. Swarm-trained models outperformed most locally trained models and matched models trained on merged datasets, and were validated on two independent UK datasets. Caveat: the outcome is a research-grade prediction from slides, not a clinical test.
ai_technology: Swarm learning with deep learning on histopathology images
organization: University of Oxford; Belfast Health and Social Care Trust; University of Leeds

title: Machine learning model predicts mental health crises from health records
summary: A model using electronic health records to flag mental health crises over 28 days reached an AUROC of 0.797, with 58% sensitivity at 85% specificity. In a six-month prospective workflow study at one NHS trust, clinicians rated predictions useful for managing caseloads or mitigating crisis risk in 64% of cases. This measures clinician-reported usefulness, not a demonstrated reduction in crises; generalizability remains limited by the single-trust cohort, and precision was modest (AUPRC 0.159). The study includes authors affiliated with the developer Koa Health.
ai_technology: Machine learning model on electronic health records
organization: Koa Health; University of Warwick; Universitat Pompeu Fabra; Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

title: AI detects Parkinson's disease from nocturnal breathing signals
summary: An attention-based AI model extracting breathing from radio waves during sleep detected Parkinson's disease with an AUC of 0.90 on held-out data and 0.85 on external sets, across 7,671 individuals. Its severity estimates correlated with MDS-UPDRS scores (R = 0.94), and it worked for at-home assessment. Caveat: largely retrospective data and no prospective diagnostic trial reported.
ai_technology: Attention-based deep learning on contactless radio-wave breathing signals
organization: Mayo Clinic; University of Rochester Medical Center; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: Spectroscopic confirmation of neural-network lens candidates from DESI imaging
summary: A residual neural network selected strong gravitational lens candidates in the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. VLT/MUSE spectroscopy of 76 candidates (223 spectra) confirmed 55 lenses with both lens and source redshifts, 15 with lens redshift only, and found 6 non-lenses. Caveat: the source is an arXiv preprint (submitted 22 September 2025) that does not name the network architecture or list institutions on its abstract page.
ai_technology: residual neural network (convolutional classifier for strong lens candidates)
organization: DESI Collaboration

title: Polybot: an autonomous lab finds processing recipes for conductive polymer films
summary: Polybot used importance-guided Bayesian optimization to select and execute experiments across seven film-processing variables. The study reports recipes for transparent conductive polymer films with mean conductivity above 4,500 S/cm; morphology and feature-importance analyses identified influential processing factors. These are laboratory fabrication results, not demonstrated industrial-scale performance.
ai_technology: Importance-guided Bayesian optimization with automated synthesis and characterization
organization: Argonne National Laboratory; University of Chicago

title: FlowER predicts ten-step pyrazole pathways consistent with known product selectivity
summary: FlowER predicted two ten-step pathways to pyrazole products already reported in 2024 patents. Human researchers supplied acidic aqueous conditions omitted from the reaction database. Quantum-chemical calculations of intermediate energies favored the experimentally major product, consistent with the reported 8:2 product ratio; the kinetic interpretation assumes the Bell–Evans–Polanyi principle. This is a computational explanation of existing outcomes, with no new reaction experiment or claim of a previously unknown mechanism. Review covered the February 18, 2025 preprint results and the August 20 journal paper’s abstract, metadata and extended-data captions; the journal main text was not assessed.
ai_technology: FlowER (flow matching on bond-electron matrices)
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Kookmin University

title: GlaViTU estimates decadal glacier-area decline from satellite imagery
summary: GlaViTU combined convolutional and transformer models to map glacier outlines from satellite images. The original supplement applies it to the Aletsch complex between 1998 and 2023 and Hardangerjøkulen between 1996 and 2022, estimating area declines in both. The reported uncertainty bands are broad and overlap across dates. These are retrospective, model-derived geophysical estimates, not independent field measurements. Review covered the paper abstract, metadata, relevant main-text discussion and the first supplementary page.
ai_technology: GlaViTU (Glacier-VisionTransformer-U-Net)
organization: University of Twente; University of Oslo

title: FragFold identifies inhibitory fragments within bacterial proteins
summary: MIT researchers used FragFold, an AlphaFold-based approach, to predict fragments that bind to and inhibit full-length proteins in E. coli. The researchers experimentally confirmed more than half of its binding or inhibition predictions, including cases without prior structural interaction data.
ai_technology: FragFold, using AlphaFold
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: SLIDE uncovers a keratinocyte-centered signal in systemic sclerosis
summary: An interpretable machine-learning analysis of multi-omic systemic-sclerosis data identified an unexplored keratinocyte-centered signature, validated by protein staining, and a previously unreported interaction between myeloid-cell and fibroblast states and macrophage HLA signaling. The same study also analyzed CD4 T-cell clonal expansion, but this record treats the paper's disease-mechanism findings as one discovery.
ai_technology: SLIDE (Significant Latent Factor Interaction Discovery and Exploration)
organization: University of Pittsburgh; and Cornell University

title: AI helps resolve an unknown regulatory mechanism in bacterial acetyl-CoA synthetase
summary: Researchers at the University of Greifswald resolved how a post-translational modification regulates Bacillus subtilis acetyl-CoA synthetase, a central metabolic enzyme. The study used AI-based structural prediction to explain the molecular mechanism at near-atomic detail.
ai_technology: AlphaFold2 and AI-assisted structural analysis
organization: University of Greifswald

title: AI structural modeling helps map nearly 300 metabolite-binding interactions in E. coli
summary: A cross-institutional study combined chemoproteomics with AI-driven structural modeling to identify nearly 300 small-molecule ligands and their binding sites on proteins in E. coli. The map adds experimentally grounded candidate links between bacterial metabolites and proteins involved in core cellular processes.
ai_technology: AI-driven structural modeling (Kozakov laboratory; specific model not named in institutional announcement)
organization: Oregon Health & Science University; and Stony Brook University

title: ProtGPS reveals sequence signals that direct proteins to subcellular compartments
summary: ProtGPS, a protein language model and generative sequence-design system, helped identify amino-acid sequence features that guide proteins to subcellular compartments. The paper applies the model to predict disease-mutation-associated localization shifts and reports cellular testing of 20 examples.
ai_technology: ProtGPS protein language model and generative design algorithm
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; and Whitehead Institute

title: CellTransformer maps previously uncatalogued regions of the mouse brain
summary: A transformer model applied to spatial transcriptomics mapped fine-grained mouse-brain tissue domains and revealed hundreds of regions absent from existing anatomical atlases. The study evaluated the data-driven domains against the Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework and reported strong alignment alongside the novel subdivisions.
ai_technology: CellTransformer
organization: University of California, San Francisco; and Allen Institute

title: SPARCS screen identifies a Golgi-pH regulator of STING signaling
summary: A genome-wide imaging and CRISPR screen of about 70 million cells identified GPR89A and GPR89B (encoding GPHR) as important for maintaining Golgi acidity and early STING trafficking and activation. The study also found a previously undescribed autophagy phenotype associated with EI24 and linked it to altered autophagosome formation.
ai_technology: SPARCS platform with machine-learning image analysis
organization: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich; Helmholtz Munich, Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry and Technical University of Munich

title: AI-guided design enables E. coli ribosomal proteins without isoleucine
summary: Researchers used computational protein design and generative AI to recode ribosomal proteins in E. coli so they function without isoleucine, then assembled an engineered strain that remained viable and genomically stable over more than 450 laboratory generations. The result shows a reduced amino-acid alphabet can support core translation machinery in this bacterium; the organism still uses isoleucine elsewhere.
ai_technology: Protein design models including ESM2, MSATr, ProteinMPNN and AfDesign
organization: Columbia University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Harvard University

title: AI-designed enhancers control gene expression in healthy mammalian cells
summary: CRG researchers measured more than 64,000 synthetic enhancers across seven stages of blood-cell development and found that enhancer combinations can activate genes in one cell type but repress them in another. The AI model used those measurements to design previously unseen regulatory DNA sequences that drove the intended cell-selective reporter expression in mouse blood cells.
ai_technology: Machine-learning enhancer design model developed by Lars Velten's group
organization: Centre for Genomic Regulation; and Barcelona Collaboratorium

title: Machine learning identifies the first enzyme for phenazine–thiol conjugation
summary: A genome-informed machine-learning workflow (ML-CITO) used contrastive learning over protein-language-model representations and genomic context, starting from 14 known phenazine-modifying sequences, to identify PTC. Biochemical characterization showed PTC catalyzes glutathione-dependent phenazine modification, a reaction previously assumed to occur non-enzymatically.
ai_technology: ML-CITO (genome-context-informed data augmentation plus protein-language-space contrastive learning)
organization: California Institute of Technology; University of California, Los Angeles; AITHYRA / Austrian Academy of Sciences

title: DefensePredictor uncovers dozens of previously unknown bacterial anti-phage systems
summary: DefensePredictor, a machine-learning classifier using protein-language-model embeddings, nominated candidate defense genes across diverse E. coli strains. Of 94 predicted gene clusters selected for testing, experiments validated 42 previously unknown systems; analyses of 1,000 prokaryotic genomes also revealed thousands of uncharacterized protein clusters without homology to known systems.
ai_technology: DefensePredictor, gradient-boosted classification over protein-language-model embeddings and genomic context
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; and Johns Hopkins University

title: Interpretable multi-omics machine learning reveals unexpected drug mechanisms in Huntington disease models
summary: An interpretable machine-learning model integrated transcriptomic, epigenomic, metabolomic and proteomic data from Huntington-disease cell models to identify previously unknown mechanisms for protective compounds. The analysis predicted autophagy activation for one compound group and mitochondrial-respiration inhibition for another; follow-up imaging, biochemical and energetics assays experimentally confirmed these effects in the cell model.
ai_technology: Interpretable network-optimization model integrating multi-omics over a molecular-interaction network
organization: University of California San Diego; and collaborators

title: Progeni predicts candidate melanoma and colorectal-cancer targets validated in cell models
summary: Progeni combines a probabilistic knowledge graph with graph neural networks to rank disease-associated molecular targets. The authors selected six candidates lacking literature support and reported that knockdown of HSP90AB1 and MME reduced proliferation in a murine melanoma line, while knockdown of ADCY5, ADRA2A and EEF2 reduced proliferation in a murine colorectal-cancer line.
ai_technology: Progeni probabilistic knowledge graph and graph neural network
organization: Tsinghua University; Westlake University; Jilin University; Silexon AI Technology

title: LIGHTHOUSE identifies riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as a PPAT inhibitor
summary: LIGHTHOUSE, a deep-learning model using protein sequence and chemical representations, nominated riboflavin 5′-monophosphate as an inhibitor of PPAT, a target without reported inhibitors in the paper. A biochemical assay measured PPAT inhibition with an IC50 of 7.5 μM, close to the model’s predicted range; the same study also tested predicted antiviral compounds in cell models.
ai_technology: LIGHTHOUSE (ensemble graph-based deep-learning platform)
organization: Kyushu University; and collaborators

title: deepDTnet repurposes topotecan as an RORγt inhibitor for multiple-sclerosis models
summary: The deep-learning network deepDTnet predicted retinoic-acid-receptor-related orphan receptor gamma-t (RORγt) as a previously unrecognized target of topotecan. Biochemical assays showed direct inhibition (IC50 0.43 μM), and topotecan improved outcomes in a mouse experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis.
ai_technology: deepDTnet, heterogeneous drug–gene–disease network embedding with deep learning
organization: Cleveland Clinic; Case Western Reserve University, Harvard Medical School and collaborators

title: CLEAN experimentally identifies SAM hydrolase activity in previously uncharacterized proteins
summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign developed CLEAN, a contrastive-learning enzyme-function predictor, and used it to identify the SAM hydrolase activity of the previously uncharacterized protein TTHA0338. In vitro HPLC–MS and enzyme-kinetic experiments also corrected the annotation of MJ1651 and confirmed the multiple activities of SsFIA.
ai_technology: CLEAN (contrastive learning-based enzyme annotation model)
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Cornell University; Georgia Institute of Technology

title: deepAMP designs broad-spectrum antimicrobial peptides active against resistant bacteria
summary: Researchers at Hunan University and collaborators used the peptide language model deepAMP to optimize antimicrobial peptides and experimentally tested 29 candidates. More than 90% inhibited Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria better than the reference peptide penetratin; three candidates showed reduced resistance emergence in serial-passage assays and activity in a mouse Pseudomonas wound-infection model.
ai_technology: deepAMP peptide language model (deepAMP-general, deepAMP-AOM, deepAMP-POM and deepAMP-predict)
organization: Hunan University; Cleveland Clinic; National Cancer Institute; Tel Aviv University

title: AlphaFold-assisted structural clustering discovers new deaminase functions and compact base-editing enzymes
summary: The team used AlphaFold2 structure predictions to cluster the deaminase family and found that most proteins in a DddA-like clade were not double-stranded DNA deaminases. The work characterized smaller single-strand-specific deaminases, developed a compact cytidine deaminase suitable for packaging a base editor into one AAV, and demonstrated robust editing by a clade member in soybean.
ai_technology: AlphaFold2-assisted structure-based protein-family clustering
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Qi Biodesign; BGI-Qingdao; Aarhus University

title: CataPro-assisted enzyme mining identifies a high-activity Sphingobium enzyme for vanillin production
summary: CataPro, a deep-learning model using pretrained protein-language representations and molecular fingerprints to predict enzyme kinetics, was combined with sequence and structure-based filtering to screen candidate enzymes for converting 4-vinylguaiacol to vanillin. The team experimentally identified Sphingobium sp. CSO (SsCSO), whose measured activity was 19.53 times that of the initial enzyme CSO2, and then used CataPro-guided engineering to increase SsCSO activity a further 3.34-fold.
ai_technology: CataPro
organization: Shandong University; Shanghai Zelixir Biotech; Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: AI-photoswitchable CRISPRi screening identifies new regulators of TFEB localization during starvation
summary: An image-classification-guided pooled CRISPRi screen mapped factors that affect TFEB movement from nucleus to cytosol during prolonged starvation. The screen identified multiple candidate genes, and follow-up assays independently validated 21 of 64 neural-network-called hits; experiments on CREB5 further linked it to TFEB retention and starvation-associated autophagy/lysosomal protein expression.
ai_technology: AI-photoswitchable screening (AI-PS), using SVM classifiers and a convolutional neural network
organization: Janelia Research Campus, Howard Hughes Medical Institute; National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, NIH

title: Machine-learning-guided mining identifies 91 previously unknown PET hydrolases, including acid-active enzymes
summary: Researchers iteratively combined sequence mining, machine-learning activity/property predictors and high-throughput assays to screen natural enzyme homologs. They experimentally identified 91 previously unknown PET hydrolases among the 212 candidates assayed; 35 had activity on crystalline PET at pH 4.5, and four matched or exceeded a benchmark enzyme under that screening condition.
ai_technology: Three-round iterative machine-learning pipeline (including VAE/rank model, supervised activity predictors, ESM embeddings and property predictors)
organization: National Renewable Energy Laboratory; BOTTLE Consortium; Agile BioFoundry; SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory; Harvard Medical School

title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies mammalian enzymes catalyzing the second step of carnitine biosynthesis
summary: The OSMES workflow screened AlphaFold-modeled vitamin-B6-dependent enzymes by docking the substrate into active sites and ranking catalytically favorable conformations. It identified human SHMT1/2 as enzymes with hydroxytrimethyllysine-aldolase activity, validated in vitro; mouse Tha1 showed much higher catalytic efficiency, supporting a species difference in the pathway. The authors infer that humans may have lost a dedicated gene, with SHMT activity partly compensating.
ai_technology: OSMES (One Substrate–Many Enzymes Screening), automated structure-based docking/ranking workflow using AlphaFold models
organization: University of Parma; University of Padua; Sapienza University of Rome; CNR Institute of Molecular Biology and Pathology

title: Machine learning and peptide-array experiments reveal new substrates for protein-modifying enzymes
summary: A hybrid workflow coupled machine-learning models with enzyme-treated peptide arrays to predict previously unexplored protein post-translational-modification sites. Experimental validation confirmed 37–43% of proposed sites across SET8 and SIRT1–7; mass spectrometry confirmed dynamic methylation for several SET8 substrates and deacetylation at 64 unique SIRT2 sites. The work also found altered SET8 substrate networks associated with breast-cancer missense mutations.
ai_technology: Enzyme-specific ML-hybrid substrate prediction models trained from high-throughput peptide-array assays
organization: Carleton University; Ben-Gurion University of the Negev

title: Machine learning-guided cell-free engineering creates specialized amide synthetases for pharmaceutical molecules
summary: A cell-free design-build-test-learn platform generated sequence-function data from 1,217 McbA variants across 10,953 reactions. Ridge-regression ML guided enzyme variants that produced nine small-molecule pharmaceuticals with activity 1.6- to 42-fold above the parent; initial substrate-promiscuity assays found McbA could make 11 pharmaceutical compounds plus hybrid molecules. This is experimental enzyme engineering, not evidence of therapeutic efficacy of the products.
ai_technology: Augmented ridge-regression ML models within a cell-free sequence-function mapping and enzyme-engineering workflow
organization: Northwestern University; Stanford University

title: DeepMet anticipates and helps identify dozens of previously unrecognized mammalian metabolites
summary: DeepMet, an LSTM chemical language model trained on known human metabolites, generated a ranked space of metabolite-like structures and was integrated with mass spectrometry data. Researchers report identifying several dozen previously unrecognized mammalian metabolites across standards, human biofluids, mouse tissues and repository data. Some standard-supported assignments still have isomer ambiguity; the study also found known metabolites missing or misannotated in HMDB.
ai_technology: DeepMet chemical language model (three-layer LSTM over SMILES), integrated with MS/MS-spectrum prediction and meta-learning
organization: Princeton University; University of Alberta; University of British Columbia; University of Toronto; Baylor College of Medicine; collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning-guided screening validates 14 previously unreported drug–GPCR interactions
summary: Chemical Space Neural Networks used network-neighborhood labels to predict drug–target interactions and were evaluated with a yeast biosensor screen of 3,773 compound–GPCR pairs (539 compounds and seven human GPCRs). The authors report 14 experimentally significant interactions with no prior literature/database evidence in the relevant chemical neighborhoods, tentatively linking some to adverse effects. This is an in-vitro receptor-screen discovery, not clinical proof of drug side effects.
ai_technology: Chemical Space Neural Networks (CSNN), neighborhood-to-prediction model using network homophily and graph neural networks with labels as features
organization: Technical University of Denmark; Biomia ApS; Joint BioEnergy Institute; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of California, Berkeley

title: Machine learning prioritizes microbiome metabolites that stimulate interleukin-8 secretion
summary: Researchers trained ML models on public drug-development data to prioritize biological properties of microbiome metabolites, then tested predictions prospectively. In vitro experiments identified previously unreported IL-8 secretion stimulation by spermine and spermidine, metabolites previously regarded as anti-inflammatory. The paper reports average accuracy of 92.86% in prospective experiments, while cautioning that sample sizes were small.
ai_technology: Machine-learning property prediction models implemented in KNIME and trained on public drug-development data
organization: Duke University; Duke Microbiome Center

title: KCML links olfactory-receptor perturbations to multicellular organization and colorectal-cancer signaling
summary: Knowledge- and Context-driven Machine Learning (KCML) analyzed perturbation phenotypes across molecular, cellular and population scales. In colorectal-cancer cells, it associated depletion of olfactory receptors and TGFβ/WNT pathway genes with abnormal multicellular organization. The authors integrated the predictions with patient data and found olfactory-receptor expression correlated with WNT/TGFβ signatures and worse outcomes in higher-grade tumors.
ai_technology: KCML, weakly supervised machine-learning framework using support-vector-machine classifiers trained on gene-ontology annotations and high-throughput perturbation phenotypes
organization: University of Oxford; University of Zurich

title: MitoReID identifies epicatechin as a cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor
summary: A deep-learning system called MitoReID classified drug mechanisms from time-resolved mitochondrial morphology and membrane-potential images. Among its natural-compound predictions, it nominated epicatechin as a COX-2 inhibitor; the authors report in-vitro follow-up including COX-2 activity, cellular thermal-shift and surface-plasmon-resonance assays. This is a target-mechanism finding, not evidence of clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: MitoReID, deep-learning re-identification model using an Inflated 3D ResNet backbone on temporal mitochondrial images
organization: Zhejiang University; Zhejiang Lab; Zhejiang Chinese Medical University; Harvard University; Karolinska Institute; Stanford University

title: BEAUT uncovers new gut-microbial bile-acid enzymes and the novel bile acid 3-acetoDCA
summary: The BEAUT workflow combines ESM-2 protein-language-model embeddings with a neural classifier and active-site-pocket-similarity data augmentation to search gut microbial proteins for bile-acid enzymes. The authors predicted over 600,000 candidate enzymes and experimentally tested selected predictions; assays identified new bile-acid activities including MABH and ADS. ADS produces 3-acetoDCA, a previously undescribed bile-acid carbon skeleton, reported in human feces and shown to alter microbial composition and promote Lactobacillus-associated effects in experimental studies.
ai_technology: BEAUT, ESM-2 protein-language-model embeddings plus dense neural-network classifier, augmented using active-site-pocket similarity
organization: Peking University; Peking University Third Hospital; Tsinghua–Peking University Joint Center for Life Sciences; Nanchang University

title: Horizyn-1 experimentally identifies enzymes for orphan and nonnatural reactions
summary: Researchers used the reaction–protein dual-encoder model Horizyn-1 to prioritize enzyme candidates, then experimentally validated activity in orphan-reaction deorphaning, enzyme-promiscuity tests and nonnatural transformations. For an uncharacterized Thermus aquaticus protein, LC–MS confirmed dCMP kinase activity; a selected transaminase produced noncanonical amino acids from lysine-derived donors, with isotope tracing supporting predominant alpha-amine transfer.
ai_technology: Horizyn-1
organization: Dayhoff Labs; and collaborating researchers

title: CellPaint-POSH screening links AURKAIP1 knockout with reduced mitochondrial abundance and mTORC1 signaling
summary: Self-supervised CP-DINO analysis of pooled Cell Painting CRISPR profiles nominated AURKAIP1 among genes with mitochondrial and mTORC1-related phenotypes. Follow-up AURKAIP1 knockout in A549 cells reduced the mitochondrial marker TOMM20 and pS6, an mTORC1 activity readout, relative to control. The authors propose that mitochondrial translation/metabolism may influence mTORC1, while the causal pathway remains unresolved.
ai_technology: CellPaint-POSH with CP-DINO-1640 self-supervised embeddings and a vision transformer
organization: Broad Institute; and collaborating institutions

title: AlphaFold-Multimer-guided experiments corroborate six novel human protein interfaces
summary: Researchers developed a fragmentation strategy for AlphaFold-Multimer and applied it to 62 human protein interactions associated with neurological disorders. Eighteen predicted structures were judged correct or likely correct, and experiments corroborated six previously unreported interfaces: FBXO23–STX1B, STX1B–VAMP2, ESRRG–PSMC5, PEX3–PEX19, PEX3–PEX16 and SNRPB–GIGYF1.
ai_technology: AlphaFold-Multimer with a protein-fragmentation strategy
organization: Institute of Molecular Biology Mainz; Hebrew University of Jerusalem and collaborators

title: Machine learning prioritizes compounds active against heterogeneous glioblastoma stem-cell models
summary: Researchers trained cell-survival predictors on image-based screening data from six patient-derived glioblastoma stem-cell lines and screened more than 12,000 compounds. Experimental follow-up identified three compounds with activity across the GBM phenotype; HSP90 inhibitor XL-888 eliminated all six tested lines at nanomolar IC50 values, with analyses consistent with HSP90 inhibition and downstream client-protein disruption.
ai_technology: Machine-learning cell-survival predictors trained on high-throughput phenotypic screening
organization: University of Edinburgh; and Cancer Research UK Scotland Centre

title: XunZi prioritizes CHK2 as a Parkinson’s disease mechanism and therapeutic target
summary: The XunZi AI-biologist integrated literature reasoning with multimodal molecular data and nominated CHK2 and IRAK4 kinase activation in Parkinson’s disease models. Follow-up experiments found that pharmacological or genetic Chk2 inhibition rescued dopaminergic-neuron loss and motor deficits in PD mouse models, supporting CHK2 as a disease-associated mediator in the tested systems.
ai_technology: XunZi AI biologist
organization: Huazhong University of Science and Technology; and Sichuan University

title: Machine-learning network analysis identifies a conserved cell-mechanics gene module
summary: Researchers combined transcriptomic profiles with single-cell mechanical measurements from mouse and human systems and used machine-learning-based discriminative network analysis to infer a conserved five-gene module associated with cell mechanical properties. In perturbation experiments, changing CAV1 expression by silencing or overexpression altered measured cell stiffness, providing experimental support for a selected marker’s role.
ai_technology: PC-corr machine-learning-based discriminative network analysis
organization: Technische Universität Dresden; Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light and collaborating institutions

title: Machine learning screening reveals ABBV-744 as a modulator of P2Y purinergic receptors
summary: Researchers used consensus machine-learning classifiers trained on known P2Y6 agonists to select compounds for pharmacological testing. The anticancer drug ABBV-744 showed non-surmountable inhibition of UDP-induced P2Y6 receptor activation and enhanced P2Y1 receptor activation in cellular assays, revealing previously unreported purinergic-receptor activity for this molecule.
ai_technology: Consensus of deep learning, AdaBoost, naive Bayes, k-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, random forest, SVM and XGBoost classifiers
organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases; and Collaborations Pharmaceuticals

title: Knowledge-graph AI prioritizes TPP1 as a Parkinson’s disease target linked to α-synuclein homeostasis
summary: Standigm ASK’s knowledge-graph model ranked Parkinson’s disease target associations; subgraph enrichment and expression analyses narrowed 2,527 predicted targets to five candidates, including TPP1. In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.
ai_technology: Standigm ASK knowledge-graph path-based deep-learning model with subgraph-level over-representation re-ranking
organization: Standigm; and Ajou University School of Medicine

title: Machine-learning-guided genome mining links an Amycolatopsis BGC to dipyrimicins
summary: A machine-learning model that predicted antibacterial activity from biosynthetic-gene-cluster sequences prioritized Amycolatopsis azurea DSM 43854. Bioactivity-guided fractionation recovered dipyrimicins A and B from this strain, and genome analysis linked them to a previously uncharacterized dip BGC with a 76% predicted antibacterial probability; broth-microdilution assays confirmed activity against several test strains.
ai_technology: Machine-learning predictor of antibacterial activity from biosynthetic gene clusters
organization: Vanderbilt University

title: Machine-learning screening finds previously unreported antibacterial compounds active against Burkholderia and ESKAPE pathogens
summary: A directed-message-passing neural network trained on a 29,537-compound Burkholderia cenocepacia screen prioritized compounds from a natural-product library. Laboratory testing found five previously uncharacterized compounds that inhibited B. cenocepacia; 22 of 43 tested prioritized compounds inhibited at least one of five ESKAPE pathogens.
ai_technology: Directed-message-passing neural network (D-MPNN) implemented with Chemprop
organization: University of Manitoba

title: MetGenX annotates two previously uncharacterized metabolites in mouse liver
summary: MetGenX, a structure-informed neural-network workflow for generating structures from tandem mass spectra, was applied to untargeted mouse-liver metabolomics and reported two previously uncharacterized metabolites, adenosyl-cysteine and adenosine 5′-diphosphate 5′-inosine (Ap2I). The paper reports validation against chemical standards using retention time and MS2 spectral matches.
ai_technology: MetGenX structure-informed encoder-decoder neural network with LightGBM reranking
organization: Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and collaborators

title: Machine learning reveals a nitrogen-assimilation strategy in Bacteroides
summary: A microbiome metabolomics study used random-forest models to associate bacterial metabolite profiles with taxonomy and found a previously undescribed nitrogen-assimilation pattern in Bacteroides/Bacteroidetes. Follow-up growth experiments tested 60 Bacteroidetes strains with asparagine or glutamine as the sole nitrogen source and supported the predicted phenotype; the study also reports a distinct reduced-sulfur utilization result in B. thetaiotaomicron.
ai_technology: Random-forest models over metabolomics profiles
organization: Stanford University; and Chan Zuckerberg Biohub collaborators

title: LAMBDAZERO generates an experimentally active soluble epoxide hydrolase inhibitor scaffold
summary: The LAMBDAZERO generative active-learning workflow searched for synthesizable soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH/EPHX2) inhibitors and produced a quinazoline scaffold absent from the authors' comparison set of known sEH inhibitors. A synthesized analog, UM0152893, inhibited sEH in vitro with sub-micromolar potency.
ai_technology: LAMBDAZERO generative active learning with deep reinforcement learning and docking
organization: Mila – Quebec AI Institute; Université de Montréal; University of Toronto; collaborators

title: Cross-species machine learning identifies transcription factors that negatively regulate plant nitrogen-use efficiency
summary: Evolutionarily informed XGBoost and GENIE3 analyses of conserved nitrogen-response expression patterns prioritized transcription factors associated with nitrogen-use efficiency in Arabidopsis and maize. Loss-of-function tests found higher NUE in Arabidopsis myb33 and tcp2 mutants under both low- and high-nitrogen conditions, and in six other tested TF mutants specifically under low nitrogen; a maize nfya3 mutant also showed higher nitrogen-use efficiency under sufficient nitrogen in field tests.
ai_technology: Evolutionarily informed XGBoost models and GENIE3 random-forest gene-regulatory-network inference
organization: New York University; Purdue University and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

title: Active learning repurposes BMS-262084 as a potent TMPRSS2 inhibitor that blocks coronavirus entry
summary: A molecular-dynamics and active-learning workflow prioritized the existing compound BMS-262084 as a nanomolar inhibitor of human TMPRSS2 (IC50 1.82 nM). Cell assays reported inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 variants and other coronavirus entry into Calu-3 lung cells.
ai_technology: Molecular-dynamics-informed active learning with a target-specific scoring function
organization: Freie Universität Berlin; Microsoft Research AI for Science, NIH NCATS, German Primate Center and collaborators

title: Machine-learning selection uncovers plant enzymes for alkaloid pathway branches
summary: Support-vector-machine ranking selected poppy homologs whose experimental characterization identified aromatic acetaldehyde synthase activity in PsTyDC6 and phenylpyruvate-decarboxylase activity in PsPDC1. In vitro and engineered E. coli metabolomics detected pathway products including norcoclaurine and reticuline, demonstrating alternative routes from tyrosine into benzylisoquinoline alkaloids.
ai_technology: High-dimensional support vector machine (SVM) enzyme-sequence classifiers
organization: Kobe University; Tokyo Denki University, and collaborators

title: Machine-learning Treg framework identifies SMARCC1 as a previously unrecognized regulator
summary: A framework combining single-cell ATAC-seq, motif analysis, topic modeling, machine learning and genetic variation identified SMARCC1 as a previously unrecognized controller of regulatory T-cell chromatin programs. CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of Smarcc1 in Tregs produced the predicted loss of accessibility in topic-3 regulatory regions, supporting the computationally inferred connection.
ai_technology: Integrated machine-learning framework using topic modeling and high-density genetic variation over single-cell ATAC-seq profiles
organization: Harvard Medical School; and Imagine Institute, University of Paris

title: Machine-learning microscopy isolates micronucleated cells and reveals chromosome-abnormality formation
summary: The MAGIC platform used an XGBoost image classifier to identify and photolabel micronucleated cells for single-cell genome sequencing. In near-diploid human cell models, the selected cells exposed new chromosome-abnormality formation patterns, including dicentric-associated breakage-fusion-bridge events; measured baseline abnormalities approximately doubled in TP53-deficient cells, and chromosome losses outnumbered gains.
ai_technology: MAGIC adaptive imaging platform with an XGBoost micronuclei classifier
organization: European Molecular Biology Laboratory; and German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ), with collaborators

title: Mechanistic machine learning links PI3K to Src-inhibitor effects in cardiac fibroblasts
summary: LogiMML, trained on high-content images of human cardiac fibroblasts, predicted that Src inhibition suppresses actin–myosin stress fibers through PI3K signaling. Follow-up PI3K inhibition reduced stress-fiber formation and procollagen I production in the fibroblasts, supporting the proposed pathway mechanism.
ai_technology: LogiMML, a logic-based mechanistic network coupled to ridge regression
organization: University of Virginia School of Medicine; and Brigham Young University

title: Machine-learned multiscale simulations reveal lipid-dependent RAS organization at membranes
summary: The MuMMI machine-learning multiscale simulation ensemble found that local membrane lipid fingerprints correlate with wild-type KRAS clustering and orientation, with many simulated RAS–RAS interfaces appearing nonspecific. Complementary liposome and diffusion experiments supported lipid-dependent RAS adhesion and dynamics, motivating the authors' conclusion that lipids can mediate RAS multimer organization.
ai_technology: MuMMI (Multiscale Machine-learned Modeling Infrastructure)
organization: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory; Los Alamos National Laboratory, and the NCI RAS Initiative

title: BIONIC links the natural product NP329 to yeast cell-wall biogenesis and β-1,6-glucan synthesis
summary: The BIONIC graph-convolutional network integrated yeast interaction datasets and predicted essential-gene chemical sensitivities to the uncharacterized compound NP329. Experimental screens supported four BIONIC-predicted sensitive genes in the cell-wall biogenesis process; follow-up tests showed related steroidal alkaloid jervine reduced β-1,6-glucan and KRE6/SKN1 mutations conferred resistance, supporting a pathway-level connection for this compound family.
ai_technology: BIONIC (Biological Network Integration using Convolutions), a graph-convolutional deep-learning network-integration method
organization: University of Toronto; RIKEN Center for Sustainable Resource Science, and collaborators

title: A recurrent neural network uncovers a non-canonical human GRHL1 DNA-binding site
summary: A convolutional recurrent neural network found 46 GRHL1 ChIP-seq sites missed by a conventional position-weight matrix, including sequences lacking the previously considered obligatory CNNG motif. Isothermal titration calorimetry confirmed GRHL1 binding to a selected non-canonical sequence lacking that core motif; nucleotide mutagenesis experiments also showed that model scores tracked measured affinity across tested variants.
ai_technology: Convolutional recurrent neural network trained on GRHL1 HT-SELEX binding data
organization: Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine; Hannover Medical School; Institute of Bioorganic Chemistry, Polish Academy of Sciences

title: A protein-language-model workflow discovers high-activity kynureninase enzymes for tumor models
summary: A workflow combining homology search, protein-language-model embeddings and regression prioritized kynureninases by predicted catalytic activity.
