Researchers experimentally tested four top-ranked candidates; the most active had nearly twice the turnover number of the prior best, and enzyme treatment was associated with a 3.4-fold reduction in tumor weight in a mouse comparison.
ai_technology: Protein language model embeddings coupled with regression in the SeekRank enzyme-prioritization workflow
organization: Seoul National University; and Galux Inc.

title: Machine learning uncovers four new extracellular contractile injection-system toxins
summary: An XGBoost classifier trained on genomic and biochemical features prioritized eCIS-associated toxins from bacterial and archaeal genomes. Four candidates, EAT14–17, were experimentally shown to be toxic in bacterial and/or yeast cells; EAT14 also inhibited Rac1/Cdc42-mediated mitogenic signaling in human cells.
ai_technology: XGBoost classifier for extracellular contractile injection-system-associated toxins (EATs)
organization: Hebrew University of Jerusalem; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; collaborators

title: Deep-learning-assisted DIP-MS identifies POLR2E as a constitutive prefoldin-like-complex subunit
summary: DIP-MS combines deep-learning-based signal processing with native-gel fractionation and mass spectrometry to resolve complex isoforms. In human prefoldin-like-complex experiments, repeated coelution and affinity-purification data supported POLR2E as a constitutive PFDL component, updating the view that it was merely an associated protein.
ai_technology: Deep Interactome Profiling by Mass Spectrometry (DIP-MS), including deep-learning-based signal processing
organization: Institute of Molecular Systems Biology; ETH Zurich and collaborators

title: Machine-learning screening yields novel potent acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors
summary: NCATS researchers trained machine-learning QSAR models and applied them to a roughly 360,000-compound library. Experimental colorimetric and orthogonal fluorescence assays confirmed new AChE/BChE inhibitors; the study reports 22 AChE and 67 BChE inhibitors with IC50 below 5 μM, including novel structural series, with some submicromolar compounds.
ai_technology: Ensemble comparison of machine-learning QSAR classifiers (including XGBoost, random forest, SVM, neural network and naïve Bayes)
organization: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, National Institutes of Health

title: EnzySFC discovers nitrile-hydratase activity in nitrilases and evolves amide-selective variants
summary: The AI-assisted EnzySFC workflow experimentally validated 10 previously uncharacterized nitrilases selected from 1,113 candidates. A wild-type Phototrophicales nitrilase showed exclusive nitrile hydratase activity; a separate Actinomycetia nitrilase was AI-evolved, with four tested top variants reaching 100% amide yield and complete substrate conversion.
ai_technology: EnzySFC AI-assisted enzyme discovery and functional-evolution platform
organization: China State Institute of Pharmaceutical Industry, Research Center for Systems Biosynthesis

title: Machine-learning metabolomics identifies widespread promiscuous activities in Escherichia coli enzymes
summary: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested. Follow-up reconstruction assigned 22 reaction stoichiometries to 11 enzymes, with four reactions experimentally validated; examples include expanded nucleotide-substrate use by DeoA, cofactor and sugar promiscuity in NanK, and FMN dephosphorylation by CobC. Follow-up assays also found that pyrimidine-specific ribonucleoside hydrolase RihB acted on thymidine, guanosine and deoxyuridine, further extending its measured substrate range.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier applied to enzyme metabolomics ion-trace data
organization: ETH Zurich; Weizmann Institute of Science; University Children’s Hospital Zurich and University of Zurich

title: Generative deep learning discovers the RIPK1 inhibitor RI-962 with an unreported scaffold
summary: A target-conditioned generative deep-learning model based on a distribution-learning conditional recurrent neural network generated a tailored compound library that was screened for RIPK1 inhibition. The study reports RI-962 as a potent inhibitor with a previously unreported scaffold, validated in vitro for protection from necroptosis and in vivo in two inflammatory models.
ai_technology: Generative deep-learning distribution-learning conditional recurrent neural network (GDL cRNN)
organization: State Key Laboratory of Biotherapy and Cancer Center, West China Hospital, Sichuan University; West China School of Pharmacy, Sichuan University

title: Machine-learning-guided screening identifies Bcl-2-family inhibitors IS20 and IS21
summary: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening followed by surface-plasmon-resonance and biological assays identified IS20 and IS21 as compounds binding anti-apoptotic Bcl-2, Bcl-xL and Mcl-1 proteins. Both affected cancer-cell viability and induced apoptosis/autophagic flux in tested cell models; IS21 also reduced tumor growth in leukemia and melanoma mouse models.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided virtual screening (model family not named in PubMed abstract)
organization: IRCCS Regina Elena National Cancer Institute; Sapienza University of Rome; Italian National Research Council and collaborators

title: Deep-learning virtual screening finds antibacterial hits in over one billion compounds
summary: Genentech and collaborators trained the deep-learning model GNEprop on high-throughput screening data and screened more than 1.4 billion synthetically accessible molecules. In follow-up experiments, 82 selected compounds showed antibacterial activity against the sensitized E. coli ΔtolC strain; the paper reports a 90-fold higher hit rate than the training screen and describes chemically diverse hits, some with activity beyond that strain and validated biological targets.
ai_technology: GNEprop deep-learning antibacterial activity predictor
organization: Genentech Research and Early Development; NVIDIA; Mila–Université de Montréal collaborators

title: Prospective machine-learning screen identifies six previously unreported OATP1B1 inhibitors
summary: Researchers trained and compared seven machine-learning classifiers for OATP1B1 transporter inhibition. In prospective CHO-cell testing, 15 of 19 compounds predicted active by SVC models inhibited the transporter; six (abamectin, asiaticoside, berbamine, doramectin, mobocertinib and umbralisib) were described as previously unreported OATP1B1 inhibitors.
ai_technology: Seven molecular-fingerprint machine-learning classifiers, with prospective selection by support vector classifier (SVC)
organization: Collaborations Pharmaceuticals; University of Arizona

title: Machine-learning screening identifies natural RORγt inhibitors with preclinical psoriasis activity
summary: An ensemble machine-learning screen of natural products prioritized protoberberine alkaloids as candidate RORγt inhibitors. In vitro assays found that berberine and coptisine inhibited Th17 differentiation and directly bound RORγt by surface plasmon resonance; coptisine also showed efficacy in a preclinical mouse psoriasis model.
ai_technology: Ensemble machine-learning models for natural-product RORγt activity and counter-screening, combining graph neural networks and molecular-fingerprint random forests
organization: Bionsight; Incheon National University; Seoul National University; Kangwon National University; Ajou University; Wright State University

title: Machine learning reveals broad and previously uncharacterized fungal polyketide-synthase activity
summary: A genome-mining and cell-free enzyme study characterized fungal type III polyketide synthases (T3PKSs), revealing broad and varied substrate/product profiles. An ML model trained on 341 enzyme–substrate pairs predicted substrate specificity and guided tests that found two fungal enzymes, AcaePKS and PansPKS, active on all ten tested substrates, including non-natural substrates absent from training data.
ai_technology: Feedforward neural-network multilayer perceptron trained on protein-language-model embeddings and substrate fingerprints
organization: University of Groningen; University of Vienna

title: CACLENS predicts and validates a zearalenone-degrading enzyme
summary: The multitask deep-learning enzyme-screening framework CACLENS selected ten candidate enzymes for zearalenone (ZEN) degradation, which were expressed and tested. One candidate degraded more than 90% of both ZEN and its analogue α-zearalenol (α-ZOL) in the reported assay.
ai_technology: CACLENS (Cross-Attention & Contrastive Learning-enabled Enzyme Selection), a multimodal multitask deep-learning enzyme classifier
organization: Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Active learning discovers eight experimental binders for the LRRK2 WDR domain
summary: A free-energy molecular-dynamics and machine-learning active-learning workflow optimized compounds against the understudied LRRK2 WDR domain. Of 35 analogs experimentally tested, eight showed measurable binding confirmed by surface plasmon resonance and, for fluorinated compounds, an orthogonal 19F-NMR assay; measured dissociation constants ranged from 18 to 230 μM.
ai_technology: Active-learning-guided relative-binding-free-energy (AL-RBFE) workflow using molecular-dynamics thermodynamic-integration calculations and an ML affinity-prediction model
organization: Carnegie Mellon University; University of Toronto Structural Genomics Consortium; University of British Columbia; University of Ottawa and collaborators

title: Biological activity-profile modeling identifies SARS-CoV-2 antiviral leads
summary: NCATS researchers used biological activity-based modeling (BABM) to infer antiviral activity from compounds’ profiles across multiple assays. Of 311 model-predicted SARS-CoV-2 candidates tested in a live-virus cell-culture assay, 99 were confirmed active (32% hit rate); follow-up assays implicated viral-entry inhibition and/or autophagy modulation among confirmed compounds.
ai_technology: Biological activity-based modeling (BABM) models trained on multi-assay compound-activity profiles
organization: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, NIH; Public Health Agency of Canada; Florida State University

title: MISPOP machine learning screening identifies the oncolytic peptide Dermaseptin-S9
summary: The MISPOP ensemble screened a natural peptide library of 1,033 sequences, prioritized 16 oncolytic-peptide candidates and selected five for synthesis and testing. Dermaseptin-S9 showed membrane disruption and immunogenic-cell-death readouts in vitro and over 92% tumor-growth inhibition in a B16F10 melanoma mouse model.
ai_technology: MISPOP mechanism-informed ensemble combining XGBoost, deep neural networks and transfer learning with physicochemical priors
organization: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Sichuan University; Naval Medical University; Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College

title: Machine-intelligence design yields selective synthetic COX-1 inhibitors from a marine natural-product template
summary: Using Marinopyrrole A as a template, an automated design workflow generated and synthesized new natural-product-inspired molecules; target-prediction software pointed to cyclooxygenases. In biochemical assays, synthetic mimetics 2 and 2a inhibited COX-1 at 0.10 and 0.16 μM, respectively, and compound 2a was crystallographically observed bound to COX-1. Human platelet assays also showed inhibition.
ai_technology: DOGS rule-based de novo molecule construction and CATS molecular-similarity ranking, coupled with SPiDER self-organizing-map machine-learning target prediction
organization: ETH Zurich; Thomas Jefferson University; University of Bari; University of Innsbruck; Goethe University Frankfurt; Friedrich Schiller University Jena

title: Pinal designs functional proteins from natural-language descriptions
summary: The 16-billion-parameter Pinal model generated protein candidates from plain-language function descriptions. In four reported design tasks—fluorescent protein, PET hydrolase, alcohol dehydrogenase and metabolic H-protein—the selected designs displayed the intended function in laboratory tests; the best H-protein raised product titre 1.7-fold relative to native E. coli H-protein in a reconstituted CO2-fixation pathway.
ai_technology: Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter protein foundation model with text-to-structure (T2struct) and text-conditioned sequence design (SaProt-T) components
organization: Westlake University; and collaborating institutions

title: Sequence-conditioned CogMol designs SARS-CoV-2 spike and main-protease inhibitors
summary: IBM Research and academic collaborators used the CogMol deep generative foundation model to design compounds from target protein sequence information alone for SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain and main protease. In vitro inhibition was reported for two of four synthesized candidates for each target; the most potent spike-RBD inhibitor also showed activity against multiple variants in live-virus neutralization assays.
ai_technology: CogMol, a sequence-conditioned deep generative foundation model using a molecular variational autoencoder and protein–ligand binding predictor
organization: IBM Research; Diamond Light Source; University of Oxford; Enamine Ltd.; associated research centers

title: Prospective deep-learning screen identifies nanomolar IRAK1 inhibitor scaffolds
summary: Ro5's prospective HydraScreen structure-based deep-learning screen ranked compounds for IRAK1 and was evaluated against a 47,000-compound robotic high-throughput screen. The study reports that 23.8% of IRAK1 hits were in HydraScreen's top 1% and identifies three nanomolar scaffolds, two described in the abstract as novel IRAK1 candidates.
ai_technology: HydraScreen structure-based deep-learning virtual screening, with SpectraView knowledge-graph target evaluation
organization: Ro5 (AI Chemistry); and Strateos

title: Machine-learning prioritization and CRISPR knockout identify OsWOX13 as a rice heat-tolerance regulator
summary: Meta-transcriptomic comparison of heat-tolerant and susceptible rice genotypes yielded 409 meta-differentially expressed genes. Random-forest and XGBoost feature ranking with SHAP independently prioritized OsWOX13; CRISPR/Cas9 knockout lines showed lower survival under heat stress (~20% versus ~60% in wild type) and delayed flowering, with accompanying changes in ABA, oxidative-stress markers and stress/flowering-associated proteins.
ai_technology: Random forest and XGBoost models with SHAP feature attribution
organization: Hainan University; Guizhou University; National Institute of Agricultural Science, Rural Development Administration (Republic of Korea); Pusan National University; Kookmin University

title: Machine learning uncovers new small-molecule chloride transporters from DrugBank
summary: After high-throughput testing 1,894 compounds and confirming 59 chloride transporters, researchers trained and evaluated machine-learning classifiers, then prioritized DrugBank compounds for wet-lab tests. Five of ten selected drugs—bazedoxifene, centhaquine, brilliant green, tamoxifen and nevanimibe—were classified by the authors as active chloride transporters, with an estimated 50–60% hit rate under their assays.
ai_technology: Machine-learning binary classifiers and consensus QSAR models trained on experimentally measured chloride-transport activity
organization: Tulane University; Rowan University

title: CHOOSER uses protein foundation models to discover functional Casλ homologs
summary: The CHOOSER framework fine-tuned ESM-2 protein-language-model representations for alignment-free CRISPR-Cas discovery and pre-crRNA self-processing predictions. It nominated 11 Casλ homologs, nearly doubling the known Casλ set. Wet-lab work on selected homologs confirmed pre-crRNA processing for five of six tested proteins; EphcCasλ also cleaved target DNA and showed trans-cleavage activity, with a TTR PAM reported.
ai_technology: CHOOSER, a protein foundation-model framework fine-tuning ESM-2 representations for Cas homolog identification and Cas12 pre-crRNA-processing classification
organization: Tongji University; Zhejiang Lab; Shanghai East Hospital; collaborating Chinese research institutions

title: Deep learning designs selective antimicrobial peptides against Cutibacterium acnes
summary: A deep-learning design pipeline combining sequence generation and classifiers, transfer learning, pretrained protein embeddings and C. acnes-specific training data produced 42 novel peptides for testing. Five showed high-potency, selective activity against C. acnes, with MICs of 2–4 µg/mL; additional in-vitro assays tested activity against other microbes, hemolysis and keratinocyte cytotoxicity.
ai_technology: Deep-learning peptide generators and activity/selectivity classifiers using transfer learning and pretrained protein embeddings
organization: Shanghai MetaNovas Biotech; Fuzhou University; Metanovas Biotech

title: AMPlify prioritizes bullfrog-genome antimicrobial peptides active against priority pathogens
summary: Researchers integrated the attentive deep-learning classifier AMPlify into a genome-mining pipeline for North American bullfrog sequences. Of 101 candidate mature peptides generated from genome-annotated precursors, AMPlify predicted 75 as antimicrobial; 11 candidates were synthesized and tested, with four showing activity against tested bacteria, including a multidrug-resistant carbapenemase-producing E. coli isolate.
ai_technology: AMPlify, an attentive deep-learning antimicrobial-peptide sequence classifier
organization: Canada's Michael Smith Genome Sciences Centre, BC Cancer; University of British Columbia; University of Victoria; British Columbia Centre for Disease Control; Vancouver General Hospital; University of Washington

title: LSTM-designed peptides show antibacterial activity and mixed efficacy in a mouse sepsis model
summary: A generative long short-term-memory recurrent neural network produced 198 candidate antimicrobial peptides; five were synthesized. PEP-38 and PEP-137 inhibited carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella isolates in vitro, and PEP-137 also inhibited Pseudomonas aeruginosa. In a small mouse K. pneumoniae sepsis experiment, PEP-137 yielded 50% survival, PEP-38 did not improve survival, and the in-vitro-inactive PEP-36 control unexpectedly yielded 66.7% survival.
ai_technology: Generative long short-term memory recurrent neural network trained on antimicrobial peptide sequences
organization: Stavropol State Medical University

title: Machine-learning-guided screening discovers potent innate immune signaling modulators
summary: At the University of Chicago, an active-learning pipeline iteratively selected molecules from a 139,998-compound library for in-vitro assays of NF-κB and interferon regulatory factor (IRF) signaling. After screening about 2% of the library, the study reported compounds suppressing NF-κB up to 15-fold or elevating NF-κB and IRF up to 5-fold and 6-fold, respectively. Follow-up cytokine assays found PME-4007 increased IFN-β secretion about threefold when co-delivered with the STING agonist cGAMP.
ai_technology: Machine-learning active-learning pipeline with variational-autoencoder molecular representations, Gaussian-process regression and Bayesian optimization
organization: University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering; University of Chicago Cellular Screening Center

title: Neural-network-guided autonomous experiments reveal an unreported TosMIC reaction
summary: A reactivity-seeking neural network coupled to an autonomous reaction platform navigated unknown chemical mixtures using real-time analytical data. Among the reactions it identified, follow-up characterization revealed an unreported photochemical reaction and a new reactivity mode for p-toluenesulfonylmethyl isocyanide (TosMIC): six equivalents of TosMIC underwent a multistep single-substrate cascade yielding a trimeric product in 47% unoptimized yield and forming five C–C bonds.
ai_technology: Reactivity-seeking neural network and junction-tree neural network integrated with an autonomous robotic synthesis and analytics platform
organization: University of Glasgow School of Chemistry

title: Machine-learning-guided optimization finds low-loading conditions for platinum-catalyzed amide reduction
summary: A machine-learning-assisted reaction-optimization study found conditions for reducing N,N-dimethylacetamide to dimethylethylamine using the known platinum complex [Pt(DMS)₂Cl₂]. The selected condition used 0.01 mol% catalyst and reached complete conversion in two hours at 39 °C without solvent, with a reported turnover frequency of 5,002 h⁻¹. The chemical catalyst identity is not claimed as new.
ai_technology: Sunthetics machine-learning reaction-optimization platform
organization: Ghent University Center for Sustainable Chemistry; Sunthetics; University of Padua

title: Machine-learning and expert co-screening identifies two new silver-catalyzed cycloadditions
summary: Researchers at the Zelinsky Institute used unsupervised machine learning to filter and cluster candidate atom-economic cycloaddition reactions generated from quantum-chemical data, then used a digital co-expert and chemist review to prioritize experiments. The team experimentally confirmed two previously undescribed silver-catalyzed cycloaddition reactions yielding new products within about one week.
ai_technology: Machine-learning candidate filtering and clustering combined with the digital co-expert reaction-prioritization workflow
organization: N. D. Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry, Russian Academy of Sciences

title: Bayesian optimization finds mild solvent-free mechanochemical conditions for cyclopropanation and epoxidation
summary: A Bayesian-optimization-guided mechanochemical study identified conditions for the established Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky reaction using KOH in place of hazardous NaH, under air-equilibrated conditions and with no solvent or liquid-assisted grinding agent. In the chalcone benchmark, one optimized condition reached cyclopropanation completion in five minutes; the study also demonstrated cyclopropanation and epoxidation across multiple substrates, including yields of 45–75% for four additional substrates.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization implemented with BoTorch/PyTorch, including multi-objective optimization of product yield and process mass intensity
organization: University of Parma SynCat Lab; University of Parma IMPLab

title: Deep-learning screening identifies covalent SARS-CoV-2 main-protease inhibitor scaffolds
summary: A two-stage deep-learning screen selected cysteine-directed compounds for testing against SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease. Of 32 top-ranked compounds experimentally assayed, 12 inhibited the enzyme; six had IC₅₀ values below 12 μM, with the strongest reported at 1.4 μM. Five of those six exhibited time-dependent inhibition consistent with covalent binding.
ai_technology: Deep-learning COVCL and NOVCL classifiers integrating a directed message-passing neural network and feed-forward network
organization: Peking University BNLMS; and Peking-Tsinghua Center for Life Sciences; Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Research Unit of Drug Design Method

title: AI and developmental profiling reveal conserved rules for microRNA strand selection
summary: Using a high-throughput qPCR assay, Arizona State University researchers measured microRNA 5p/3p strand use across six Caenorhabditis elegans developmental stages and selected tissues. A machine-learning model trained on experimentally measured strand usage identified compositional and structural sequence features associated with strand preference; the learned relationships predicted strand usage in other vertebrates, including humans, and the authors report that the rules are conserved but context-dependent.
ai_technology: Predictive machine-learning model using 77 biologically informed features, trained on high-throughput qPCR measurements from the HiTmiSS platform
organization: Arizona State University Biodesign Institute and School of Life Sciences; Arizona State University School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence

title: Biochemical-constrained generative AI yields experimentally active antimicrobial peptides against E. coli
summary: A University of Hong Kong-led team used a conditional variational autoencoder constrained by biochemical properties and a random-forest activity classifier to generate and prioritize antimicrobial peptides. In vitro testing of 54 generated peptides found 18.5% with MIC ≤10 μg/mL and 38.9% with MIC ≤50 μg/mL against the study’s E. coli model; nine peptides were classified as both active and non-toxic in the reported assays.
ai_technology: CVAE-BIO: conditional variational autoencoder with biochemical constraints and a random-forest antimicrobial-activity classifier
organization: The University of Hong Kong; University of Hong Kong-Shenzhen Hospital; Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Machine learning prioritizes ruthenium complexes with increased MRSA antibacterial hit rates
summary: Researchers trained machine-learning models on 288 modularly synthesized ruthenium arene Schiff-base complexes and used them to prioritize 54 new compounds for antibacterial-activity testing. The model-selected set had a 53.7% hit rate against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, compared with 9.4% in the original library, an approximately 5.7-fold enrichment.
ai_technology: Machine-learning activity-prediction models trained on ruthenium arene Schiff-base complex structures and antibacterial assay data
organization: University of Bern Department of Chemistry, Biochemistry & Pharmaceutical Sciences; National University of Singapore Department of Chemistry

title: Machine learning discovers D-amino-acid mixtures that boost anti-biofilm antibiotic cocktails
summary: A machine-learning-guided high-throughput screen identified a five-component D-amino-acid mixture (“D-mix”) with about 78% anti-biofilm activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa at 100 μM. Combining D-mix with half the lowest effective gentamicin dose retained about 91% bacterial-growth inhibition and about 93% anti-biofilm efficacy in vitro. In a small mouse lung-infection model, gentamicin/D-mix treatment reduced measured P. aeruginosa burden by about 95% in blood and 91% in lung tissue at 72 hours.
ai_technology: High-throughput screening coupled to machine-learning regression and iterative global optimization of D-amino-acid mixture ratios
organization: University of Science and Technology Beijing Institute for Advanced Materials and Technology; National Materials Corrosion and Protection Data Center; Beijing University of Chemical Technology

title: Machine-learning-assisted screening yields an experimentally active FtsZ inhibitor candidate
summary: A fused machine-learning and virtual-screening workflow narrowed compounds from three libraries to five candidate FtsZ inhibitors for bioactivity evaluation. The compound T3995 inhibited Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 6538 and Bacillus subtilis ATCC 9732 in reported assays, with MIC values of 32 and 2 μg/mL, respectively. Morphology and FtsZ-polymerization assays supported FtsZ-related antibacterial activity.
ai_technology: ROC-guided machine-learning selection combined with virtual screening, clustering and binding-model analysis
organization: Jiangxi Provincial Key Laboratory of Drug Design and Evaluation, Jiangxi Science and Technology Normal University; Jiangxi University of Traditional Chinese Medicine Cancer Research Center

title: AI-guided HuJ3 mutation improves HIV-1 gp120 binding and neutralization in assays
summary: The IsAb2.0 workflow, combining AlphaFold-Multimer complex modeling with FlexddG mutation scoring, proposed five substitutions to improve the binding of humanized J3 nanobody HuJ3 to HIV-1 gp120. Of these, E44R experimentally improved binding (ELISA EC50 1.696 nM) and neutralization relative to HuJ3; the other proposed substitutions did not consistently improve binding, and T99R failed to express. The gain did not restore neutralization to the parental llama J3 level.
ai_technology: IsAb2.0 antibody-design protocol integrating AlphaFold-Multimer 2.3/3.0, SnugDock, alanine scanning and FlexddG
organization: University of Pittsburgh School of Pharmacy; University of Pittsburgh Center for Antibody Therapeutics; University of Pittsburgh Center for AIDS Research

title: Generative machine learning nominates a chiral ligand validated in asymmetric C–H activation
summary: A transfer-learned chemical language model generated novel chiral amino-acid ligands for palladium-catalyzed asymmetric β-C(sp³)–H activation, while an ensemble of 30 fine-tuned deep-learning regressors predicted reaction enantioselectivity. From 490 generated ligand candidates, mechanistic and synthetic filters retained 73; the authors tested selected reactions prospectively without disclosing the model-predicted enantioselectivity to the experimentalists. One highlighted reaction using generated ligand L5 gave 94% ee, matching the model prediction of 94%.
ai_technology: Transfer-learned ULMFiT chemical language model (FnG) for ligand generation and a 30-model deep-learning ensemble (EnP) for enantioselectivity prediction
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay; Scripps Research

title: Generative antibody language model yields a pseudovirus-neutralizing XBB spike binder
summary: Tencent AI Lab and collaborators developed PALM-H3, a pretrained antibody language model that generates heavy-chain CDRH3 sequences, and A2binder to rank antigen-antibody binding. For SARS-CoV-2 XBB, which the paper says was not present during training, the selected generated antibody (Artificial 1) bound spike and neutralized pseudovirus in vitro, with reported KD 0.13 nM and IC50 0.00301 μg/mL. The study also assayed generated antibodies against wild-type, Alpha and Delta; performance varied by antibody and variant.
ai_technology: PALM-H3 pretrained antibody generative language model and A2binder antigen-antibody affinity predictor
organization: Tencent AI Lab; Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School; Xijing Hospital of Digestive Diseases, Fourth Military Medical University

title: PROBY screening uncovers target-selective fluorescent probes for tau, BCL-2 and TDP-43
summary: The PROBY deep-learning pipeline screened 26,416 target-validated molecules for useful optical properties, identified 11 candidates for testing and found target-responsive probes PE859 (tau), obatoclax (BCL-2) and B3 (TDP-43). The study reports selectivity assays, cell/tissue labeling and ex-vivo tumor imaging with obatoclax. AI-guided structural modification of PE859 yielded 859-2, which enabled in-vivo two-photon and cleared-brain imaging of tau pathology in P301S transgenic mice; its measured tau-aggregate dissociation constant was 54.8 nM.
ai_technology: PROBY two-stage message-passing neural network pipeline (PROBY-L1 fluorescence classification and PROBY-L2 photophysical-property prediction)
organization: Children’s Hospital of Chongqing Medical University; Stanford University School of Medicine; Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital; Sichuan University; South-Central Minzu University

title: CycleRFdiffusion-designed TP4 is a reproducible cyclic peptide binder to TREM2
summary: A structure-conditioned workflow combining CycleRFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and HighFold generated and screened 1,500 cyclic peptide–TREM2 complexes and prioritized four candidates. The lead TP4 showed weak but reproducible TREM2 binding in spectral-shift, microscale-thermophoresis and surface-plasmon-resonance assays. The authors report favorable plasma stability and moderate metabolic stability, presenting the work as an initial proof of concept for TREM2-targeted cyclic binders.
ai_technology: CycleRFdiffusion backbone design, ProteinMPNN sequence design and HighFold structural prediction/screening
organization: Weill Cornell Medicine; Macao Polytechnic University; University of Gdańsk

title: AI-guided natural-product-inspired molecules inhibit two multidrug-resistance transporters
summary: Combining marine natural-product fragment mining, AI-based molecular generation and structure-guided selection, the authors designed optimized analogues Ib18 and It12 targeting the ABC transporters P-glycoprotein (ABCB1) and BCRP (ABCG2). Both analogues reversed transporter-mediated resistance in overexpressing cells and outperformed reference inhibitors. Target-engagement assays supported transporter inhibition without expression downregulation. In xenografts, Ib18 increased mitoxantrone antitumor activity and tumor accumulation without a detected increase in systemic toxicity.
ai_technology: AI-based molecular generation integrated with marine natural-product fragment mining and structure-guided prioritization
organization: Zhejiang University of Technology; Zhejiang–Egypt Joint Laboratory on Intelligent Discovery of Marine Drugs; Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital; University of Pittsburgh

title: LIMITS-guided peptide design yields selective anti-tuberculosis host-defense peptides
summary: The Penn State/University of Minnesota team used the Lead Informed Machine Interrogation of Therapeutic Sequences (LIMITS) workflow to train random-forest and neural-network predictors on approximately 100 host-defense peptides, using lead mutational scans and biophysical sequence features. Experimentally tested neural-network-designed MAD5.1 and MAD5.3 showed reported MICs of 5 μM against M. tuberculosis H37Rv, selectivity indices >16 against an eight-organism non-mycobacterial panel, and mammalian-cell toxicity indices >100. The study identifies peptide length as a potentially underappreciated activity determinant.
ai_technology: LIMITS (Lead Informed Machine Interrogation of Therapeutic Sequences), using random-forest and feed-forward neural-network predictors
organization: Pennsylvania State University; University of Minnesota

title: AI generates compounds with experimentally validated pancreatic cancer cell selectivity
summary: The IRB Barcelona team trained cell-line cytotoxicity predictors on data from more than 11,000 compounds assayed across pancreatic-cancer and control cell lines, then integrated the models with a reinforcement-learning generative system to design molecules for cell-selective effects. In follow-up tests, 45 AI-designed molecules or close analogues were assayed; 20 showed the intended cell-specific cytotoxicity, and dose-response testing confirmed 18 of those 20. Across the seven selectivity exercises, at least one hit was found in five; measured IC50 values could be calculated for 12 confirmed hits and ranged from 0.97 to 16.6 μM in the targeted cell lines.
ai_technology: Cell-line-specific cytotoxicity prediction models coupled to a reinforcement-learning molecular generator (REINVENT-based workflow)
organization: Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB Barcelona), The Barcelona Institute of Science and Technology; ICREA

title: Machine learning generates active daunomycin-binding synthetic nucleic-acid polymers outside selected sequence families
summary: The study combined in-vitro selection with a conditional variational autoencoder trained on selection data to generate high-affinity highly functionalized nucleic-acid polymer (HFNAP) sequences. Experimentally generated CVAE sequences bound daunomycin with reported dissociation constants of 9–26 nM despite having no apparent primary-sequence similarity to experimentally selected polymers; competition selections found selected generated variants performed as well as or better than sequences obtained after multiple rounds of high-stringency selection.
ai_technology: Conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) trained on in-vitro selection-derived HFNAP sequence/fitness data
organization: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Harvard University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Brigham and Women's Hospital

title: Deep learning designs abiotic miniproteins that improve antisense-oligonucleotide nuclear delivery
summary: A generator–predictor–optimizer deep-learning workflow trained on quantitative delivery assays was used to design abiotic Mach miniproteins. Twelve selected predicted constructs were synthesized/tested; the strongest library construct improved phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO) delivery nearly 20-fold over unconjugated PMO in the standardized HeLa assay, while the authors describe the best designs as up to 50-fold more effective than prior polypeptide-based variants. PMO–Mach3/4 also produced dose-dependent reporter-protein restoration in skeletal muscle, diaphragm and heart in transgenic mice after a single intravenous dose.
ai_technology: Deep-learning generator–predictor–optimizer workflow: nested-LSTM sequence generator, CNN activity predictor on residue chemical fingerprints, and evolutionary optimization
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Harvard Medical School; Sarepta Therapeutics

title: AI-accelerated virtual screening identifies small-molecule binders to KLHDC2 and Nav1.7
summary: The OpenVS platform combined target-specific neural-network active learning with RosettaVS physics-based docking to search billion-scale compound libraries. The study reported seven low-micromolar KLHDC2 degron-pocket binders and four Naᵥ1.7 VSD4 binders. KLHDC2 hit C29 competed with a degron peptide at IC50 about 2.9 μM and its predicted pose was supported by a 2.0 Å crystal structure; the strongest Naᵥ1.7 hit, Z8739902234, had IC50 1.3 μM in whole-cell electrophysiology.
ai_technology: OpenVS active-learning platform with target-specific feed-forward neural-network triage, coupled to RosettaVS physics-based docking and RosettaGenFF-VS scoring
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design; and Department of Biochemistry; Howard Hughes Medical Institute; University of California, Davis; Korea Institute of Science and Technology; Sungkyunkwan University

title: AI-ranked SARS-CoV-2 protein interactions guide discovery of an NSP10–NSP16 inhibitor
summary: A machine-learning classifier applied to quantitative PPI assay data and AlphaFold-Multimer predictions to prioritize SARS-CoV-2 protein interactions; 15 of 34 high-confidence interactions were not previously listed in IMEx. The team then targeted the NSP10–NSP16 methyltransferase interface in an ultra-large virtual screen. Compound 459 bound NSP10 (MST affinity about 13 μM), reduced NSP10–NSP16 interaction in cells (BRET IC50 9.2 μM), inhibited complex methyltransferase activity by about 50% at 100 μM, and reduced SARS-CoV-2 reporter replication in cells (IC50 39.5 μM).
ai_technology: Multi-adaptive support-vector-machine (maSVM) classifier for quantitative protein–protein interaction data, coupled with AlphaFold-Multimer complex prediction; VirtualFlow/QuickVina2 and later docking methods performed compound screening
organization: Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine; University of Luxembourg; University of California, San Francisco; Harvard Medical School; University of California, San Diego; University of Toronto; University of Cambridge; University of Antwerp and collaborators

title: Transcriptome-based machine learning reveals an MCL1 dependency in alveolar soft part sarcoma
summary: A support-vector-regression model trained to infer gene dependencies from RNA-sequencing profiles predicted selective MCL1 dependence in alveolar soft part sarcoma (ASPS), distinct from TFE3-translocation renal cell carcinoma. The authors tested the prediction with CRISPR knockout and the MCL1 inhibitor murizatoclax in two ASPS cell lines; the reported viability effects were greater in ASPS than comparator tRCC lines.
ai_technology: Transcriptome-based support-vector regression model (RBF kernel; 657 highly predictable gene dependencies)
organization: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard

title: ProT-VAE designs synthetic enzymes with measured activity and high-temperature stability
summary: The transformer–variational-autoencoder ProT-VAE generated synthetic enzyme sequences that were tested experimentally. Among 190 designed human phenylalanine-hydroxylase sequences, 69 had measurable activity and 19 exceeded wild-type activity, with the best at 2.5× wild type. A designed γ-carbonic anhydrase had a measured melting temperature of 116 °C (61 °C above the most thermostable sequence previously reported by the authors) and remained active in 23% methyl diethanolamine at pH 11.25 and 93 °C.
ai_technology: Protein Transformer Variational AutoEncoder (ProT-VAE), using ProtT5nv transformer representations and a family-specific variational autoencoder
organization: Evozyne; NVIDIA

title: TeleProt-guided engineering yields a nuclease variant with improved neutral-pH biofilm degradation
summary: A machine-learning-guided design and high-throughput screening campaign produced a Bacillus licheniformis NucB variant with 19-fold higher measured specific activity than wild type at pH 7. At 1 μM in a laboratory biofilm assay at neutral pH, the selected variant degraded 71% ± 2% of the biofilm versus 13% ± 3% for wild-type NucB.
ai_technology: TeleProt machine-learning-guided protein-library design framework; best-performing ML3 variant selected by model-based optimization with a deep neural network (MBO-DNN)
organization: X, the Moonshot Factory; Google DeepMind; Triplebar; University of Cambridge

title: FRASE-bot screening identifies a small-molecule ligand that selectively kills CIB1-dependent cancer cells
summary: FRASE-bot used a neural-network nativeness score to triage protein–ligand fragments, then used the retained structural features to seed virtual screening for Calcium and Integrin Binding Protein 1 (CIB1). Of 56 purchased virtual-screen hits, 29 showed dose-dependent CIB1 displacement; compound UNC10245380 (UNC5380) had a TR-FRET displacement IC50 of 8.0 ± 2.5 μM and selectively killed CIB1-depletion-sensitive triple-negative breast cancer cells in the reported assays, with no detected killing in an insensitive line.
ai_technology: FRASE-bot: fragment-in-structural-environment screening with a neural-network nativeness scoring model
organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; University of Missouri

title: Chemical language models produce experimentally confirmed dual ligands for three target pairs
summary: A generative chemical language model was fine-tuned on known ligands for paired targets. Prospective synthesis and in-vitro assays found seven of twelve tested designs modulated both intended targets, with confirmed dual activity across FXR/sEH, FXR/THRβ and PPARδ/sEH. Activities varied substantially and were often unbalanced; the strongest reported sEH inhibitor, compound 7, had IC50 17 nM with micromolar PPARδ agonism.
ai_technology: Target-pair-fine-tuned chemical language model (four-layer LSTM recurrent neural network trained on SMILES, pretrained on 365,000 ChEMBL molecules)
organization: Goethe University Frankfurt; Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München; Fraunhofer Institute for Translational Medicine and Pharmacology

title: Iterative machine learning identifies potent inhibitors of alpha-synuclein secondary nucleation
summary: A structure-based iterative-learning workflow combined prior α-synuclein fibril-binding hits, a junction-tree variational autoencoder, a random-forest regressor and Gaussian-process residual model to rank compounds for repeated testing. Prospective iterations produced multiple molecules inhibiting seeded α-synuclein aggregation in vitro; lead I4.05 had a reported kinetic inhibitory constant (KIC50) of 0.52 μM (95% CI 0.45–0.59 μM), compared with extrapolated values of 18.2 μM for its parent and 36.4 μM for Anle-138b in the authors’ assay. Leads also showed activity in lipid-induced and spontaneous aggregation assays.
ai_technology: Iterative structure-based learning workflow using a junction-tree variational autoencoder, random-forest regressor and Gaussian-process residual model
organization: University of Cambridge; US National Institutes of Health, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases; A*STAR; Indiana University School of Medicine

title: ClickGen designs PARP1 inhibitors with measured nanomolar activity
summary: ClickGen combines reaction-based molecular generation, reinforcement learning and inpainting to generate synthesizable candidate structures. In a PARP1 case study, researchers selected and synthesized three generated lead molecules; two showed nanomolar PARP1 inhibition in vitro, with reported IC50 values of 19.24 ± 1.63 nM and 69.73 ± 14.57 nM. The two compounds also showed antiproliferative activity in several tested cancer cell lines and lower toxicity in the reported normal-cell assays than the most toxic lead compounds.
ai_technology: ClickGen deep-learning reaction-based molecular generator with reinforcement learning, Monte Carlo tree search and an inpainting generator
organization: Zhejiang University; Chengde Medical University; Hunan University; Macau University of Science and Technology; CarbonSilicon AI Technology Co., Ltd.; Macau Polytechnic University

title: Joint molecular modeling identifies seven low-micromolar kinase hits beyond its training chemistry
summary: A joint molecular model combined bioactivity prediction and molecule reconstruction to estimate how unfamiliar a candidate structure was to its training distribution. In a prospective screen of commercial compounds against PIM1 and CDK1, unfamiliarity-informed selection led to seven compounds with low-micromolar potency and limited similarity to training molecules. The authors also evaluated the metric across 33 experimentally labelled bioactivity datasets.
ai_technology: Joint molecular model (JMM): semi-supervised molecular property-prediction and reconstruction model using a SMILES encoder; reconstruction loss defines the unfamiliarity score
organization: Eindhoven University of Technology; Centre for Living Technologies (TU/e, WUR, UU and UMC Utrecht)

title: ESM-guided metagenome mining identifies seven new Cas12a subtypes with distinct activities
summary: AIL-Scan fine-tuned an evolutionary-scale protein language model (ESM) on Cas proteins to search metagenomic sequences and identify previously undocumented Cas12a lineages. The study classified seven previously unreported Cas12a subtypes with distinct CRISPR-locus organization, then biochemically characterized 16 Cas12a proteins from the candidate clades, documenting different DNA-cleavage and PAM-recognition preferences. The authors also demonstrated a specific assay strategy for distinguishing the KRAS G12C variant using a Cas12a variant with broader PAM recognition.
ai_technology: AIL-Scan, using fine-tuned ESM-2 protein language-model embeddings and a machine-learning classifier to identify Cas proteins and predict Cas12a trans-cleavage activity
organization: Zhejiang Lab; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Nanjing Medical University; Tongji University; National University of Singapore; ShanghaiTech University; Zhejiang University; Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Evo genomic language model designs functional toxin-antitoxin and anti-CRISPR systems
summary: Evo used genomic context to generate functional bacterial defence-system components. The paper reports an AI-generated toxin and low-sequence-similarity antitoxins that neutralized it in growth assays, including antitoxins that also acted against multiple natural toxins; it also reports five generated anti-CRISPR proteins that protected bacteria against Cas9 activity in cell and phage assays. Two generated anti-CRISPR proteins lacked significant sequence similarity to known proteins. These experiments demonstrate function-guided genomic design beyond simple copying of natural sequences.
ai_technology: Evo 1.5, a long-context generative genomic language model trained on prokaryotic DNA sequences
organization: Arc Institute; Stanford University

title: AI-generated virtual spatial proteomics reveals lung-cancer tumor–immune niches associated with immunotherapy response
summary: HEX, a pathology-image AI model, predicts spatial expression of 40 protein biomarkers from routine H&E slides. In retrospective NSCLC cohorts, combining HEX-derived virtual spatial proteomics with histology improved prognosis prediction and, in a separate 148-patient immune-checkpoint-inhibitor cohort, improved response prediction over H&E-only and virtual-proteomics-only models. The authors interpreted virtual maps as showing co-localized T-helper and cytotoxic T-cell niches among responders and immunosuppressive macrophage/neutrophil aggregates among non-responders.
ai_technology: HEX (H&E to protein expression), using a pathology foundation-model backbone; MICA (multimodal integration via co-attention)
organization: Stanford University; and collaborating institutions

title: Contrastive-learning biomarker discovered from phase 2 data retrospectively generalizes to phase 3 immunotherapy outcomes
summary: The Predictive Biomarker Modeling Framework (PBMF), an ensemble neural network trained with a treatment-versus-control contrastive objective, identified a composite clinicogenomic biomarker using phase 2 POPLAR data for atezolizumab versus docetaxel. When applied retrospectively to the phase 3 OAK trial, its biomarker-positive group had a treatment-versus-control overall-survival hazard ratio of 0.59 (95% CI 0.47–0.74); an interpretable distilled decision tree produced HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.43–0.70). The tree used baseline ctDNA maximum allele frequency, lesion diameter, and mutation status in KMT2D, TSC1, ATM, PDGFRA and LRP1B.
ai_technology: Predictive Biomarker Modeling Framework (PBMF), an ensemble of neural networks using a contrastive treatment/control objective; knowledge-distilled decision tree
organization: AstraZeneca; Tempus AI

title: Deep-learning splice prediction links a PARP2 variant to altered protein isoforms and influenza susceptibility
summary: By combining single-cell splicing-QTL analysis during influenza A infection with SpliceAI/Pangolin annotation and statistical fine-mapping, researchers prioritized causal splice variants. They experimentally characterized rs2297616 in PARP2: its A allele creates an alternative 5′ splice donor, adding 39 nucleotides and producing a protein isoform 13 amino acids longer. CRISPR-edited A549 cells showed the predicted splice and protein changes; the A-allele edited cells also had higher influenza A infection than G-allele cells. The variant was associated with higher viral burden in a panel of 96 lymphoblastoid cell lines.
ai_technology: SpliceAI and Pangolin deep-learning splice-effect predictors, integrated with single-cell scHi-HOST sQTL mapping and SuSiE statistical fine-mapping
organization: Duke University

title: AlphaFold2-guided mining identifies context-independent cytidine deaminases for efficient base editing
summary: Researchers used AlphaFold2 to predict structures for 1,483 cytidine deaminases, clustered the predictions and experimentally characterized representatives. The screen identified previously uncharacterized enzymes with high editing efficiency, and CD0208^P52A showed little sequence-context preference across AC/GC/TC/CC motifs, a narrow editing window and relatively low off-target activity. In mammalian cells, its base editor introduced stop codons in single- and multicopy genes without DNA double-strand breaks.
ai_technology: AlphaFold2 protein-structure prediction, followed by structural clustering of candidate cytidine deaminases
organization: Agricultural Genomics Institute at Shenzhen, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

title: GPT-3.5 reasoning helps connect MRE11 to social-context sleep regulation in Drosophila
summary: A study combined GPT-3.5-generated gene-function context with a genome-wide Drosophila RNAi behavioral screen. It identified MRE11 knockdown as reducing sleep in group-housed flies, a result the authors report as previously unrecognized in this social context. GPT-3.5 reasoning proposed a link from MRE11 to Dop1R1/dopaminergic signaling; treatment with a Dop1R1 antagonist partially rescued sleep, locomotor and social-activity phenotypes in MRE11-RNAi flies.
ai_technology: GPT-3.5, prompted for genome-wide Drosophila gene-function interpretation and chain-of-thought relationship hypotheses
organization: Huazhong University of Science and Technology; and collaborating institutions

title: GET and interaction assays link a leukemia-risk PAX5 variant to stronger NR2C2 binding
summary: The General Expression Transformer (GET) model inferred cell-type-specific transcription-factor motif interactions from regulatory data and nominated a lymphocyte-specific interaction between PAX5 and nuclear-receptor-family factors. AlphaFold multimer modeling and PAX5 proximity-labeling in a B-ALL cell line supported interaction with NR2C2; the leukemia-associated PAX5 G183S variant showed increased PAX5–NR2C2 proximity signal. The variant-specific expression profile was enriched for predicted NR/3 and shared PAX5/NR/3 target genes, suggesting a possible regulatory mechanism for the germline risk variant.
ai_technology: GET (General Expression Transformer) foundation model for cell-type-specific regulatory grammar; AlphaFold2/AlphaFold Multimer for structural hypothesis assessment
organization: Columbia University; Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence; collaborating institutions

title: Paper2Agent integrates perturbation datasets to prioritize GPR137 at a psoriasis risk locus
summary: Paper2Agent-generated agents used AlphaGenome to prioritize GPR137 as the top predicted gene affected by psoriasis-associated variant rs887314 in CD4+ T cells, then integrated that prediction with existing MPRA-coupled scCRISPRi and CD4+ T-cell Perturb-seq data. A cross-screen correlation of gene-expression signatures supported GPR137 as the probable causal gene under stimulated conditions (Spearman rho 0.613 at 8 h and 0.630 at 48 h; FDR < 0.05), but not at rest. The paper presents this as activation-dependent computational evidence.
ai_technology: Paper2Agent-generated AlphaGenome, MPRA-coupled scCRISPRi and CD4+ T-cell Perturb-seq agents, coordinated through an AI co-scientist
organization: Stanford University; collaborating institutions

title: Machine learning links mycobacterial protein disorder to targeted degradation potential
summary: Researchers combined a genetic chemical-proximity platform and experimental screening of 72 Mycobacterium smegmatis protein candidates with machine learning. A Lasso model trained on measured degradation data identified N-terminal disorder propensity as associated with degradation potential and predicted candidate targets among 348 essential proteins conserved between M. smegmatis and M. tuberculosis. Experimentally induced degradation of selected essential M. smegmatis proteins inhibited bacterial growth and, for some targets, potentiated antimicrobial compounds.
ai_technology: Lasso regression model trained on sequence and structural protein descriptors, including AlphaFold2 confidence and predicted disorder propensity
organization: Harvard Medical School; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning-guided closed-loop synthesis experimentally realizes unreported dye molecules
summary: A closed-loop molecular discovery platform combined machine-learning property prediction, automated synthesis and characterization, and iterative model updates to explore dye-like molecules. In the published Science abstract, the team reports experimentally realizing 294 previously unreported molecules across three design–make–test–analyze cycles on four rarely reported scaffolds, while also identifying six top-performing molecules in a second case study using pre-existing chemical-space examples.
ai_technology: Autonomous molecular-discovery platform integrating generative and property-prediction machine-learning models, Bayesian optimization, and synthesis-planning software with automated chemical synthesis and characterization
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; collaborating institutions

title: Sequential model-based optimization discovers two previously unreported chemical reactions
summary: A programmable robotic synthesis platform used inline HPLC, Raman or NMR feedback and closed-loop optimization to explore selected reaction spaces. In a tosMIC campaign, sequential model-based optimization with a Gaussian-process surrogate identified a reaction between toluenesulphonylmethyl isocyanide and benzylidenemalononitrile; subsequent optimization increased yield from the 27% initial condition to 49% (22 percentage points) over 50 reactions. The article also reports a second previously unreported reaction and an exploratory trifluoromethylation campaign that discovered new molecules.
ai_technology: ChemputationOptimizer, a sensor-integrated reaction engine with sequential model-based optimization (Gaussian-process surrogate); the platform also exposes random search, design-of-experiments, Bayesian-optimization and genetic-algorithm routines
organization: University of Glasgow

title: CHAI image-only histology biomarker stratifies metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer outcomes in independent trial data
summary: A computational histology AI platform built a prognostic signature from diagnostic whole-slide images in 507 CHAARTED participants and evaluated the locked signature in 684 ENZAMET participants. In the independent ENZAMET cohort, the unfavorable-risk group had worse overall survival (HR 2.6, 95% CI 2.0–3.4) and progression-free survival (HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.7–2.7); associations remained after adjustment for clinical variables. The article also reports treatment-interaction analyses, but this retrospective secondary analysis does not establish prospective treatment-selection benefit.
ai_technology: Computational Histology Artificial Intelligence (CHAI) platform
organization: Valar Labs; and the CHAARTED/ENZAMET trial collaborators

title: Prospective multicentre study combines EV protein biomarkers and machine learning for preclinical oesophageal cancer detection
summary: The BarFlare assay and an interpretable multi-criteria decision-making classification-fusion machine-learning framework combined extracellular-vesicle SCC and MMP13 biomarkers with clinical factors. The model was evaluated in prospective multicentre diagnostic cohorts and two population cohorts; the longitudinal cohort contained baseline samples from 30 people who later developed oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma, with a reported median lead time of 34.9 months and AUC 0.864. The paper also reports external diagnostic validation in two cohorts.
ai_technology: Multi-criteria decision-making Classification Fusion (MCF) machine-learning framework; 289 candidate feature-selector/classifier pairs were compared and three base models fused
organization: Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; and collaborating hospitals/cohorts

title: Machine-learning selection of a six-protein panel for atherosclerosis severity and patient stratification
summary: Five machine-learning classifiers integrated clinical and serum-proteomic data from carotid atherosclerotic stenosis (60 participants), dyslipidemia (55) and healthy controls (66). A consensus approach identified a six-protein panel (B2M, GPV, MMP9, PLF4, TSP1 and fibrinogen/FB isoforms) that distinguished the atherosclerosis group from the comparison groups, with reported ROC-AUC above 0.9 across the tested classifiers. Protein levels were evaluated by flow cytometry and ELISA in an independent external cohort that included patients with acute atherothrombotic stroke.
ai_technology: Five machine-learning classifiers: Naive Bayes, linear SVM, random forest, Extra Trees and AdaBoost
organization: Biomedical Research and Innovation Institute of Cadiz, University of Cadiz and collaborating clinical institutions

title: ESM-FEP combines protein-language-model fitness screening and free-energy calculations to engineer herbicide-detoxifying maize dioxygenase
summary: ESM-FEP was applied to Zea mays dioxygenase ZmHSL1B and nominated a quadruple mutant (Q140H/Y205F/L332R/K336F) with approximately sevenfold higher catalytic efficiency for mesotrione detoxification than wild type, measured by in-vitro assays and kinetic analysis. Arabidopsis thaliana expressing the engineered variant showed enhanced herbicide tolerance in the reported transgenic tests.
ai_technology: ESM-FEP (fine-tuned ESM-2 protein language model plus alchemical free-energy perturbation)
organization: Central China Normal University, State Key Laboratory of Green Pesticide

title: ESM-Ezy mining identifies multicopper oxidases and asparaginases with experimentally improved catalytic properties
summary: The ESM-1b semantic-embedding mining strategy nominated low-sequence-similarity enzyme candidates. In the reported experimental assessment, 44% of tested multicopper oxidases outperformed their query enzymes in at least one measured property (including catalytic efficiency, heat/solvent tolerance or pH stability); 51% were reported to excel in environmental-remediation applications. Among mined L-asparaginases, 40% had higher specific activity and catalytic efficiency than query enzymes.
ai_technology: ESM-Ezy, using ESM-1b protein-language-model embeddings and semantic-space similarity
organization: Westlake University; and collaborating institutions

title: PepMLM designs experimentally binding target-conditioned peptide ligands, including peptides used for targeted protein degradation
summary: PepMLM fine-tunes ESM-2 using masked-language modeling conditioned on a target protein sequence to generate de novo linear peptide binders without structural input. In the reported experiments, selected peptides showed sequence-specific binding to targets including NCAM1 and AMHR2; incorporation into ubiquitin-based antibody constructs enabled targeted degradation of disease-relevant proteins, including Huntington’s disease drivers and viral phosphoproteins.
ai_technology: PepMLM, ESM-2 fine-tuned with target-sequence-conditioned masked language modeling
organization: Cornell University; and collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning analysis of plasma metabolomic fingerprints yields a 21-metabolite gastric-cancer panel validated across multicentre cohorts
summary: In a multicentre study, machine-learning analysis of plasma metabolic fingerprints from 1,944 retrospective participants selected a 21-metabolite panel that differentiated gastric-cancer from non-cancer cohorts; five model types achieved AUCs of 0.921–0.971 in discovery and 0.907–0.940 in external verification. Prospective testing in 264 participants using both NPELDI-MS and UPLC-MS reported diagnostic AUCs of 0.855–0.918 and 0.856–0.916, respectively. The paper also reports a four-metabolite prognostic score based on retrospective survival data.
ai_technology: Neural network, lasso regression, ridge regression, support-vector machine and random-forest models applied to plasma metabolic fingerprints
organization: Zhejiang Cancer Hospital; Shanghai Jiao Tong University and six collaborating clinical centers

title: Machine-learning-guided CsrA homolog screens reveal divergent bacterial regulatory activities
summary: A Swarm-seq assay tested more than 500 bacterial CsrA homologs for regulation of Bacillus subtilis swarming and found two functional classes: several homologs strongly inhibited swarming while others failed despite conserved sequence and canonical GGA motifs in the hag transcript. A random-forest model trained on these assays predicted homolog activity across thousands of sequences; experimental testing supported predicted Class I regulatory activity for Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus CsrA and Pseudomonas putida RsmA. The findings indicate sequence conservation and the canonical RNA motif do not alone determine these tested regulatory effects.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning classifier trained on Swarm-seq functional assay data
organization: University of Chicago

title: GRACE designs two carbonic-anhydrase-like enzymes with measured catalytic activity
summary: The GRACE workflow combined RFdiffusion structure generation, ProteinMPNN sequence design, CLEAN enzyme classification and solubility/structure filtering to select two carbonic-anhydrase-like sequences from 10,000 candidates. The authors report experimental expression and carbonic anhydrase activity: dCA12_2 at 400 WAU/mL and dCA23_1 at 260 WAU/mL in the reported assay.
ai_technology: GRACE (RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and CLEAN, with computational solubility/structural filters)
organization: National Cheng Kung University; and collaborating institutions

title: Self-iterative learning finds RNA-targeting prokaryotic Argonautes and an RNA-modification-sensing activity
summary: The self-iterative hierarchical ensemble model (SIM) nominated six high-confidence prokaryotic Argonaute candidates; five were experimentally validated as RNA-targeting proteins. The study identified three uncharacterized Agos with a novel N-terminal domain, defining a previously unrecognized subclass. Biochemical and in-vivo experiments on Haloferax profundi Ago (HpAgo) established RNA cleavage and a distinctive RNA-modification-sensing capability, which the authors used to build a method for quantifying modified RNA.
ai_technology: Self-Iterative hierarchical ensemble Model (SIM), an ensemble-learning and self-training pipeline
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; ShanghaiTech University and collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning models identify carbon-source-dependent metabolic reactions that control Escherichia coli growth
summary: Elastic-net and multilayer-perceptron models integrated genome-wide gene-deletion data and simulated fluxes to predict beneficial and detrimental reactions for E. coli growth on 30 carbon sources. Beyond training-set examples, the authors experimentally validated model predictions about the glyoxylate shunt, pyruvate dehydrogenase, and redundant purine-biosynthesis reactions. The findings showed that effects of energy-generating pathways depend on carbon source, while biosynthetic pathways were more generally growth-promoting across the tested conditions.
ai_technology: Elastic-net regression and multilayer-perceptron models
organization: Konkuk University

title: Deep-learning-guided mining of NRPS scaffolds yields active naturally inspired antimicrobial peptides
summary: The team mined 216,408 bacterial genomes, identifying 335,024 NRPS clusters and 328 dereplicated peptide scaffolds. Deep-learning scoring selected five synthesized peptides; P2 showed MIC50 values of 1–2 μM against Vibrio parahaemolyticus and V. alginolyticus. Deep-learning-guided sequence optimization produced P2.2, which showed increased antibacterial activity, membrane effects and reduced hemolysis in assays.
ai_technology: Deep-learning peptide activity scoring and sequence-optimization algorithms
organization: Zhejiang University of Technology; and collaborating institutions

title: KPPepGen generates experimentally active pathogen-specific antimicrobial peptides
summary: KPPepGen combines Gene Ontology and pathogen-knowledge-graph prompts with a diffusion model to generate pathogen-conditioned peptide sequences. The paper reports valid peptide generation for 56 pathogens and wet-lab evaluation of nine novel peptides for Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, reporting antimicrobial activity and low cytotoxicity. Its Magainin 2 optimization result is a separate model-comparison metric, not a clinical outcome.
ai_technology: KPPepGen knowledge-aware prompt diffusion model
organization: Huazhong Agricultural University

title: Latent diffusion designs antimicrobial peptides active against fungi and drug-resistant bacteria
summary: A latent-diffusion and molecular-dynamics pipeline generated and filtered peptide sequences; 40 synthesized candidates were tested, and 25 met the study's MIC threshold for antibacterial or antifungal activity. AMP-29 showed activity against Candida glabrata and efficacy in a murine skin-infection model, while AMP-24 showed in-vitro Gram-negative activity and efficacy in murine Acinetobacter baumannii skin and lung infection models.
ai_technology: Latent diffusion model coupled to molecular dynamics and peptide filtering/ranking
organization: Shandong University; and collaborating institutions

title: CAIMAN validates AI prescreening of typical and atypical large-bowel biopsies across UK and Portuguese cohorts
summary: CAIMAN is a weakly supervised deep-learning model trained on pathologist-labeled whole-slide images to classify typical, atypical non-neoplastic and atypical neoplastic bowel biopsies. In three external cohorts comprising 1,536 slides from the UK and Portugal, it detected atypical biopsies with AUROC values of 0.9431, 0.9576 and 0.9636. At 99% sensitivity, it outperformed the prior IDaRS pipeline on two external cohorts, but not the third.
ai_technology: CAIMAN (Colorectal AI Model for Abnormality Detection), a weakly supervised deep-learning whole-slide image classifier
organization: University of Warwick; University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Foundation Trust, collaborating UK hospitals and IMP Diagnostics (Portugal)

title: Multi-centre validation tests AI-empowered OncoSeek across 15,122 participants and four assay platforms
summary: A 2025 study added four cohorts to evaluate the seven-protein-marker OncoSeek test, which combines blood protein tumor markers and clinical variables with AI. Across seven cohorts from seven centres in China, Brazil and the United States, totaling 15,122 participants, the reported overall sensitivity was 58.4% at 92.0% specificity; the symptomatic cohort had 73.1% sensitivity at 90.6% specificity. The study also tested performance across four platforms and two sample types.
ai_technology: OncoSeek AI-empowered blood test combining seven protein tumor markers with individual clinical data
organization: SeekIn; Henan Cancer Hospital, Peking University Shenzhen Hospital, First Saúde, Yonsei University and collaborating clinical centres

title: HiDDEN finds malignant-like cell signals in early multiple-myeloma precursor samples
summary: HiDDEN refines sample-level case labels at single-cell resolution. In human bone-marrow single-cell RNA-seq data, its labels tracked manual neoplastic-cell annotations in mixed precursor samples and inferred malignant-like cells in three low-purity MGUS samples that the original manual analysis had labeled as containing only healthy cells. The inferred cells were enriched for previously described malignancy-associated gene signatures. In a separate mouse demyelination dataset, HiDDEN identified an early endothelial subpopulation with expression changes associated with angiogenesis, blood–brain-barrier breakdown and extracellular-matrix responses.
ai_technology: HiDDEN, a machine-learning framework for refining disease/condition labels at single-cell resolution
organization: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; collaborating institutions

title: MILTON-augmented disease cohorts surface putative new gene–disease associations in UK Biobank data
summary: MILTON uses machine learning on routine clinical biomarkers, quantitative traits and plasma proteomics to predict disease phenotypes and augment case labels in UK Biobank. In a phenome-wide analysis of 484,230 genome-sequenced participants, the authors report 182 putative novel gene–disease associations that were not genome-wide significant in baseline cohorts or explained by biomarker associations; 38.9% of the 167 mappable signals were nominally supported with the same direction in FinnGen.
ai_technology: MILTON (Machine Learning with Phenotype Associations), an ensemble machine-learning framework for disease prediction from clinical and molecular biomarkers
organization: AstraZeneca Centre for Genomics Research; and collaborating UK Biobank/FinnGen research institutions

title: SCimilarity links fibrosis-associated macrophage states across diseases and validates a matching in-vitro cell state
summary: SCimilarity searched a 23.4-million-cell reference atlas spanning 412 single-cell RNA-sequencing studies using query profiles from interstitial-lung-disease macrophages and fibroblasts. It identified fibrosis-associated macrophage-like states in other fibrotic diseases, COVID-19 and selected tumour datasets, and a 3D hydrogel culture as a high-ranking in-vitro match; the authors report experimentally demonstrating that this system reproduces the queried macrophage state.
ai_technology: SCimilarity, a deep metric-learning model for querying cell-state similarity across single-cell atlases
organization: Genentech; and collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning analysis identifies a plasma protein signature associated with ALS years before symptoms
summary: In a plasma-proteomics study, machine learning selected a 17-protein panel from 33 proteins that differed between 183 people with ALS and 309 controls. The panel distinguished ALS from healthy participants and other neurological diseases in a held-out test set (AUC 96.2%, balanced accuracy 89.3%) and was assessed in independent cohorts, including UK Biobank samples. Applying the model to presymptomatic samples from people who later developed ALS showed risk-score shifts up to about 10 years before symptom onset.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classification model trained on Olink plasma proteomic features
organization: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke; and collaborating ALS registry and research institutions

title: A seven-gene machine-learning score shows an Alzheimer-associated signal in an independent plasma cohort
summary: A machine-learning pipeline selected a seven-gene lactylation-related transcriptomic score (LDS) from nine Alzheimer disease cohorts. The study evaluated the signature in seven independent brain transcriptomic datasets and a single-center clinical plasma cohort of 540 participants (180 controls, 90 with amnestic mild cognitive impairment and 270 with Alzheimer disease). Plasma LDS had AUC 0.772 for Alzheimer disease; combining LDS with p-tau181 and p-tau217 had AUC 0.859. LDS scores increased across control, aMCI and Alzheimer groups and correlated with MMSE and Braak stage.
ai_technology: Lactylation-Derived Score (LDS), a random-forest feature-screening and partial least-squares logistic-regression model
organization: Southeast University Zhongda Hospital; and collaborating clinical and research institutions

title: A machine-learning plasma panel classifies some REM sleep behavior disorder participants years before motor Parkinson diagnosis
summary: Researchers developed a targeted multiplex mass-spectrometry assay for eight plasma proteins and applied machine learning to distinguish Parkinson disease from healthy controls and classify people with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD). In the reported longitudinal iRBD cohorts, the model classified 79% of participants up to seven years before motor Parkinson disease or dementia with Lewy bodies onset. The work connects a targeted protein panel to a pre-motor disease signal in measured blood samples.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classifier using recursive feature elimination on targeted plasma proteomic measurements
organization: University of Oxford; University Medical Center Göttingen and collaborating European research institutions

title: Machine learning selects CSF and serum protein panels associated with early Alzheimer disease
summary: In a proteomic study, researchers measured paired CSF and serum samples in a discovery cohort and used random-forest machine learning to select a 19-protein CSF panel and an eight-protein serum panel to distinguish mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer disease from cognitively normal participants. Targeted proteomics verified candidate proteins in an independent multicenter cohort. In small held-out test groups, the CSF panel reached AUC 0.984 and the serum panel AUC 0.881; the CSF panel also distinguished Alzheimer-related MCI from frontotemporal dementia, ALS and Huntington disease in the reported analyses.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning classifiers on CSF and serum proteomic profiles
organization: Capital Medical University; Westlake University, Zhejiang University and collaborating Chinese clinical institutions

title: LightGBM links a three-protein blood panel to biopsy-staged MASLD fibrosis
summary: A translational study combined a disease-related mouse gene-expression signature, human liver-biopsy transcriptomes and serum protein measurements to select IGFBP7, SSc5D and Sema4D as a three-protein panel for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). A LightGBM model classified biopsy-staged fibrosis, with AUCs 0.82 for F0/F1, 0.89 for F2 and 0.87 for F3/F4 in the development/testing data. In an independent Danish cohort of 156 patients, AUC was 0.84 for F0/F1 and F3/F4; performance for F2 was lower (AUC 0.62).
ai_technology: LightGBM classifier (TLM3) using the three serum proteins IGFBP7, SSc5D and Sema4D
organization: TNO; Amsterdam UMC, Leiden University Medical Center and collaborating Dutch and Danish clinical institutions

title: A machine-learning-selected P4 serum panel detects hepatocellular carcinoma and signals cirrhosis-to-cancer progression
summary: A staged serum-proteomics study across 1,002 individuals used random-forest machine learning to select a four-marker panel, P4 (HABP2, CD163, AFP and PIVKA-II). In an independent validation set, the panel distinguished hepatocellular carcinoma from cirrhosis (AUC 0.979; sensitivity 0.925; specificity 0.915) and from healthy controls (AUC 0.992). In a prospective external cohort of cirrhosis patients followed for HCC, it predicted conversion with AUC 0.890 and median lead time of 11.4 months before imaging diagnosis.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning model for serum-protein panel selection and HCC classification
organization: Mengchao Hepatobiliary Hospital of Fujian Medical University; Fujian Cancer Hospital, Zhejiang University and collaborating Chinese clinical institutions

title: Mal-ID maps disease-associated immune-receptor patterns across infections and autoimmune conditions
summary: Mal-ID analyzed B-cell and T-cell receptor repertoires from 593 people, including patients with COVID-19, HIV, systemic lupus erythematosus and type-1 diabetes, influenza-vaccination recipients and healthy controls. Its combined models classified held-out immune states and highlighted disease-associated receptor patterns; interpretation identified distinct autoreactivity features in lupus and type-1 diabetes and antigen-associated receptor sequences in COVID-19. The authors also evaluated classification on independent COVID-19 cohorts.
ai_technology: Mal-ID (MAchine Learning for Immunological Diagnosis), an ensemble using repertoire feature models and ESM-2 protein-language-model embeddings
