organization: Stanford University; Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation, Duke University, University of Pennsylvania and collaborating institutions

title: Active learning identifies a higher-activity streptavidin variant for gold-catalyzed hydroamination
summary: An iterative active-learning campaign engineered a streptavidin artificial metalloenzyme for the known-to-the-authors gold-catalyzed hydroamination of 2-ethynylaniline to indole. Gaussian-process models guided screening across five residues in a 3.2-million-variant sequence space. The final-round library contained 38% variants more active than the prior reference, compared with 3% in the initial library. The leading variant, Sav CTNLV, showed 18-fold higher cell-specific activity than wild-type Sav and threefold higher activity than the previous reference variant in replicate testing.
ai_technology: Active-learning Gaussian-process regression model with optimized sequence descriptors and experimental-noise estimates
organization: ETH Zurich; University of Basel and University of Regensburg

title: MODIFY-guided library screening identifies a cytochrome c variant active in both carbon–boron and carbon–silicon bond formation
summary: Researchers applied MODIFY, an ensemble model combining protein language models and sequence-density models, to design a diverse high-fitness library for Rhodothermus marinus cytochrome c. Experimental screening identified variant MLYPPT, which catalyzed both non-natural borylation and silylation: reported total turnover numbers were 2,880 and 2,740, with enantiomeric ratios of 94:6 and 97:3, respectively. The same library yielded distinct high-performing variants for each reaction.
ai_technology: MODIFY (ML-optimized library design with improved fitness and diversity)
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology; University of Pittsburgh; University of California, Santa Barbara

title: Active learning identifies a protoglobin variant with 99% yield and cis-selective cyclopropanation
summary: An iterative machine-learning campaign engineered the protoglobin from Pyrobaculum arsenaticum (ParPgb) for non-native cyclopropanation of 4-vinylanisole. After two model-guided rounds following an initial library screen, variant MPFDY gave 99% total cyclopropane yield and a 14:1 cis:trans ratio in the reported assay, compared with a parent variant that produced about 40% yield and favored trans product. The result demonstrates a specific sequence combination with improved yield and stereoselectivity in this enzyme scaffold.
ai_technology: ALDE (Active Learning-assisted Directed Evolution), using a bootstrapped deep-neural-network ensemble and Thompson sampling
organization: California Institute of Technology; University of California, Berkeley; Elegen Corp

title: An ML-generated MinE homolog restores bacterial cell division patterning in vivo
summary: A machine-learning-generated MinE homolog, synMinEv25, restored Min oscillations and wild-type-like cell growth and morphology when substituted for the native minE gene in an E. coli strain lacking minDE. Researchers generated variants with a multiple-sequence-alignment variational autoencoder, used AlphaFold2-based structural scoring to select candidates, and screened them in synthetic-cell mimics before in-vivo testing. The validated variant is a distant homolog with less than 50% sequence identity to E. coli MinE.
ai_technology: Multiple-sequence-alignment variational autoencoder (MSA-VAE), AlphaFold2 Multimer, and a structure-based divide-and-conquer scoring pipeline
organization: Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry

title: Closed-loop learning links donor–acceptor molecules’ photostability to higher triplet states
summary: A closed-loop synthesis and learning campaign found that solution photostability across a donor–bridge–acceptor molecular series correlated with the high-energy portion of the triplet excited-state manifold, beyond the commonly considered lowest triplet state. Researchers tested the model-derived hypothesis on an experimental set and changed solvent triplet energy to test the proposed Dexter triplet-energy-transfer degradation pathway. The study used Bayesian optimization and interpretable supervised learning to extract the chemical hypothesis from measured photostability data.
ai_technology: Closed-loop transfer (CLT), combining Gryffin Bayesian optimization with physics-feature supervised learning
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; University of Toronto; Vector Institute; University of Chicago; University of California, Berkeley

title: Machine-learning search of archived spectra reveals vinyl–NHC coupling products in palladium catalysis
summary: MEDUSA Search mined archived high-resolution mass spectra and uncovered previously unreported vinyl–N-heterocyclic-carbene (NHC) coupling products in Pd/NHC-catalyzed Mizoroki–Heck reactions. Researchers retrieved the corresponding reaction records and independently tested the proposed transformation with multiple palladium–NHC complexes; ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry and MS/MS supported the product formulas and structures. The work also found an ethyl–NHC product across tested reaction mixtures, suggesting additional catalyst-transformation pathways.
ai_technology: MEDUSA Search, an isotope-distribution-driven HRMS search engine with machine-learning ion-threshold regression and false-positive classification
organization: Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry, Russian Academy of Sciences; Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

title: Deep learning on routine pathology slides prescreens FGFR-altered bladder cancers in a global study
summary: A deep-learning device analyzed routine H&E whole-slide images to estimate whether advanced urothelial tumors carried selected FGFR2/FGFR3 alterations used for erdafitinib eligibility. In a separate 350-slide retrospective validation set, the device achieved 88.7% sensitivity and 31.8% specificity; it was also prospectively integrated into a non-interventional study spanning 89 sites in nine countries. The paper projected a 28.7% reduction in molecular tests assuming 15% biomarker prevalence; that estimate was simulated, not a measured population-level reduction.
ai_technology: FGFR Device, a multi-instance-learning attention model with a convolutional neural-network backbone
organization: Janssen Research & Development, LLC (Johnson & Johnson)

title: Machine-guided synthetic regulatory DNA drives cell-type-specific expression across cell lines and vertebrates
summary: The CODA platform used the Malinois deep-learning model and sequence-search algorithms to design synthetic cis-regulatory elements (CREs). In massively parallel reporter assays, 94.1% of the synthetic sequences met the authors’ cell-type-specificity criterion, versus 73.6% of model-selected natural sequences and 40.6% of chromatin-mark-selected natural sequences; synthetic sequences also had higher measured target/off-target separation across K562, HepG2 and SK-N-SH cells. In transgenic zebrafish, two of three liver-directed and two of three neuron-directed CREs showed the intended activity. One neuron-directed sequence, synN1, retained cortical and neuronal expression in mice, including postnatal neocortical layer 6 and subplate neurons.
ai_technology: CODA (Computational Optimization of DNA Activity) with Malinois deep neural network and AdaLead, simulated annealing, and Fast SeqProp sequence search/design algorithms
organization: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; The Jackson Laboratory; Yale University

title: AI-derived histology biomarker stratifies first-line chemotherapy outcomes in advanced pancreatic cancer
summary: The CHAI computational-histology platform generated a locked H&E-based biomarker intended to distinguish advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients with differential outcomes on fluoropyrimidine-based versus gemcitabine-based chemotherapy. In an independent validation cohort of 299 patients from the prospectively collected COMPASS and Know Your Tumor cohorts, the 173 patients classified F-pref had longer time to next treatment or death (8.6 vs 7.5 months, P=.035) and overall survival (14.4 vs 11.7 months, P=.003) on F- versus G-based therapy. Among 126 G-pref patients, G-based therapy was associated with longer time to next treatment or death (9.6 vs 7.2 months, P=.038), but not significantly different overall survival.
ai_technology: Computational Histology Artificial Intelligence (CHAI) platform
organization: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; Valar Labs; Johns Hopkins University; University of Pittsburgh Medical Center; Pancreatic Cancer Action Network; University Health Network / Princess Margaret Cancer Centre

title: PlantRNA-FM identifies translation-associated RNA motifs and structure motifs in plants
summary: The PlantRNA-FM model, pretrained on sequence and predicted RNA structure from 1,124 plant transcriptomes, identified 5′-UTR motifs associated with translation efficiency across plant transcriptomes. Reporter assays in plants tested selected predictions: mutating a high-translation-associated RNA secondary-structure motif reduced measured translation efficiency by up to 5.3-fold, while disrupting a model-prioritized low-translation-associated RNA G-quadruplex motif increased it by up to 5.8-fold. The paper reports the rG4 motifs as translation-repressive, consistent with prior evidence on individual rG4s; the transcriptome-wide model prioritization and tested instances are the scoped findings here.
ai_technology: PlantRNA-FM, an interpretable RNA foundation model integrating RNA sequence and predicted structure
organization: Northeast Normal University; Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Exeter; John Innes Centre; Alan Turing Institute

title: Deep learning mines venom proteomes for antimicrobial peptides active in vitro and in a mouse infection model
summary: The APEX deep-learning model screened 16,123 venom proteins by generating and scoring 40,626,260 venom-encrypted peptides. After activity prediction and filtering for low similarity to known antimicrobial peptides, the authors selected 58 for experiments; 53 showed antimicrobial activity against at least one tested pathogen. Three selected peptides reduced bacterial counts after topical treatment in a mouse Acinetobacter baumannii skin-abscess model; the wolf-spider-derived Arachnoserver-5 peptide produced a reported three-log reduction versus untreated controls through day four, without significant body-weight change under the study conditions.
ai_technology: APEX deep-learning model for bacterial strain-specific minimum inhibitory concentration prediction
organization: University of Pennsylvania

title: CHANCE uses tumor genomes to prioritize non-cancer drugs with activity in patient-derived cancer cells
summary: CHANCE, a supervised machine-learning model integrating patient-specific coding and non-coding mutations with drug and protein-interaction information, screened 5,197 TCGA/ICGC tumors against 923 FDA-approved non-oncology drugs. For ex-vivo validation, the investigators sequenced tumor cells from seven patients with pancreatic or esophageal cancer and tested CHANCE-prioritized drugs; at least one predicted non-oncology drug showed anticancer activity in tumor cells from five of the seven patients. This is patient-specific cell-assay validation, not a treatment-response study in patients.
ai_technology: CHANCE, a supervised gradient-boosted-tree model integrating coding/non-coding variants, protein–protein interaction networks, drug targets and drug-response data
organization: Tianjin Medical University; collaborating Chinese cancer research and clinical institutions

title: AlphaCD maps experimentally measured catalytic properties across cytidine deaminases and supports a high-fidelity editor
summary: The researchers measured catalytic efficiency, editing windows, motif preferences and off-target activity for 1,100 APOBEC-like cytidine deaminases fused to nCas9 in HEK293T cells, then trained AlphaCD to predict these properties. They applied it to 21,335 UniProt deaminases and experimentally checked a 28-protein subsample. As an application, the team used AlphaCD to identify a high-efficiency deaminase and alanine scanning to produce the E100A variant, which retained editing activity while reducing off-target activity; cell experiments tested editing at endogenous loci and a PCSK9 splice site.
ai_technology: AlphaCD, a machine-learning model trained on sequence, predicted structure and related protein features
organization: Agricultural Genomics Institute at Shenzhen, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

title: Deep-learning design produced soluble analogues of membrane-protein folds with preserved binding functions
summary: A deep-learning pipeline based on inversion of AlphaFold2 and ProteinMPNN designed soluble proteins with claudin, rhomboid-protease and GPCR-like folds. Experiments reported stable, folded soluble designs and structural agreement with target folds. The researchers grafted functional motifs, including a ghrelin-receptor epitope that bound its antibody and active/inactive A2A-receptor-like designs that differed in mini-Gs binding; a binding-site knockout served as a control.
ai_technology: AF2seq deep-learning backbone design with ProteinMPNN sequence design
organization: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne; University at Buffalo; University of Washington; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: MIMaL predicts and experimentally validates five yeast gene functions from protein–metabolite profiles
summary: MIMaL used tree-based regression and SHAP interpretation on yeast proteome/metabolome measurements, then clustered protein-control profiles across single-gene knockouts. It predicted functions for five genes, with experimental validation reported for all five. Two previously uncharacterized genes, YJR120W and YDL157C, were predicted to modulate mitochondrial translation; functions were also predicted and validated for SDH9, ISC1 and FMP52. The study additionally validated previously unrecognized protein links to citrate.
ai_technology: MIMaL: ExtraTrees regression of metabolite abundance from proteomic profiles, SHAP interpretation, and UMAP/OPTICS clustering of protein-control profiles
organization: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; Medical College of Wisconsin; Stockholm University; University of Gothenburg

title: SIMMER-guided experiments identify gut bacterial strains that deplete methotrexate
summary: SIMMER combines reaction-chemistry and protein-sequence similarity to predict gut microbial species and enzymes responsible for drug biotransformations. For methotrexate (MTX), the model predicted candidate strains and enzyme sequences; researchers tested 42 gut bacterial isolates by HPLC. SIMMER predicted 13 isolates as MTX-metabolizing, and 10 of those tested isolates showed MTX depletion; the association was significant in the study (Fisher exact p=0.046). Predicted MTX-hydrolysis enzyme signatures were also enriched in stool samples of MTX nonresponders in an analyzed rheumatoid-arthritis cohort.
ai_technology: SIMMER, a computational reaction-similarity and protein-homology pipeline using chemical fingerprints, MetaCyc reactions and gut metagenomic sequences
organization: Gladstone Institutes; University of California, San Francisco; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub San Francisco

title: AlphaFold structure analysis helps reveal PHGDH transcriptional activity linked to Alzheimer’s amyloid pathology
summary: AlphaFold-based structural analysis highlighted a helix-helix-turn-helix subdomain in PHGDH that resembles a TALE homeodomain, prompting tests of a previously unrecognized DNA-binding and transcriptional function. Experiments supported PHGDH binding to promoters and activation of IKKα and HMGB1 in astrocytes, independently of its metabolic enzyme activity. In mouse models and human brain organoids, PHGDH expression promoted amyloid pathology; a blood-brain-barrier-permeable inhibitor of its transcriptional function reduced amyloid pathology and improved measured behavioral deficits in mice.
ai_technology: AlphaFold structure prediction, followed by structural comparison of the predicted PHGDH fold
organization: University of California San Diego; collaborating biomedical research institutions

title: iTARGEX analysis identifies ELG1 as a regulator of yeast transcription buffering and four protein-turnover regulators
summary: iTARGEX applied a mixture-regression model to gene-expression profiles from 1,484 single-gene deletion yeast mutants, associating transcriptomic changes with S-phase transcriptional buffering and global protein turnover. Experiments supported ELG1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of transcriptional buffering during S phase; the phenotype was reproduced in a second genetic background and rescued by a PCNA-D150E mutation. Follow-up protein-turnover measurements showed altered turnover in MRN1, UPF3, RAM1 and SSN3 deletion strains.
ai_technology: iTARGEX, a finite-mixture regression framework fitted by expectation maximization to single-gene-deletion transcriptomic data
organization: Academia Sinica, Taiwan

title: CAMIL regression predicts continuous homologous-recombination deficiency and tumor immune biomarkers from histology
summary: A self-supervised, attention-based deep-learning regression model predicted continuous homologous-recombination deficiency (HRD) scores and tumor-microenvironment biomarkers from H&E pathology slides. On TCGA internal validation, HRD classification AUROC exceeded 0.70 in five of seven cancer types; external CPTAC validation reached AUROC 0.81 for lung adenocarcinoma and 0.96 for endometrial cancer. In 2,297 colorectal-cancer patients in the DACHS cohort, continuous regression scores for leukocyte fraction and lymphocyte-infiltration-related signatures were independently prognostic in multivariable survival analysis.
ai_technology: CAMIL regression, a self-supervised contrastive-clustering and attention-based multiple-instance deep-learning model
organization: Technische Universität Dresden; University Hospital Dresden; collaborating clinical and pathology institutions

title: An integrated Arabidopsis regulatory network predicts 13 previously unlinked reactive-oxygen-stress regulators
summary: Researchers integrated DNA-motif, chromatin-accessibility, TF-binding and expression evidence with supervised learning to build an Arabidopsis gene-regulatory network of 1,491 transcription factors and 1.7 million TF–target interactions. The network predicted candidate reactive-oxygen-species (ROS) regulators; loss- and gain-of-function phenotyping supported 13 regulators not previously linked to ROS or stress responses. Newly tested examples included WRKY55, WRKY47, AT2G33710 and AT5G57150. The paper also reports that 75% of its ROS-predicted TFs had ROS or physiological stress functions supported by either this study or prior evidence.
ai_technology: Supervised-learning integrated gene-regulatory network (iGRN) built from motif, open-chromatin, transcription-factor-binding and expression-based networks
organization: Ghent University; VIB Center for Plant Systems Biology; Bioinformatics Institute Ghent

title: Longitudinal EHR machine learning identifies patients who may need autoimmune rheumatic-disease evaluation years earlier
summary: A random-forest model trained on longitudinal electronic health records from 161,584 people across two institutions identified records associated with high-specificity autoantibody testing for systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs). The model achieved AUROC 0.93 in internal validation and 0.87 on the external All of Us cohort. In a separate BioMe cohort, model probabilities tracked SARD and other autoimmune diagnoses; records could predict later autoantibody testing and rheumatology encounters up to five years before those events. The study also found higher autoantibody yield among model-prioritized individuals than under the comparison clinical-testing rate.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning model using longitudinal electronic-health-record diagnoses, medications, laboratory results and vital signs
organization: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; University of Maryland School of Medicine; Hospital for Special Surgery

title: Deep learning detects elevated tissue-derived cfDNA across cancer and cirrhosis cohorts
summary: A study built a fragment-level methylation atlas from 521 noncancer tissue samples spanning 29 human tissue types and used it with cfSort, a supervised deep neural network, to estimate tissue composition in plasma cell-free DNA. Applying cfSort to patient data, the investigators found higher cfDNA fractions from the affected tissue in liver, lung, colorectal and stomach cancer and cirrhosis cohorts than in healthy controls; the estimated fractions also increased with cancer stage. The tissue-origin signal was reproduced on an independent whole-genome-bisulfite-sequencing dataset for liver cancer. In serial samples from four non-small-cell lung cancer patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, estimated liver or kidney tissue fractions tracked measured biochemical markers of organ injury.
ai_technology: cfSort, an ensemble of two dense deep neural networks trained on simulated mixtures using a fragment-level tissue methylation atlas
organization: University of California, Los Angeles; Stanford University; EarlyDiagnostics; University of Southern California; University of California, San Diego

title: EHR deep learning and sequencing identify two previously undiagnosed Noonan syndrome cases
summary: Investigators applied a deep-learning model to diagnosis text in the electronic health records of 92,428 pediatric patients. It flagged 171 patients above a prespecified Noonan syndrome risk threshold for chart review; genetic sequencing and specialist assessment identified two previously undiagnosed Noonan syndrome cases among evaluated patients, in addition to three patients diagnosed during the study period. The confirmed cases had pathogenic variants in Noonan-associated genes, including PTPN11 and LZTR1. This supplies real-world evidence that EHR-based model screening can surface rare-disease cases for clinical genetic evaluation.
ai_technology: Deep convolutional neural network trained on structured electronic-health-record diagnosis text to estimate Noonan syndrome risk
organization: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center; University of Cincinnati College of Medicine; University of Wisconsin–Madison

title: Machine learning identifies plasma protein signatures that predict onset of common and rare diseases
summary: Researchers used regularized machine-learning models to select sparse plasma-protein signatures for 10-year incidence across 218 diseases in 41,931 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project participants. Five to twenty proteins improved held-out risk prediction over basic clinical information for 67 diseases and over clinical information plus routine assays for 52. The study identified TNFRSF17 as a specific predictor for future multiple myeloma and TNFRSF13B for monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance. In bone-marrow single-cell data from 11 newly diagnosed myeloma patients and three controls, four of five myeloma predictor proteins were most highly expressed by plasma cells; FCRLB and QPCT elevation was attributable to malignant plasma cells. Proteomic signatures also replicated improved prediction for five of six diseases tested in EPIC-Norfolk.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection and regularized Cox machine-learning models integrating plasma proteomics and clinical covariates
organization: MRC Epidemiology Unit, University of Cambridge; Queen Mary University of London; University College London; GSK Research and Development; Berlin Institute of Health at Charité; EPIC-Norfolk

title: AstroREG maps functional enhancer–gene links in human astrocytes
summary: A CRISPRi and single-cell RNA-sequencing screen tested 979 candidate enhancers in cultured human primary astrocytes and identified 158 functional enhancer–gene pairs, including enhancers regulating genes implicated in Alzheimer disease. The study trained the EGrf random-forest model on the measured screen and used it to predict additional enhancer–gene regulatory interactions genome-wide; selected model-predicted interactions were then functionally assessed by CRISPRi and qRT–PCR.
ai_technology: EGrf random-forest enhancer–gene interaction model, trained on the AstroREG CRISPRi/single-cell RNA-sequencing screen
organization: University of New South Wales; University of Western Australia; Macquarie University; Monash University; University of Michigan

title: Single-cell imaging and machine learning reveal a Cdk2–COP9 interaction that induces a senescence-like immune state in Drosophila cells
summary: A synthetic genetic-interaction and cell-morphology map covering more than 6,800 Drosophila genes supported machine-learning-based gene-function assignments across 47 modules. In follow-up, Cytoclass single-cell classification revealed a state-specific interaction between Cdk2 and COP9 signalosome knockdown: co-depletion arrested cell-cycle progression and produced a senescence-like phenotype with increased antimicrobial-peptide expression in cultured cells and hemocytes, including without bacterial infection.
ai_technology: Single-cell morphology classifier ensemble and machine-learning analysis of genetic-interaction profiles (Cytoclass; support-vector machines and random forest)
organization: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ); Heidelberg University; University of Applied Sciences Bingen

title: Deep learning of salivary-gland biopsies identifies acinar CD8 T-cell infiltration associated with Sjögren disease
summary: A deep-learning model trained on digitized minor salivary-gland biopsy slides from five expert centres and externally validated at a sixth classified focus score and Sjögren disease in a retrospective cohort of 545 participants. Explainable-model analysis identified a histological pattern of CD8-positive T cells around acinar epithelial cells associated with Sjögren disease. External-validation AUROC was 0.89 for disease classification and 0.92 among patients negative for anti-SSA antibodies.
ai_technology: Deep-learning histopathology classifier with Shapley-value interpretation
organization: Scienta Lab; William Harvey Research Institute, Queen Mary University of London; University of Birmingham; National and Kapodistrian University of Athens; Newcastle University; Université Paris-Saclay; participating NECESSITY consortium centres

title: Deep-learning CT response score stratifies outcomes in lung-cancer immunotherapy cohorts
summary: A deep-learning radiomic pipeline generated a pretreatment CT response score (CTRS) for advanced non-small-cell lung cancer treated with PD-(L)1 checkpoint inhibitors. In an independent real-world test cohort, high-response-score first-line ICI-monotherapy patients had longer progression-free and overall survival after adjustment for baseline covariates including PD-L1 (adjusted HR 0.46 and 0.50). In a secondary analysis of 54 participants from a prospective sasanlimab trial, the score was associated with overall survival (adjusted HR 0.33) but not progression-free survival.
ai_technology: Three-dimensional hierarchical convolutional neural network feature extractor combined with a Cox survival model (CT response score, CTRS)
organization: Onc.AI; Pfizer; University of Pennsylvania; Moffitt Cancer Center

title: Machine learning identifies a high-risk diabetic cardiomyopathy phenotype linked to future heart failure
summary: Unsupervised clustering of 25 echocardiographic and biomarker variables in 1,199 ARIC participants with diabetes identified three phenogroups; the group with the greatest cardiac remodelling and neurohormonal-stress abnormalities had 12.1% five-year heart-failure incidence, versus 4.6% and 3.1% in the other groups. A deep-neural-network classifier trained to recognize this phenotype identified corresponding high-risk groups in the external CHS cohort (n=802) and UT Southwestern EHR cohort (n=5,071); phenotype classification was associated with incident heart failure in both.
ai_technology: Unsupervised hierarchical clustering and a deep neural network (DeepNN) classifier, with random forest variable-importance analysis
organization: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; Texas Heart Institute; Houston Methodist DeBakey Heart & Vascular Center; Duke University; National Heart Centre Singapore; University of Toronto; University of Colorado; Massachusetts General Hospital

title: Deep learning identifies externally replicated fast and slow cognitive-progressor groups in early Alzheimer dementia
summary: Deep learning clustered cognitive and functional trajectories in 283 people with early dementia probably due to Alzheimer disease into fast- and slow-progressing groups. The trajectory groups were externally validated and independently replicated in a 2,779-person dementia cohort. A classifier using cross-sectional data at diagnosis predicted progression group in external validation with AUC 0.70 ± 0.01.
ai_technology: Deep-learning clustering of longitudinal cognitive/functional trajectories, followed by machine-learning classification from cross-sectional diagnosis data
organization: Fraunhofer Institute for Algorithms and Scientific Computing (SCAI); University of Bonn; Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School; Boehringer Ingelheim

title: Deep-learning histopathology identifies tertiary lymphoid structure features linked to stage II colorectal cancer relapse
summary: SurvFinder analyzed 6,950 H&E slides from 1,604 stage II colorectal cancer patients across four cohorts and identified tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) as prognostic tissue features. Its multi-view model integrated TLS morphology and spatial location; explainable analysis highlighted TLS maturity and position near the tumor periphery as features associated with relapse-free survival and adjuvant-chemotherapy outcome patterns across the retrospective datasets.
ai_technology: SurvFinder, a multi-component deep-learning pipeline: WSINet for prognosis-associated tissue features, SegNet for TLS segmentation/subtyping, and MVNet for multi-view risk prediction
organization: Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; Sun Yat-sen University; Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital; Johns Hopkins University; Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center

title: Machine learning identifies new CYP2C9-inhibiting drugs and drug metabolites
summary: A structure-, dynamics- and physicochemical-feature machine-learning approach predicted CYP2C9 inhibition and experimentally identified four drugs—vatalanib, piriqualone, ticagrelor and cloperidone—as strong inhibitors, plus sertindole, asapiprant, duvelisib and dasatinib as moderate inhibitors in reported assays. Vatalanib had a reported CYP2C9 inhibition IC50 of 0.067 μM. Separate metabolism assays characterized CYP2C9-produced metabolites for abemaciclib, cloperidone, vatalanib and tarafenacin.
ai_technology: Machine-learning inhibitor predictors combining CYP2C9 structural/dynamics information with inhibitor physicochemical properties
organization: INSERM; CNRS and Université de Paris; Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers; Université de Lorraine; Nantes Université

title: Deep learning enables multi-site bone marrow adiposity genetics in UK Biobank
summary: Deep learning measured bone marrow fat fraction at four skeletal sites in UK Biobank MRI data; after quality control, 48,608 participants contributed to genome-wide analyses. In the white-participant meta-GWAS, the study reported 67, 147, 134 and 174 independent significant variants for femoral head, total hip, femoral diaphysis and spine, mapping to 54, 90, 43 and 100 genes, respectively. Analyses also identified site- and sex-specific genetic associations and added signals in multi-ancestry analyses.
ai_technology: Previously validated deep-learning models for MRI segmentation and bone marrow fat-fraction measurement
organization: University of Edinburgh; University of Lille; Heriot-Watt University; University of Southern Denmark; University of Dundee; University of Southern Denmark and collaborating UK Biobank institutions

title: Deep learning maps previously unknown disease signals in ECGs across two health systems
summary: Researchers independently trained PheWASNet on ECG and electronic health-record data from Stanford Health Care and Cedars-Sinai to assess 1,243 disease phenotypes. In held-out patient splits at both centers, the study reported previously unrecognized ECG associations for disorders including respiratory failure, neutropenia and menstrual disorders (AUCs 0.86, 0.83 and 0.84 at Stanford, respectively). Cross-condition model-output analysis found that 35 of 37 strongly detectable non-cardiac phenotypes shared signals with only four other disease outputs, and simple ECG measurement models explained some findings.
ai_technology: PheWASNet, a multi-task deep-learning model based on a one-dimensional EfficientNet architecture
organization: Stanford University; Cedars-Sinai Medical Center; University of California, Los Angeles

title: Machine learning finds plasma protein signals up to 14 years before Parkinson diagnosis
summary: Using UK Biobank measurements of 2,937 plasma proteins, researchers found 446 dysregulated proteins in incident Parkinson cases and used machine learning to select a 23-protein panel for prediction. The panel achieved test AUCs of 0.78 in incident and 0.795 in prevalent cases; nine selected proteins were already dysregulated 10–14 years before diagnosis. In a separate Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative cohort, a 16-protein subset shared between platforms achieved validation AUC up to 0.76.
ai_technology: Support vector machine and other machine-learning models, with recursive feature elimination for panel selection
organization: Johnson & Johnson; UK Biobank; Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative collaborators

title: Machine learning and tear-fluid proteomics identify a six-protein ALS signature
summary: In discovery samples from 49 people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and 54 controls, mass spectrometry detected 876 tear-fluid proteins, of which 106 differed in abundance. Biostatistical and machine-learning analyses produced a six-protein signature (CRYM, PFKL, CAPZA2, ALDH16A1, SERPINC1 and HP). In an independent cohort of 51 ALS cases and 52 controls, Western blots replicated significant group differences for SERPINC1 and HP; their combination had the best reported in-silico discrimination.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models applied to data-independent acquisition mass-spectrometry proteomics and biomarker-panel discrimination
organization: Technical University of Munich; Helmholtz Munich; Ludwig-Maximilians University of Munich; University of Melbourne; University Medical Center Göttingen; Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences; German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases

title: Machine learning identifies serum protein signatures for progression from asymptomatic atherosclerosis to ischemic stroke
summary: In a discovery cohort of 43 patients with asymptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis and a validation cohort of 39, investigators combined serum proteomics with machine learning to distinguish acute ischemic stroke from large-artery atherosclerosis. XGBoost selected a three-protein panel (RNASE4, HBA1 and ATF6B; reported AUC 0.917, specificity 80%) and a six-protein panel distinguishing patients from healthy controls (reported AUC 0.971, specificity 86%). ELISA assays confirmed higher GUCA2A and FLNA in patient groups.
ai_technology: XGBoost machine-learning models applied to serum proteomics; DeepPRM-Stellar targeted mass spectrometry supported peptide validation and panel optimization
organization: Huashan Hospital, Fudan University; Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University; Xiamen University; Xiang An Biomedicine Laboratory

title: MP4 text-to-protein design yields ATP-active proteins, including one with a novel fold
summary: The transformer MP4 maps plain-language prompts to protein sequences. The study reports two experimentally validated de novo designs that were expressible and thermostable and showed ATP binding and hydrolysis in vitro. X-ray structures at 1.30 Å and 1.77 Å showed that one design adopts a fold not previously observed in the authors’ structural comparisons.
ai_technology: MP4, a transformer-based text-to-protein model
organization: 310 AI; University of California, Berkeley; McGill University; Arctoris

title: A graph neural network nominates OSM–OSMR for melanoma immunotherapy, with ex-vivo explant evidence
summary: MIDAS, a multimodal graph-neural-network model, ranked candidate immuno-oncology targets from gene-interaction, patient multi-omic and immune-biology data. In eight stage III/IV melanoma patient-derived explants, researchers blocked OSM–OSMR signalling with an anti-OSM antibody. The paper reports reduced dysfunctional CD8+ T-cell populations and lower CCL4 levels; PTPN22 inhibition did not produce comparable changes in this assay.
ai_technology: MIDAS, a multimodal graph neural network for immuno-oncology target ranking
organization: University College London; The Francis Crick Institute; Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust; University College London Hospitals; Royal Holloway, University of London

title: Machine-learning metabolomics identifies DHEAS and citrate signatures in anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis
summary: In a single-centre cohort of 183 patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathy and 104 healthy controls, seven machine-learning classifiers and LASSO feature selection were used with plasma and PBMC metabolomics to distinguish anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis. DHEAS and citrate were selected across the integrated analyses; plasma assays showed lower levels in anti-MDA5-positive cases, with concordant patterns reported in a separate 33-patient/33-control validation cohort. Within cases, DHEAS correlated inversely with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease and citrate with rash.
ai_technology: Seven machine-learning classifiers (including random forest and XGBoost) with LASSO feature selection
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University

title: Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes succinate in sepsis-associated encephalopathy
summary: In plasma samples from 29 controls, 32 sepsis patients and 27 patients with sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), LC–MS/MS plus machine-learning feature selection identified a 12-metabolite profile. Succinate rose stepwise from controls to sepsis to SAE, ranked among the five leading XGBoost features, and correlated with APACHE II, SOFA and lactate. In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.
ai_technology: Random forest and support-vector-machine feature ranking with XGBoost classification
organization: Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology

title: Machine learning and Mendelian randomization prioritize CA2 as a diabetic nephropathy biomarker
summary: Across six kidney-expression datasets, researchers identified 314 differentially expressed genes in diabetic nephropathy and used LASSO, SVM-RFE and random forest to prioritize seven candidate genes. Mendelian-randomization integration further prioritized carbonic anhydrase II (CA2); its ROC AUC exceeded 0.878 across the analyzed datasets. The authors also reported qPCR validation of CA2 in clinical patient and control samples and an association with inferred immune-cell infiltration.
ai_technology: LASSO, support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination and random-forest feature selection
organization: Shanghai Tenth People’s Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine; Yangpu Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine

title: Machine learning prioritizes 1-methylnicotinamide as a serum signal across HBV cirrhosis-to-HCC progression
summary: Untargeted serum metabolomics from 69 participants, including eight patients followed from HBV-related cirrhosis to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), was analyzed with LASSO and random forest to prioritize metabolites. 1-methylnicotinamide (1-MNAM) declined across healthy, cirrhosis and HCC groups and was lower at the HCC than cirrhosis stage in the eight progressors. Targeted mass spectrometry in a separate cohort of 25 healthy controls and 25 early-stage HCC patients confirmed lower 1-MNAM in HCC (AUC 0.954 for HCC versus healthy controls).
ai_technology: LASSO regression and random forest classifier applied to serum metabolomics
organization: Centre for Medical Research, Ningbo No. 2 Hospital; Liver Disease Department of Integrative Medicine, Ningbo No. 2 Hospital

title: Multi-omics machine learning identifies lysophosphatidic acid in PRRSV infection and links it to immune suppression
summary: Machine-learning analysis of untargeted serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles from clinical pig cohorts identified lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) as a PRRSV-associated biomarker. Follow-up infection experiments reported increased LPA with autotaxin upregulation; in porcine alveolar macrophages, LPA manipulation altered RIG-I/type-I-interferon responses and viral replication. In infected pigs, targeting LPA was reported to protect against infection and associated disease outcomes.
ai_technology: Random-forest analysis of serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles
organization: Sun Yat-sen University; Huazhong Agricultural University; Wen’s Foodstuff Group Co. Ltd.; Stanford University

title: Machine-learning metabolomics distinguishes SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and RSV from respiratory swabs
summary: Untargeted metabolomics and machine learning identified upper-respiratory-swab signatures for SARS-CoV-2 positivity, followed by targeted LC-MS/MS profiling. Across 1,226 samples (521 SARS-CoV-2-positive, 97 influenza A, 96 RSV, 211 other respiratory viruses and 301 virus-negative), the best SARS-CoV-2 LightGBM model had AUC 0.99, sensitivity 0.96 and specificity 0.95. Separate models reported AUC 0.97 for influenza A and 0.99 for RSV. The top-ranked SARS-CoV-2 features included 3-oxo-heneicosanoic acid and 2-(4-hydroxyphenyl) ethanol.
ai_technology: Light Gradient Boosting Machine and other machine-learning classifiers applied to mass-spectrometry metabolomics
organization: British Columbia Centre for Disease Control Public Health Laboratory; University of British Columbia; Stanford University School of Medicine; Stanford Health Care; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub

title: Multi-omics machine learning prioritizes a plasma lipid signature for active tuberculosis differentiation
summary: Machine-learning integration of plasma functional-omics data in two discovery cohorts and a validation cohort identified biosignatures that distinguished active tuberculosis from nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, latent TB infection and other lung diseases. Cohorts included 76 people in the TB–NTM discovery set, 72 in the TB–LTBI–other-lung-disease set, and 68 TB plus 30 LTBI participants in the validation set. PC(14:0_22:6) was the most important predictor and was lower in active TB; additional external datasets yielded reported AUCs of 0.77–1.00.
ai_technology: Multi-omics integration and machine-learning predictive models for feature selection and classification
organization: Inje University College of Medicine; Ton Duc Thang University; Hanoi University of Pharmacy; University of Copenhagen; Korea University Guro Hospital

title: TriSCOPE links cell-type-specific Alzheimer’s expression programs to inherited risk loci
summary: TriSCOPE combined cell-level predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression and pseudotime analysis across six single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets (about 4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors). It identified cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that were often missed by univariate differential-expression analysis; conditional GWAS–eQTL colocalization supported 27 gene–cell-type pairs at Alzheimer’s risk loci, including pairs without significant differential expression. Selected gene signals and analytical branches were compared across independent cohorts.
ai_technology: TriSCOPE, using LightGBM-based multivariate predictive modeling integrated with differential expression and pseudotime analysis
organization: Harvard Medical School; Harvard College; New York Genome Center; Rush Alzheimer’s Disease Center, Rush University

title: Spatial glycan imaging and machine learning identify a serum N-glycan panel for HCC in cirrhosis
summary: Spatial N-glycan imaging of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissue and paired serum identified thirteen altered glycan structures; glycoproteomics linked them to more than 50 proteins, and sixteen glycoproteins were assessed in a separate patient set. Machine-learning algorithms combining glycan/glycoprotein features with clinical variables differentiated early-stage HCC from cirrhosis in a case-control cohort of 100 HCC and 101 cirrhosis-only patients, with reported AUROC values across the algorithms of 0.88–0.97.
ai_technology: Machine-learning algorithms using serum N-glycan and glycoprotein features, age, sex and AFP
organization: Medical University of South Carolina; GlycoPath, Inc.; HTX Technologies; University of California San Diego; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

title: Multimodal AI distinguishes ten dementia etiologies across nine clinical datasets
summary: A multimodal AI model analyzed demographics, personal and family history, medications, cognitive and functional testing, and neuroimaging across nine datasets totaling 51,269 participants. It assigned probabilities to ten primary or contributing dementia etiologies and addressed mixed cases. The paper reports microaveraged AUROC 0.96 for dementia-etiology differentiation; model probabilities aligned with etiology-specific biomarkers and postmortem pathology. In a review of 100 cases, AI-augmented neurologist assessment outperformed neurologist-only ratings.
ai_technology: Multimodal machine-learning model combining clinical, neuropsychological, functional and neuroimaging data
organization: Boston University; Stanford University; Peking Union Medical College Hospital; Columbia University Irving Medical Center; University of Nebraska Medical Center; additional clinical and research centers contributing cohorts

title: Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes serum metabolites for SLE diagnosis and activity assessment
summary: Targeted serum metabolomics compared 89 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and 44 healthy participants, identifying 146 differential metabolites. The authors combined statistical screening with seven machine-learning models to prioritize eight diagnostic biomarker candidates (reported AUCs above 0.95). Two additional metabolites, N-methyl-L-glutamic acid and L-2-aminobutyric acid, were evaluated by ELISA in a 90-patient SLE validation cohort and associated with SLE Disease Activity Index scores.
ai_technology: Seven machine-learning classification models applied to targeted serum metabolomics
organization: The Affiliated Guangzhou Panyu Central Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University; Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine; Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University; Panyu District Central Hospital

title: EHR machine learning and genetic colocalization link osteoporosis to female Alzheimer’s risk near MS4A6A
summary: Random-forest models trained on UCSF records (749 expert-diagnosed Alzheimer’s disease cases and 250,545 controls) identified clinical features predictive up to seven years before the recorded onset; the seven-year model’s AUROC was 0.72 using clinical features alone. Matched-cohort follow-up in external University of California health-system records found faster Alzheimer’s diagnosis after osteoporosis in women. Genetic colocalization analyses supported a female-specific shared signal between Alzheimer’s disease, low heel bone mineral density and MS4A6A expression near the MS4A gene cluster. The paper also reports shared APOE-locus support for hyperlipidemia and Alzheimer’s disease.
ai_technology: Random-forest models on longitudinal electronic health records, interpreted with the SPOKE biomedical knowledge network
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Stanford University; University of California health-system collaborators; University of Oxford

title: Machine-learning proteomics identifies a replicated plasma signature associated with Alzheimer’s disease
summary: A three-stage analysis of plasma proteomics from 1,270 people with clinical Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and 2,096 cognitively normal controls identified 416 proteins associated with clinical AD, including 294 that the paper classified as not previously associated with AD in large-scale plasma or CSF proteomic studies. A LASSO-selected seven-protein model predicted clinical AD and biomarker-defined AD status, with validation in external cohorts and orthogonal assays; the signature also stratified later progression to symptomatic AD among initially cognitively normal participants.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection with logistic regression, using five-fold cross-validation and age/sex covariates
organization: Washington University School of Medicine; and Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center; Stanford Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center; Rush Alzheimer’s Disease Center; Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium; collaborating Alzheimer research centers

title: Deep learning identifies previously unreported protein interactions in human bacterial pathogens
summary: A RoseTTAFold2-Lite pipeline combined residue coevolution, deep-learning complex prediction and AlphaFold modelling to screen protein pairs across 19 human bacterial pathogens. In a validation set selected using the deep-learning pipeline, co-immunoprecipitation detected four of six predicted interactions. Three pairs lacked prior direct interaction evidence: E. coli UbiE–YcaR, P. aeruginosa PA4105–PA4106, and P. aeruginosa WbpG–HisF2. The PA4105–PA4106 structural similarity to proteins in 3-thiaglutamate biosynthesis and the WbpG–HisF2 result provide functional hypotheses, not established native-pathogen mechanisms.
ai_technology: RoseTTAFold2-Lite integrated with direct coupling analysis and AlphaFold complex modelling
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; Broad Institute; Massachusetts General Hospital; University of Connecticut; Seoul National University; collaborating institutions

title: Machine learning identifies plasma metabolite panels for gastric-cancer diagnosis and prognosis
summary: In a multicenter study of 702 participants, targeted plasma metabolomics and machine learning produced a 10-metabolite gastric-cancer diagnostic model and separate 28-metabolite survival-risk model. The diagnostic model was evaluated in an independent 95-person cohort (AUROC 0.920; sensitivity 0.905, specificity 0.75) and detected stage IA disease with AUROC 0.909. Among 181 patients followed for a median 40 months, the prognostic model achieved test-set concordance index 0.83. Succinate, uridine and lactate were among diagnostic features.
ai_technology: LASSO, random forest and random survival forest
organization: Tsinghua University; National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer, China; Harbin Medical University Cancer Hospital; collaborating Chinese cancer centers

title: Machine-learning selection and external mass-spectrometry testing identify an ARDS 28-day prognosis protein panel
summary: A multicenter observational serum multi-omics study used LASSO and Boruta to select candidate biomarkers for 28-day outcome in acute respiratory distress syndrome. Eight proteins (VCAM1, LDHB, MSN, FLG2, TAGLN2, LMNA, MBL2 and LBP) showed consistency in an independent cohort of 183 patients and were confirmed by targeted parallel-reaction-monitoring mass spectrometry. The protein model AUC was 0.802 in validation versus 0.738 for the clinical model. The discovery analysis also reported sphingosine-1-phosphate association with ARDS prognosis and an enriched sphingolipid pathway.
ai_technology: LASSO and Boruta feature selection; machine-learning prognostic model; targeted PRM validation
organization: Fudan University; Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine; collaborating Shanghai hospitals

title: Integrated radiogenomic machine learning predicts neoadjuvant chemotherapy response in metastatic ovarian cancer
summary: The IRON ensemble combined baseline clinical data, CA-125, ctDNA and CT radiomics from primary and metastatic lesions to estimate tumor-volume change during neoadjuvant chemotherapy for high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma. In an independent 42-patient Barts cohort, the integrated model achieved AUC 0.78 for RECIST 1.1 response classification versus 0.47 for a clinical-only model; radiomics-containing scores significantly correlated with volume change in internal holdout. The study also measured spatial heterogeneity, with omental lesions showing better response than pelvic/ovarian disease.
ai_technology: IRON ensemble combining elastic net, support-vector regression and random forest
organization: University of Cambridge; and Cambridge University Hospitals; Barts Health NHS Trust; Medical University of Vienna; collaborating institutions

title: Elastic-net proteomic risk modeling and multi-cohort validation identify proteins associated with incident diabetes
summary: An untargeted analysis of 4,955 plasma proteins in the ARIC cohort identified 140 associations with incident diabetes; 64 were significant in an internal sample and 47 (including 22 reported as novel) were associated in the external Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort. Elastic-net Cox modeling selected a 27-protein panel for 20-year risk prediction. In internal validation, adding those proteins to conventional risk factors including fasting glucose and HbA1c increased the C statistic from 0.720 to 0.731. Genetic-instrument analyses supported possible causal roles for SHBG, ATP1B2 and GSTA1, although ATP1B2’s genetic and observational directions differed.
ai_technology: Elastic-net Cox regression for protein feature selection and incident-diabetes risk prediction
organization: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health; Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study centers; National University of Singapore; New York University Grossman School of Medicine; collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning models identify cerebrospinal-fluid protein signatures for multiple-sclerosis activity and disability progression
summary: Using Olink proteomics of 1,463 proteins in CSF and plasma from two prospective Swedish cohorts, the study trained prediction models for multiple-sclerosis diagnosis, 2-year disease activity and long-term disability worsening. Lower CSF neurofilament light (NfL) predicted absence of disease activity at two years (replication AUC 0.77). A stepwise model using 11 CSF proteins (CXCL13, LTA, FCN2, ICAM3, LY9, SLAMF7, TYMP, CHI3L1, FYB1, TNFRSF1B and NfL) predicted normalized age-related MS severity; subgroup classification AUCs in the replication cohort ranged from 0.88 to 0.90.
ai_technology: Stepwise logistic regression for diagnosis and disease activity; stepwise linear regression for long-term disability severity
organization: Linköping University; University of Skövde; Karolinska Institutet and Karolinska University Hospital; collaborating Swedish institutions

title: Unsupervised clustering identifies three blood immune endophenotypes associated with distinct multiple-sclerosis trajectories
summary: In two multicenter longitudinal cohorts of early multiple sclerosis (discovery n=309; validation n=232), unsupervised clustering of high-dimensional flow-cytometry and serum-proteomics profiles identified three peripheral-blood immune endophenotypes. Follow-up associated the groups with different trajectories of inflammation versus early structural damage. In the endophenotype-3 subgroup, patients subsequently treated with interferon beta had higher four-year progression and MRI activity than patients receiving other therapies.
ai_technology: Unsupervised clustering of high-dimensional flow-cytometry and serum-proteomics profiles (the reviewed abstract does not name the clustering algorithm)
organization: University of Münster; German Competence Network Multiple Sclerosis; Max Delbrück Center; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; collaborating German and international centers

title: LightGBM feature selection identifies a four-protein panel associated with incident chronic kidney disease
summary: In a prospective UK Biobank cohort of 27,429 participants without baseline chronic kidney disease, the study evaluated 2,920 plasma proteins and found 205 associated with incident CKD after protein-wide Cox regression with Bonferroni correction. LASSO reduced these to 23 candidates and LightGBM feature selection identified EDA2R, GDF15, HAVCR1 and SCARB2 as a four-protein panel. The protein panel alone had an AUC of 0.796 versus 0.805 for demographic variables; adding the proteins to the demographic model raised AUC to 0.830 in the study data.
ai_technology: Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) feature selection
organization: Nanjing Medical University, School of Public Health, Department of Epidemiology and Center for Global Health; UK Biobank

title: External validation reveals distinct plasma proteomic signatures across biopsy-proven primary glomerular diseases
summary: Profiling 5,416 plasma proteins in Korean cohorts, the study found distinct signatures across four biopsy-proven primary glomerular diseases. An elastic-net model using 93 proteins differentiated disease subtypes and controls in discovery and external validation cohorts. It achieved AUCs above 0.8 for minimal change disease, membranous nephropathy and IgA nephropathy; the model correctly classified 14 of 15 minimal-change cases and 20 of 32 IgA-nephropathy cases, but only 3 of 14 focal-segmental glomerulosclerosis cases. Functional analysis highlighted hemostasis-related proteins in minimal change disease.
ai_technology: Elastic-net-regularized logistic regression using plasma proteomic features
organization: Seoul National University College of Medicine; and Seoul National University Hospital; KORNERSTONE investigators; collaborating Korean hospitals

title: Machine-learning analysis separates genetic from environmental drivers of stimulated cytokine responses in healthy adults
summary: In 406 healthy GEOCODE cohort participants, whole-blood cytokine responses to Toll-like-receptor (TLR) and T-cell-receptor (TCR) stimulation varied across people, including high- and low-IL-6-response profiles associated with monocyte counts, sex and sampling season. Feature-importance analysis of machine-learning models found TCR-induced cytokine predictions were mainly driven by genetic features, whereas TLR-induced predictions were driven more by environmental and biological features. Combining genetic with biological and environmental data improved prediction by about 0.2 on average, and the reported findings were evaluated in the independent Milieu Intérieur cohort.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models including random forest, gradient-boosted trees, artificial neural networks and elastic net; random forest feature-importance analysis
organization: Université libre de Bruxelles; Hôpital Erasme; Milieu Intérieur cohort collaborators

title: Stability-based machine learning selects IL-8 and CCL3 as a two-protein serum signature for early silicosis
summary: A stability-based feature-selection workflow combining LASSO, random forest and SVM recursive feature elimination identified serum IL-8 and CCL3 as a two-protein signature distinguishing Stage I silicosis from controls. The study used a discovery cohort of 57 cases and 57 matched controls, then assessed the signature in an independent, unmatched cohort of 40 cases and 40 controls. The article reports validation AUC 0.973, specificity 95.0% and sensitivity 77.5%; both proteins were lower in silicosis cases.
ai_technology: Stability-based ensemble feature selection using LASSO, random forest and SVM recursive feature elimination, followed by logistic regression
organization: Nanjing Medical University; Jiangsu Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention; Southeast University; China University of Mining and Technology

title: Computer-vision and metabolomics fusion links paired serum–urine flux mismatch to early diabetic kidney disease
summary: In a two-center cohort of 364 participants with type 2 diabetes and controls, targeted serum/urine metabolite measurements found a high-serum/low-urine pattern for indoxyl sulfate and related metabolites in early diabetic kidney disease (DKD), consistent with reduced tubular secretion. Computer vision quantified urine foam stability and chromaticity; Random Forest recursive feature elimination selected these image features together with metabolite ratios and clinical variables for the FluxPro-DKD classifier. It distinguished DKD from diabetes without kidney disease with AUC 0.90 in discovery and 0.85 in a geographically distinct external cohort of 82.
ai_technology: Computer-vision urine phenotyping and Random Forest recursive feature elimination (RF-RFE) for multimodal feature selection
organization: Beijing University of Chinese Medicine; Dongfang Hospital; Third Affiliated Hospital of Beijing University of Chinese Medicine; Tianjin Institute of Nephropathy

title: SONAR identifies 3′UTR sequence features that raise T-cell receptor protein expression and CD8-cell killing
summary: The XGBoost-based SONAR pipeline modeled protein abundance from thousands of sequence features across human immune cells and cell lines, identifying cell-type- and activation-dependent regulatory patterns. Reporter assays found that CT-rich 3′UTR motifs increased protein output while AG-rich motifs were generally repressive. SONAR-informed synthetic 3′UTRs raised CDK4-specific T-cell-receptor protein without increasing its mRNA; engineered CD8+ T cells carrying the CT-rich constructs killed CDK4-expressing melanoma cells more effectively in a coculture assay.
ai_technology: SONAR, an XGBoost machine-learning pipeline using thousands of sequence features to predict protein abundance
organization: Sanquin Blood Supply Foundation; University of Amsterdam; Amsterdam UMC; Oncode Institute

title: Few-shot protein-language-model design yields high-output bicyclogermacrene synthase variants
summary: After experimentally screening activity-enhancing single mutants of LdTPS5, the researchers used PIFS-PLM, a few-shot model that selects features from protein-language-model embeddings using active-site and conserved-residue information, to propose mutation combinations. All 10 tested model-predicted combinations were active; nine produced more than 100 mg/L bicyclogermacrene in yeast, and the top variant produced 213.59 mg/L versus 2.93 mg/L for wild type (about 73-fold higher yield). A related selectivity-optimized combination increased bicyclogermacrene selectivity by 15%.
ai_technology: PIFS-PLM (Physics-Inspired Feature Selection of Protein Language Models), using ESM-2 embeddings with a few-shot mutation-combination classifier
organization: Tsinghua University; Tianjin University; Inner Mongolia University; Zhejiang Institute of Tianjin University

title: Tree-based machine learning nominates Parabacteroides merdae and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine as ulcerative-colitis alleviators in a mouse model
summary: The researchers combined personalized gut-microbiome community metabolic models from human iHMP data with tree-based machine-learning feature selection to identify microbial strains and metabolites associated with ulcerative-colitis samples. Parabacteroides merdae ATCC 43,184 and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine were among the most predictive features; the strain was also the main modeled microbial contributor to the metabolite. In a DSS-induced mouse colitis experiment, oral administration of the bacterium or metabolite improved reported colitis measures.
ai_technology: Tree-based supervised classifiers including random forest, gradient-boosted regression trees, XGBoost, XGBoost-random forest and LightGBM, combined with individualized genome-scale microbiome community models
organization: Jiangnan University; Wuxi Translational Medicine Research Center; Jiangsu Translational Medicine Research Institute Wuxi Branch; Wuxi People’s Hospital

title: XGBoost-guided splice switching identifies NEDD4L exon 13 as a TNBC cell vulnerability
summary: SpliceCore’s XGBoost models used splicing-factor RNA-binding and spliceosome information to nominate NEDD4L exon 13 (NEDD4Le13) and the SSO-0205 binding site. In triple-negative breast-cancer MDA-MB-231 cells, SSO-0205 increased exon inclusion (67% versus 15% control), reduced proliferation and decreased migration by 40–50%; the effects were not observed in the non-tumorigenic MCF10A comparator under the reported assays.
ai_technology: SpliceCore XGBoost models with SHAP and out-of-bag feature analysis
organization: Envisagenics, Inc.

title: Machine-learning multi-omics links gut metabolites to GPCR targets and tau changes in Alzheimer’s patient-derived neurons
summary: A machine-learning and multi-omics framework screened 1.09 million pairs across 408 human GPCRs and 335 gut microbial metabolites. It prioritized orphan receptor GPR84 and the metabolite triacanthine, which activated GPR84 in a cell assay. In Alzheimer’s patient-derived iPSC neurons, agmatine reduced C3AR and tau markers, while phenethylamine reduced phosphorylated and total tau in the reported experiments.
ai_technology: Extra Trees machine-learning model integrated with molecular docking, multi-omics and Mendelian-randomization analyses
organization: Cleveland Clinic; Case Western Reserve University; Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research; Tel Aviv University and collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning selection identifies a six-metabolite signature for one-year cardiovascular events after PCI in type 2 diabetes
summary: VSURF feature selection prioritized six serum metabolites—ADPR, 1-methylnicotinamide, D-ribose 5-phosphate, nicotinamide, L-tryptophan and phosphatidylcholine PC(36:2)—for one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) after PCI in patients with type 2 diabetes. Random-forest and XGBoost models were tested in a nested case-control study and an independent prospective cohort of 301 patients; in the external cohort, reported AUCs were 0.92 and 0.94 for MACEs, respectively. The study also linked NAD+ biosynthesis perturbation to altered bioenergetics, inflammation and proliferation in high-glucose-cultured human aortic smooth-muscle cells.
ai_technology: VSURF random-forest variable selection; random forest and XGBoost classifiers
organization: The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University; Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University

title: Machine learning prioritizes a protective Arabidopsis leaf fungus that suppresses oomycete infection
summary: Four classifiers (random forest, support-vector machine, logistic regression and multilayer perceptron) used six years of natural Arabidopsis leaf-microbiome data to prioritize taxa associated with Albugo infection status. Follow-up plant assays found that selected health-associated microbes reduced infection; Cystofilobasidium macerans OTU126 gave the strongest individual protection, reducing Albugo infection by an average of 73%. In a 15-member synthetic leaf community, adding this fungus increased the reported infection reduction to 40.25%, compared with 19.36% for the community alone.
ai_technology: Random forest, support-vector machine, logistic regression and multilayer perceptron classifiers with cross-validated feature selection
organization: University of Tübingen; Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1 and collaborating institutions

title: Machine learning identifies bacterial strains and combinations that reduce pathogen colonization in Arabidopsis
summary: Random forest and elastic-net models analyzed 136 synthetic communities, each composed of five bacterial strains, and identified strain identity as the strongest predictor of protection against Pseudomonas syringae DC3000 in Arabidopsis. Independent test communities confirmed predictive performance, and follow-up plant assays showed that Acidovorax Leaf76, Rhizobium Leaf68 and Pseudomonas Leaf15 each reduced pathogen colonization by about two orders of magnitude versus axenic controls; a Rhizobium Leaf371–Arthrobacter Leaf337 combination also reduced colonization.
ai_technology: Random forest and elastic-net generalized linear models (GLMNet)
organization: ETH Zurich; Institute of Microbiology

title: Machine-learning-guided PBMC proteomics identifies SLE diagnosis and activity biomarker panels
summary: A random-forest and OPLS-DA prioritization pipeline applied to peripheral-blood mononuclear-cell proteomics identified candidate protein combinations for distinguishing systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) from healthy and rheumatoid-arthritis controls and for separating active from inactive SLE. ELISA in a separate 80-person cohort supported a six-protein diagnosis panel (IFIT3, MX1, TOMM40, STAT1, STAT2 and OAS3; AUC 0.723 versus healthy controls and 0.815 versus rheumatoid arthritis) and a nine-protein activity panel (AUC 0.990). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis mapped several associated interferon-signature proteins to specific immune-cell populations.
ai_technology: POC-SLE: random-forest feature ranking with 1,000 bootstrap iterations, combined with OPLS-DA variable-importance selection
organization: Jinan University; Shenzhen People’s Hospital; collaborating institutions

title: Integrated proteomics and metabolomics with LASSO nominate a four-analyte early IgA-nephropathy plasma panel
summary: A study of biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy (IgAN) integrated plasma proteomics and untargeted metabolomics and used LASSO logistic regression to select PRKAR2A, IL6ST, SOS1 and palmitoleic acid as candidate discriminators from healthy controls. The panel had AUC 0.994 in the training set and 0.977 in the test split; ELISA assays in a separate 9-case/10-control sample set yielded an AUC of 0.91. Proteomic and metabolomic analyses also indicated complement/immune activation and altered energy and amino-acid metabolism in the studied cases.
ai_technology: LASSO logistic regression (glmnet), with tenfold cross-validation and additional random-forest/SVM model checks
organization: Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital; and collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning proteomics prioritizes four plasma markers associated with ankylosing-spondylitis activity
summary: A plasma-proteomics study of 48 active ankylosing-spondylitis (AS) patients, 21 stable-stage patients and 35 healthy controls combined random-forest and OPLS-DA scores to prioritize candidate markers. SAA1, FERMT3, ILK and TLN1 were elevated in active-stage AS and returned toward control levels in stable-stage patients; ELISA in a separate cohort (27 active, 28 stable, 24 controls) reproduced these patterns. A combined ELISA model distinguished active AS from healthy controls with AUC 0.932. FERMT3, ILK and TLN1 are integrin-pathway proteins.
ai_technology: Machine-learning biomarker scoring matrix combining random forest and OPLS-DA
organization: Guang’anmen Hospital, China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences; Beijing Institute of Lifeomics; collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning-guided electrochemical screening isolates five new reaction products
summary: A machine-learning-guided, chemist-in-the-loop screen predicted electrochemical reactivity for 38,865 potential partners with 1,4-dicyanobenzene (DCB). Automated tests of 20 prioritized, previously untested partners yielded DCB conversion in 16; five produced an isolable major product judged of synthetic or mechanistic interest. The reported examples include a silyl-enol-ether coupling and electrochemical benzylic arylation of benzyltrimethylsilane with DCB, plus three mechanistically unexpected products.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-guided reaction-competency classifier using a DFT-informed molecular representation
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning-guided photoredox design experimentally enables three transformations
summary: A workflow combining a variational-autoencoder latent space of 11,069 literature photoredox reactions with random-forest catalyst/reagent recommendations was used to propose three transformations. Experiments synthesized a previously inaccessible substituted dihydroquinolinone 43 using fac-Ir(ppy)3, a related oxidative cross-coupling product 46 in 64% yield, and heterocycle product 49 in 74% yield. The paper presents these as experimentally validated transformations identified through model-assisted precedent retrieval and condition selection.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder for reaction-space navigation and random-forest multilabel catalyst/reagent recommendation
organization: Wuhan University; HOURS Inc.; collaborating institutions

title: Cross-tissue machine learning prioritizes a 13-gene rheumatoid-arthritis activity score
summary: A machine-learning feature-selection pipeline integrated public whole-blood (1,885 samples) and synovial-tissue (284 samples) transcriptomic datasets and selected a 13-gene rheumatoid-arthritis score. Across five independent transcriptomic datasets, the score tracked DAS28 disease activity, distinguished rheumatoid arthritis from osteoarthritis, separated polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis from healthy controls, and was associated with treatment effects. In an independent immunoblot cohort, two of six tested proteins, TNFAIP6/TSG-6 and HSP90AB1/HSP90, were confirmed.
ai_technology: Cross-tissue machine-learning feature-selection pipeline for transcriptomic data
organization: University of California, San Francisco; Oregon Health & Science University

title: Random-forest metabolite profiling reduces false-positive newborn screens for four inherited disorders
summary: A 121-analyte LC–MS/MS panel combined established markers, untargeted-metabolomics features and chromatographically resolved isobars with random-forest classification of California newborn-screen dried blood spots. In 883 archived infant samples, the study reports that the second-tier approach maintained 100% sensitivity while reducing false positives by 83% for glutaric acidemia type I, 84% for methylmalonic acidemia, 100% for ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency and 51% for very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. Several long-chain acylcarnitine and hydroxy-acylcarnitine isobar features contributed to classification, although their chemical identities were unresolved.
ai_technology: Random Forest classifier trained on targeted LC–MS/MS metabolite profiles
organization: Stanford Health Care; Yale University; California Department of Public Health

title: 3D-HiChAT predicts embryonic enhancer hubs validated by CRISPR interference
summary: A random-forest model integrating ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq and HiChIP data predicted enhancer effects across mouse trophoblast stem cells, embryonic stem cells and extraembryonic endoderm cells. CRISPRi tests supported a shared Enh14 hub regulating both Tfcp2l1 and Gli2 in embryonic stem cells, and an Enh4 hub linked to seven genes in extraembryonic endoderm; four of those seven showed expression reductions as predicted. Across 40 tested enhancer-promoter pairs, experiments yielded 12 true positives and 13 true negatives, with overall prediction accuracy 0.71.
ai_technology: 3D-HiChAT, an optimized Random Forest model combining chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac and 3D HiChIP connectivity features
organization: Weill Cornell Medicine; New York Genome Center; collaborating institutions

title: CellOracle-guided zebrafish perturbations identify axial-mesoderm effects of noto and lhx1a loss
summary: The CellOracle machine-learning workflow used single-cell gene-regulatory networks to prioritize transcription factors for perturbation in zebrafish development. CRISPR/Cas9 tests confirmed a model-predicted, previously unreported increase in prechordal-plate differentiation after loss of noto, alongside the known loss of notochord. Model-prioritized lhx1a loss also inhibited axial-mesoderm differentiation: single-cell RNA-seq found expansion of early notochord cells and reductions in later notochord and prechordal-plate populations; orthogonal RNA assays supported reduced notochord/prechordal markers.
ai_technology: CellOracle, a machine-learning gene-regulatory-network model with in-silico transcription-factor perturbation
organization: Washington University in St. Louis; collaborating institutions

title: AcRanker-guided discovery of AcrIIA20 and AcrIIA21 anti-CRISPR proteins
summary: AcRanker, an XGBoost ranking model using amino-acid sequence features, ranked proteins from prophage regions in self-targeting Streptococcus genomes. Experimental testing identified two previously unknown type II-A anti-CRISPRs: AcrIIA20 (ML1), which strongly inhibited Streptococcus iniae Cas9 and weakly inhibited S. pyogenes Cas9, and AcrIIA21 (ML8), which inhibited S. pyogenes, S. aureus and S. iniae Cas9 with lower potency.
ai_technology: AcRanker, an XGBoost pairwise ranking model trained on amino-acid composition and grouped di- and tri-mer features
organization: University of California, Berkeley; Monash University; University of Melbourne

title: AI-prioritized CRISPR screen identifies ALOX5 and OXTR as regulators of keratinocyte IL17RA in psoriasis
summary: A genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in primary human epidermal keratinocytes, combined with VirtualCRISPR language-model prioritization, identified ALOX5 and OXTR as previously underappreciated cell-intrinsic regulators of surface IL17RA. Targeted knockout in keratinocytes from two adult donors reduced IL17RA and inflammatory cytokine secretion. Topical inhibition of ALOX5 or OXTR also reduced disease signs in an imiquimod mouse model of psoriasiform dermatitis.
ai_technology: VirtualCRISPR, a functional-genomics language-model framework trained on BioGRID-ORCS screens
organization: Biohub; Northwestern University; University of Chicago

title: CellOracle-guided pancreatic islet differentiation experiments reveal STAT1 and ZEB1 lineage roles
summary: A digital model built from 400,603 cells across 61 single-cell datasets used CellOracle gene-regulatory-network inference and in-silico transcription-factor perturbations to nominate regulators of stem-cell-derived human islet differentiation. CRISPRi experiments supported a previously unreported role for STAT1 in exocrine specification: transient STAT1 knockdown reduced exocrine markers, and JAK–STAT inhibition preserved beta-cell markers and improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.
