CRISPRi also supported a stage-dependent role for ZEB1, whose early knockdown impaired endocrine specification and later knockdown reduced off-target serotonergic cells while increasing beta-cell proportion. The date is the first preprint posting; this entry summarizes the later version reviewed in the research record, which reports the specific STAT1 and ZEB1 experiments.
ai_technology: CellOracle v0.12.0 within a digital model integrating single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility data
organization: Washington University School of Medicine; University of Miami

title: BacterAI experimentally maps amino-acid growth requirements of two oral Streptococcus species
summary: BacterAI autonomously designed and ran growth experiments with robotic liquid handling to learn amino-acid requirements for the oral commensals Streptococcus gordonii and S. sanguinis. It learned separate growth rules for each organism and showed that the closely related species have different amino-acid auxotrophies. For S. gordonii, its neural-network growth predictions exceeded 90% accuracy after nine days and 3,024 experiments; the article also reports transfer-learning tests in larger media.
ai_technology: BacterAI, a reinforcement-learning agent coupled to iterative neural-network growth models and automated laboratory robots
organization: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; University of Michigan

title: Prospective multicenter validation of TriVerity links a 29-mRNA host response to infection type and near-term severity
summary: In the prospective SEPSIS-SHIELD study, a machine-learning blood test using isothermal amplification of 29 host-response mRNAs was evaluated in adults presenting to 22 emergency departments with suspected infection or sepsis. Among 1,222 patients with valid results, its bacterial and viral scores distinguished clinically adjudicated infection status with AUROCs of 0.83 and 0.91, respectively, and the system also produced a separate score for risk of ICU-level care within seven days. The test’s high/very-high and low/very-low interpretation bands had 92–99% sensitivities and specificities for selected infection/severity endpoints.
ai_technology: TriVerity on the Myrna instrument, using logistic-regression classifiers on expression measurements for 29 host-response mRNAs
organization: Inflammatix; Stanford University; Washington University in St. Louis; 22 emergency-department study sites

title: Deep-learning knee imaging phenotypes reveal osteoarthritis genetic and fracture associations
summary: Using knee DXA scans from the UK Biobank, a ResNet-101 model identified 1,931 more probable knee-osteoarthritis cases than health-record coding and a U-Net segmentation model estimated minimum joint-space width (mJSW). In 29,257 participants, the quantitative mJSW phenotype had substantially higher SNP heritability than the binary phenotypes and yielded 18 genome-wide-significant loci, compared with one for the image-based binary classifier and six for ICD-10 coding; only one mJSW locus was already significant in a large prior knee-OA GWAS. The AI-derived mJSW phenotype was also associated with fracture history in an epidemiological analysis, a signal not seen with the binary case labels.
ai_technology: ResNet-101 convolutional neural network for knee-OA classification and U-Net image segmentation for joint-space measurement
organization: University of Texas at Austin; Dell Medical School; Columbia University; New York Genome Center

title: Machine-learning-selected plasma markers distinguish Lewy body and frontotemporal dementias
summary: A six-cohort plasma proteomics study used cross-validated LASSO to select a 21-protein multiplex panel for dementia differential diagnosis. In the new DLB/FTD results, ITGAV and ITGAM were reduced in dementia with Lewy bodies and also tracked Lewy-body pathology in independent autopsy-confirmed cohorts; a panel including ITGAV, ITGAM and ERBB3 distinguished DLB from controls and Alzheimer dementia in an independent multicenter cohort. For frontotemporal dementia, NfL and B4GAT1 contributed to the panel distinguishing FTD from controls. Validation-set AUCs were 0.83 for DLB versus controls, 0.78 for DLB versus Alzheimer dementia, 0.85 for FTD versus controls and 0.77 for FTD versus Alzheimer dementia.
ai_technology: Cross-validated LASSO regression and multivariable logistic-regression models applied to Olink proximity-extension plasma proteomics
organization: University of Perugia; Amsterdam University Medical Center; CSIRO; Charles University; Sant Pau Research Institute; collaborating international dementia centers

title: Deep-learning-designed enhancers drive target-tissue reporter activity in mouse embryos
summary: Researchers trained convolutional neural networks on E11.5 mouse heart, limb and midbrain chromatin-accessibility data, then fine-tuned the models using validated human and mouse enhancers and used model-guided sequence optimization to design 15 synthetic enhancers. In vivo transgenic reporter assays found all 15 reproducibly active in their intended tissue. Four of five heart designs and four of five CNS designs were exclusive to the target tissue; all five limb designs were strongly active in limb and had weaker activity in other TWIST1-expressing mesenchymal tissues.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural networks for sequence-to-accessibility and sequence-to-activity prediction, transfer learning, and Ledidi gradient-based sequence design
organization: Research Institute of Molecular Pathology (IMP), Vienna BioCenter; University of California, Irvine; Vienna BioCenter PhD Program, University of Vienna and Medical University of Vienna

title: EnzGFM-Agent experimentally prioritizes activity-enhancing secreted alkaline phosphatase variants
summary: EnzGFM-Agent scored all possible single amino-acid substitutions in secreted alkaline phosphatase (SEAP) and selected top candidates from EnzGFM-1.5B and ESM2-3B for testing in transfected Chinese hamster ovary cells. Among the five variants uniquely prioritized by EnzGFM, all five had significantly higher measured activity than wild type in the reported assay; three exceeded 1.5-fold, and A46I reached 6.52-fold. This is an experimentally measured enzyme-engineering result for the tested SEAP variants.
ai_technology: EnzGFM-Agent with EnzGFM-1.5B and ESM2-3B
organization: Henan Medical University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Shanghai AI Laboratory

title: Routine-laboratory LightGBM screening identifies monoclonal immunoglobulin positivity across independent hospitals
summary: A LightGBM classifier trained on routine clinical and laboratory data distinguished serum immunofixation-positive monoclonal immunoglobulin cases from negative cases. In an independent three-hospital cohort of 2,270 patients referred for immunofixation testing, the model achieved an AUC of 0.945, with 87.0% sensitivity and 89.6% specificity. In a subset with serum protein electrophoresis results, model sensitivity was 84.6% versus 75.3% for electrophoresis; in a separate 627-patient time-extended cohort, sensitivity was 88.2%, above each of three nonspecialist clinicians in that study.
ai_technology: LightGBM classifier selected from eight machine-learning models
organization: Xijing Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University; 3201 Hospital; Shaanxi Provincial People’s Hospital; Xi’an Medical University; Xianyang Normal University

title: HMD-AMP mining uncovers evolutionarily remote antimicrobial peptides with validated antibacterial activity
summary: A protein-language-model pipeline, HMD-AMP, screened host and gut-microorganism genomes from nine mammalian species and nominated antimicrobial peptides, including candidates with little similarity to known AMPs. Of 91 high-confidence peptides selected for experiments, 74 showed strong antibacterial activity and 48 were evolutionarily remote from known AMPs. Four tested peptides had broad-spectrum activity at low effective concentrations and low toxicity; the most potent reported candidate showed efficacy in a mouse peritoneal E. coli infection model.
ai_technology: HMD-AMP protein-language-model pipeline
organization: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Chinese University of Hong Kong; Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Broad Institute and collaborating institutions

title: AI-designed bacterial anti-defense proteins enable phage infection and plasmid retention
summary: RFdiffusion-based de novo binder design and experimental screening produced synthetic proteins that inhibited three bacterial defense systems: Thoeris and Avs1 in Bacillus subtilis assays, and DdmDE in Vibrio cholerae. Five designed proteins inhibited Thoeris and nine inhibited Avs1 in the reported screens. An engineered SBSphiJ phage carrying both anti-Thoeris and anti-Avs1 proteins replicated in B. subtilis cells expressing both defenses. In native V. cholerae O1 El Tor, two of four tested DdmDE binders improved plasmid resistance to clearance.
ai_technology: RFdiffusion de novo binder design, ProteinMPNN sequence design and AlphaFold2/3 structure-guided candidate scoring
organization: Weizmann Institute of Science; École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)

title: AI-guided promoter editing raises maize ZmVTE4 expression and kernel alpha-tocopherol
summary: Basenji2-based deep-learning models and editing-plasticity analysis guided CRISPR editing of maize ZmVTE4, a gene involved in vitamin E biosynthesis. Researchers isolated a previously unobserved four-base deletion in the gene’s 5′ untranslated region; the edited allele significantly increased ZmVTE4 expression and α-tocopherol content in kernels. A separate promoter-variant assay supported the four-base deletion, rather than a co-occurring 82-base deletion, as the key change associated with increased reporter activity.
ai_technology: Basenji2-long and Basenji2-3K-NAM sequence-to-expression deep-learning models with editing-plasticity analysis
organization: Huazhong Agricultural University; Hubei Hongshan Laboratory; Yazhouwan National Laboratory; Institute of Agricultural Sciences of Xishuangbanna Prefecture; Max Planck Institute of Molecular Plant Physiology

title: Machine-learning-derived seven-protein panel distinguishes remission from active ANCA-associated vasculitis
summary: Confounder-aware machine-learning feature selection on plasma proteomics identified a seven-protein signature—AHSG, CLEC3B, COMP, F9, LRG1, MCAM and MRC1—to classify remission versus active ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV). After targeted PRM mass-spectrometry assay development, a generalized linear model was evaluated in an independent cohort of 108 AAV patients and achieved AUC 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.98); combined discovery and validation performance was AUC 0.97. In the study cohorts, the panel outperformed routine CRP and ANCA titer measurements.
ai_technology: MetaDeconfoundR confounder-aware feature analysis, LASSO and Boruta feature selection, and a generalized linear model applied to targeted PRM mass-spectrometry data
organization: Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Berlin Institute of Health; Charles University and General University Hospital Prague; University of Oslo

title: CRISPR perturbation and Bayesian network inference map immune-disease regulatory cascades in primary CD4+ T cells
summary: The study used CRISPR knockouts of 84 genes in primary human CD4+ T cells and a new linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB) network-inference method to estimate 211 regulatory connections. Integrating the inferred network with immune GWAS analyses identified an interconnected module in which KMT2A was inferred upstream of JAK-STAT and IL-2 signaling regulators including IRF4, STAT5A/B and IL2RA, linking an epigenetic regulator to immune-disease-associated pathways.
ai_technology: Linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB), a Bayesian extension of linear latent causal network inference, applied to CRISPR knockout and RNA-sequencing data
organization: Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology; University of California, San Francisco; Johns Hopkins University; Stanford University; University of California, Berkeley

title: Multicenter targeted metabolomics and machine learning identify a six-metabolite rheumatoid-arthritis diagnostic panel
summary: Across seven cohorts and five medical centers, targeted metabolomics confirmed six metabolites—imidazoleacetic acid, ergothioneine, N-acetyl-L-methionine, 2-keto-3-deoxy-D-gluconic acid, 1-methylnicotinamide and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate—as a panel for classifying rheumatoid arthritis against healthy controls and osteoarthritis. LASSO selected the six features, and logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost models were externally evaluated in geographically distinct cohorts; reported AUCs were 0.8375–0.9280 for RA versus healthy controls and 0.7340–0.8181 for RA versus osteoarthritis in three validation cohorts.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection and logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine and XGBoost classifiers applied to untargeted and targeted metabolomics
organization: Tongren Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine; The First Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University; Guanghua Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; The First Hospital of Lanzhou University; Xinhua Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine

title: Prospective Swedish cohort validates multimodal AI prostate-biopsy biomarker for recurrence and adverse pathology after prostatectomy
summary: A previously developed multimodal AI score was retrospectively applied to archived diagnostic biopsies and follow-up from a prospectively collected Swedish prostatectomy cohort. The score, derived from digitized diagnostic prostate-biopsy images plus age, PSA and clinical T-stage, was associated with post-surgical biochemical recurrence and adverse pathology. Among 143 men with evaluable data and median 8.8-year follow-up, the continuous score was associated with recurrence (subdistribution HR 2.45, 95% CI 1.77–3.38); among 88 evaluable for adverse pathology, OR was 4.85 (95% CI 2.54–10.78). Estimated 5-year recurrence was 25% in intermediate/high score versus 4% in low score.
ai_technology: Artera multimodal artificial-intelligence (MMAI) prostate biomarker combining deep-learning features from digitized biopsy histopathology with age, PSA and clinical T-stage
organization: Skåne University Hospital; Lund University; Artera Inc.; University of California, San Francisco

title: Machine-learning-guided proteomics identifies APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1 for plaque-rupture classification in acute coronary syndrome
summary: In an acute-coronary-syndrome derivation cohort matched for plaque rupture (PR) versus intact fibrous cap (IFC), quantitative mass spectrometry measured 1,121 plasma proteins. Five machine-learning algorithms screened candidate proteins; APOC3, RAB39A and KNG1 were then significantly different between PR and IFC in an independent 85-patient cohort using ELISA. The three proteins discriminated plaque rupture better than the study’s conventional biomarkers and risk factors, suggesting a candidate biomarker panel for identifying PR among ACS patients.
ai_technology: Unbiased machine-learning feature screening of quantitative mass-spectrometry plasma proteomics using five algorithms
organization: Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University; Beijing Institute of Heart Lung and Blood Vessel Diseases; First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University

title: Machine learning links circulating tyrosine and distinct lipid-metabolite features to diabetic kidney disease and retinopathy detection
summary: In 2,772 adults with diabetes from Singapore’s population-based SEED study, LASSO and gradient-boosting models screened 220 circulating metabolites and 19 clinical factors for prevalent diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and retinopathy (DR), then were externally assessed in 5,843 UK Biobank participants. Both outcomes shared diabetes duration, insulin use, age and tyrosine as important model features. DKD additionally selected cardiovascular disease history, antihypertensive use, lactate, citrate and the intermediate-density-lipoprotein cholesterol-ester/total-lipid ratio; DR additionally selected HbA1c, glucose, pulse pressure and alanine. External AUCs were 0.791 for DKD and 0.778 for DR, versus 0.691 and 0.760 for conventional adjusted logistic-regression comparators.
ai_technology: Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression and gradient-boosting decision trees applied to metabolomics and clinical risk factors
organization: Singapore Eye Research Institute; Singapore National Eye Centre; National University of Singapore; Duke-NUS Medical School

title: Prospective silent-trial validation of a fine-tuned pathology foundation model for EGFR mutation screening in lung adenocarcinoma
summary: A fine-tuned Prov-GigaPath ViT-g model, named EAGLE, predicted EGFR mutation status from routine H&E slides plus clinical features in lung adenocarcinoma. Across an international dataset of 8,461 slides it achieved mean AUC 0.847 internally and 0.870 in external cohorts. In a four-month prospective silent trial on 197 primary lung-adenocarcinoma samples, EAGLE achieved AUC 0.890. Simulated AI-assisted triage thresholds reduced rapid molecular EGFR tests by up to 43% while maintaining the study’s performance criteria.
ai_technology: EAGLE, a task-specific model fine-tuned from the Prov-GigaPath ViT-g pathology foundation model, combining H&E whole-slide image features with clinical variables for EGFR mutation prediction
organization: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; Technical University of Munich; Sahlgrenska University Hospital and University of Gothenburg; SUNY Upstate Medical University; University of Montreal Hospital Centre

title: A six-metabolite machine-learning panel and isovalerylcarnitine findings for gastric cancer
summary: In two multicenter cohorts totaling 597 people, LASSO feature selection and five machine-learning classifiers produced a six-metabolite plasma panel for gastric-cancer diagnosis, with AUCs of 0.947–0.982 in discovery and 0.920–0.951 in validation. The panel included isovalerylcarnitine (C5), which was lower in cancer plasma and paired tumor tissue; the paper further reported a Mendelian-randomization association and cell-assay evidence linking C5 treatment to reduced gastric-cancer cell migration and invasion through calpain-associated changes in VE-cadherin and MMP2.
ai_technology: LASSO regression score feature selection with neural-network, support-vector-machine, ridge-regression, logistic-regression and naive-Bayes classifiers
organization: Zhejiang Cancer Hospital; and six collaborating clinical centers; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Zhejiang Chinese Medical University; Wenzhou Medical University; National Cancer Center/National Clinical Research Center for Cancer, China

title: A seven-metabolite AI model detected renal-cell carcinoma across six validation cohorts
summary: An SVM-based screen of untargeted plasma metabolomics identified candidate renal-cell-carcinoma metabolites, which were confirmed by targeted analysis and used in the RCAID AI diagnostic model. In 1,680 participants across five hospitals, seven plasma metabolites supported AUROCs of 0.977, 0.911, 0.945 and 0.972 in internal, external, multicenter and temporal validation cohorts, respectively; validation also included late-stage and non-clear-cell RCC. The authors report six associated dysregulated pathways from multi-omic analyses.
ai_technology: Support-vector-machine metabolite selection and the Renal Cell Carcinoma Artificial Intelligence Detector (RCAID)
organization: Peking University First Hospital; and Peking University Health Science Center; Beijing Miyun Hospital; Beijing Friendship Hospital; collaborating Chinese hospitals

title: A gradient-boosted model detected untreated infection before antimicrobial administration
summary: The eDENTIFI gradient-boosted model estimated the probability of untreated infection during the next six hours from demographics, vital signs and laboratory results. Trained on 3,357 adult hospitalizations at two Illinois health systems and validated in 1,632 patients at a third, it achieved validation AUC 0.80 versus 0.64 for SIRS criteria. At the reported threshold it detected infection a median two hours before antimicrobial administration (47.6% sensitivity; 93.6% negative predictive value).
ai_technology: eDENTIFI, a gradient-boosted machine model using longitudinal discrete-time predictions
organization: University of Chicago Medical Center; Duke University; Emory University; Loyola University; Endeavor Health; University of Wisconsin-Madison

title: Explainable neural-network analysis nominated GPC6 as a Parkinson disease dopaminergic-neuron marker
summary: An explainable machine-learning workflow applied to four post-mortem midbrain single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets identified cell-type-specific gene signatures that distinguished Parkinson disease from control cells across datasets (mean balanced accuracy 0.92) and nominated ten candidate genes. GPC6 emerged as a marker in dopaminergic neurons; rare GPC6 variants were enriched among Parkinson disease cases in analyses spanning three case-control cohorts.
ai_technology: Explainable neural-network classifiers with LIME feature attribution applied to single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data
organization: McGill University; Montreal Neurological Institute-Hospital

title: Machine-learning protein signatures predicted Crohn disease years before diagnosis
summary: Regularized logistic-regression and other machine-learning analyses of 178 Olink proteins identified a 29-protein preclinical Crohn disease signature. It distinguished future cases from controls with AUC 0.85 in a Swedish discovery cohort and 0.87 in an independent preclinical cohort; a separate inception cohort produced AUC 1.0. The study also reported a less predictive ulcerative-colitis signature and found that downregulated proteins related to gut-barrier integrity and macrophage function correlated with time to Crohn diagnosis.
ai_technology: Regularized logistic regression and additional machine-learning methods (L1-penalized regression, elastic net, support-vector machines and random forests) applied to Olink protein measurements
organization: Örebro University; Karolinska Institutet; Uppsala University; Linköping University; University of Gothenburg; Umeå University; Swedish population-based cohorts and BIOIBD consortium collaborators

title: A 16-feature AI model distinguished Sjögren disease from clinically similar conditions using routine tests
summary: The retrospective multicenter SMFIF study screened routine laboratory data and used multi-algorithm feature selection, SHAP ranking and a stacked ensemble to construct a 16-feature Sjögren disease model. Across a 34,958-patient source population from three Chinese hospitals, reported AUCs were 0.923 in testing, 0.934 in internal validation and 0.964 in a 545-person external cohort. The study also compared the model with conventional autoantibody and laboratory markers and evaluated discrimination from rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, systemic sclerosis and osteoarthritis.
ai_technology: SMFIF, a stacked ensemble of five selected classifiers built from multi-algorithm feature selection and SHAP-ranked routine laboratory features
organization: Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital/Nanjing University Medical School; Suzhou Municipal Hospital/Nanjing Medical University; Huai’an First People’s Hospital/Nanjing Medical University

title: Proteomic profiling and machine learning identified an externally validated diagnostic panel and severity markers for infective endocarditis
summary: The study profiled plasma and excised vegetation samples from 238 infective-endocarditis patients and 100 controls, then used an ensemble machine-learning pipeline to select a 10-protein plasma diagnostic panel. The paper reports AUCs of 0.97 in the held-out discovery test set and 0.98 and 0.94 in two external plasma cohorts. Integrating proteomic and clinical features also produced a prognostic model for severe heart-failure status (abstract AUC 0.87). LRG1 and NDUFB4 were associated with infection severity in the cohort analyses.
ai_technology: Ensemble machine-learning diagnostic and prognostic models; the diagnostic workflow compared six algorithms and used recursive feature elimination with cross-validation to select a 10-protein panel
organization: Fudan University; Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital/Southern Medical University; Fuwai Hospital/Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences; collaborating hospitals in China

title: Blood DNA methylation machine learning signatures classified brain insulin resistance across three cohorts
summary: A machine-learning framework applied to blood DNA-methylation profiles identified 540 CpG sites that classified brain insulin resistance in adults without type 2 diabetes. In the 167-person discovery cohort, the selected methylation signature was tested in two separate replication cohorts of 33 and 24 participants, with reported classification accuracy of 83–94%. The CpGs mapped to 445 genes enriched for neuronal-development and axonogenesis annotations; 98 sites showed significant blood–brain methylation correlation.
ai_technology: Supervised machine-learning framework using blood DNA-methylation profiles; a multi-fold elastic-net approach was described in the associated institutional and conference materials
organization: Institute for Diabetes Research and Metabolic Diseases, Helmholtz Munich/University of Tübingen; German Center for Diabetes Research; German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbruecke; University Hospital Ulm; University of Lübeck; University of Potsdam

title: Automated methylome analysis identified candidate blood epigenetic markers for first-episode schizophrenia
summary: An automated machine-learning workflow screened public blood-methylation datasets and selected IGF2BP1, CENPI and PSME4 as candidate schizophrenia-associated methylation markers. The researchers then measured these genes by targeted qMSP in 30 first-episode, drug-naive schizophrenia patients and 30 controls: IGF2BP1 methylation was higher and PSME4 lower in cases, while CENPI did not differ. A five-feature model combining the three genes with age and sex classified cases versus controls with AUC 0.755 (95% CI 0.636–0.862).
ai_technology: JADBio AutoML platform, comparing classifiers including support-vector machines, random forests, ridge logistic regression and decision trees with feature selection and cross-validation
organization: Democritus University of Thrace; Aristotle University of Thessaloniki; University of Crete; Hellenic Mediterranean University; Foundation for Research and Technology – Hellas

title: PICNIC machine learning predictions revealed previously poorly characterized human proteins in cellular condensates
summary: The PICNIC gradient-boosting model ranked proteins for membership in biomolecular condensates using sequence-pattern and AlphaFold2-derived structural features. To test its predictions, researchers expressed 24 poorly characterized human proteins in U2OS cells: 21 formed mesoscale fluorescent foci, and 18 met the paper’s high-confidence condensate threshold. The experiments mapped examples to cytoplasmic bodies, nuclear bodies, nucleoli or P-bodies; for example, TYW5 and RAD51AP1 showed distinct localization patterns. Across the tested set, the authors found condensate localization was not limited to highly disordered proteins.
ai_technology: PICNIC, a gradient-boosting machine-learning classifier using protein sequence co-occurrence patterns, sequence complexity/disorder features and AlphaFold2-derived structural features
organization: Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics; Center for Systems Biology Dresden; TU Dresden Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life

title: AI-guided subtilisin variants improve aqueous amide formation
summary: The study reports that wild-type subtilisin BPN′ directly catalyzed condensation of free carboxylic acids and amines in aqueous PBS (pH 8, 40 °C), forming a peptide-bond amide without stoichiometric coupling reagents. The authors combined AI-guided mutation ranking with a FRET assay, reducing 7,999 in-silico variants at three active-site positions to five experimental candidates. The top triple mutant N155G/N218D/M222Q had reported relative activity of 753 ± 14% of wild type and also coupled biotin to a peptide fragment in water, extending beyond peptide–peptide ligation.
ai_technology: AI-guided enzyme mutation prediction combining binding-free-energy analysis of active-site substitutions with an experimental FRET-based rapid product-detection platform
organization: Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory; collaborating Chinese research institutions

title: Machine-learning analysis linked two sepsis-associated neutrophil clusters to five mouse-validated marker genes
summary: Reanalysis of single-cell profiles from four sepsis patients and two healthy controls identified two neutrophil clusters enriched in the sepsis samples and a set of cluster-associated gene modules. LASSO and seven additional machine-learning classifiers prioritized eight hub genes, including ALPL, CD177, S100A8, S100A9 and STXBP2. Expression analyses in separate public sepsis transcriptome cohorts supported several markers, and qRT-PCR in cecal-ligation/puncture and LPS mouse models found increased neutrophil expression of those five genes. The result links sepsis-associated neutrophil states to a small marker panel, with experimental expression validation in mice.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection followed by seven machine-learning classifiers (k-nearest neighbors, linear discriminant analysis, logistic regression, naive Bayes, random forest, recursive partitioning and support-vector machine), combined with hdWGCNA and single-cell transcriptomic analysis
organization: Department of General Surgery, General Hospital of Northern Theater Command, Shenyang, China

title: Machine learning uses historical warming patterns to constrain future climate projections
summary: A CatBoost model trained on CMIP6 simulations used the observed 1971–2020 grid-cell warming pattern to identify tropical and polar regions that best constrain later global warming. Applying these spatial constraints reduced projection error variance by about 70%, compared with about 48% using global-mean warming alone; the results depend on model-based emergent relationships and are projections rather than direct observations of future climate.
ai_technology: CatBoost machine-learning emergent-constraint model
organization: East China Normal University; Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology; Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium; University of Victoria

title: Deep learning maps six high-potential deep-Earth scattering zones
summary: Researchers used deep learning with iterative manual optimization to identify 174,929 PKP precursors in more than two million earthquake waveforms recorded from 1990 to 2024. The expanded global map connected previously isolated sampling regions and highlighted six high-potential scattering zones near the core–mantle boundary that the authors report had not previously been documented. These are model-inferred targets for later seismic imaging, not fully characterized structures.
ai_technology: Deep-learning PKP precursor detector with human iterative optimization
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: AI-guided experiments establish feasible 500–950 W printing configurations for GRCop-42
summary: A closed-loop Bayesian experimental-design method, BEAM, found multiple defect-free directed-energy-deposition configurations for GRCop-42 copper alloy at infrared laser powers from 950 down to 500 W. Researchers report that these experimentally successful settings solved a process-development problem that had resisted several months of manual trials, enabling GRCop-42 fabrication on lower-power platforms. This is a manufacturing-process result for an existing alloy, not a new alloy composition.
ai_technology: BEAM (Bayesian Experimental design for Additive Manufacturing)
organization: Washington State University

title: Machine-learning screening and experiments identify two new superconductors, Be₂HfNb₂ and Be₂Hf₂Nb
summary: An AI-accelerated workflow screened more than 1.3 million material structures, combining a graph-neural-network model of superconducting properties with density-functional calculations and stability filters. The researchers experimentally synthesized and confirmed superconductivity in Be₂HfNb₂ and Be₂Hf₂Nb, reporting two previously unreported compounds among 741 computationally screened stable candidates. The two compounds were confirmed in the Be₂Nb₃ substitution series; other listed candidates remain computational predictions.
ai_technology: BEE-NET equivariant graph neural networks in an AI-accelerated high-throughput screening workflow
organization: University of Florida; Oak Ridge National Laboratory; Quantum Formatics

title: Machine-learning triage identifies a dormant wandering black hole in a galaxy’s outskirts
summary: The off-nuclear transient TDE 2025abcr revealed a dormant supermassive black hole about 9.3 kiloparsecs from its host galaxy’s center, with a mass described as similar to the Milky Way’s central black hole. A machine-learning program searching for tidal-disruption flares anywhere in the sky selected the event for follow-up three months after deployment; astronomers then collected multi-instrument evidence and interpreted it as the strongest known wandering-black-hole case. Its precise origin remains uncertain, with stripped remnant and black-hole-ejection scenarios both discussed.
ai_technology: Off-nuclear tidal-disruption-event classifier (tdescore)
organization: University of Maryland; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of California Observatories and collaborators

title: AI-guided autonomous experiments map phase domains in bismuth–titanium oxide films
summary: A robotic active-learning campaign using SARA-H mapped processing regions that stabilize δ-Bi₂O₃ and Bi₂Ti₂O₇ in thin films and examined dwell-dependent phase behavior in the Bi–Ti–O system. The study also experimentally supported the prediction that bismuth substitution in TiO₂ inhibits the anatase-to-rutile transformation. This is a human-in-the-loop experimental materials result; the compounds/phases were not all newly discovered, while the mapped processing domains and comparative evidence are the study-specific contribution.
ai_technology: SARA-H (Scientific Autonomous Reasoning Agent with human input) and automated probabilistic phase labeling
organization: Cornell University; California Institute of Technology; Liquid Sunlight Alliance

title: Multiscale machine-learning microscopy identifies robust paleomagnetic carriers in meteorite WIS 91600
summary: A multiscale microscopy study of carbonaceous chondrite WIS 91600 used a deep-learning classifier to segment magnetic remanence-carrying ensembles and quantify their volume and texture. Combined chemical mapping, 3D nanotomography, and diffraction showed fine matrix-hosted magnetite has paleomagnetic recording potential comparable to magnetite framboids but is less susceptible to strong interactions; transient heating also reduced the contribution of matrix pyrrhotite through its vacancy-ordering state. This is one meteorite case study, and the mineralogical conclusions draw on the full microscopy and diffraction workflow, not AI alone.
ai_technology: UNET segmentation, SIGMA interactive machine-learning mineral analysis, and few-shot image segmentation
organization: University of Cambridge; and collaborators

title: A machine-learning-assisted TESS search confirms a previously unknown hot Jupiter
summary: The T16 pipeline processed 83.7 million TESS Cycle 1 full-frame-image light curves and reported 10,091 new transiting-planet candidates, alongside previously known candidates. Radial-velocity follow-up confirmed TIC 183374187 b as a newly identified hot Jupiter, demonstrating that the semi-automated search yielded at least one bona fide new planet. Most entries in the catalog remain candidates rather than confirmed planets.
ai_technology: T16 semi-automated transit search with random-forest machine-learning vetting
organization: Princeton University; and collaborating institutions

title: Machine-learning X-ray analysis provides bulk evidence for a Bragg-glass phase in PdₓErTe₃
summary: Researchers combined extensive X-ray diffraction with X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC) to identify Bragg-glass signatures in the charge-density-wave material PdₓErTe₃. Their analysis extracted diffraction features across about 20,000 Brillouin zones and found a diverging correlation length and a phase diagram consistent with a Bragg-glass transition. The result provides bulk diffraction evidence for a phase that had been difficult to establish experimentally.
ai_technology: X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC), a machine-learning analysis of X-ray diffraction peaks
organization: Cornell University; Stanford University; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

title: Machine-learning image search helps identify Pavo, an isolated star-forming dwarf galaxy
summary: A search combining low-surface-brightness galaxy detection and machine-learning candidate classification identified Pavo in Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey imaging. Follow-up Magellan imaging resolved young and old stellar populations and measured a tip-of-the-red-giant-branch distance of about 1.99 Mpc, establishing Pavo as an extremely isolated, low-mass star-forming dwarf galaxy just beyond the Local Group.
ai_technology: Machine-learning image candidate classifier used with low-surface-brightness galaxy search algorithms
organization: University of Arizona; University of Chicago; University of Minnesota Duluth; and collaborators

title: Deep learning reveals more than 500 previously unrecognized earthquakes beneath David Glacier
summary: A deep-learning analysis of regional Antarctic seismic records identified more than 500 previously unrecognized intermediate-depth earthquakes roughly 100–150 km beneath David Glacier in East Antarctica. The earthquakes occur within a tectonic plate rather than at a plate boundary. The authors explain the concentration through bending stresses associated with variable thermally driven uplift and an abrupt change in lithospheric strength; the ice sheet may also affect regional stress.
ai_technology: Deep-learning seismic-event detector applied to regional seismic records
organization: University of Alabama; Complutense University of Madrid; University of Oklahoma

title: Swin-Transformer discovery of planetary nebulae with spectroscopic confirmation in VPHAS+
summary: A Swin-Transformer search of VPHAS+ Hα images identified faint, resolved planetary-nebula candidates in crowded Galactic fields that prior point-source searches missed. Follow-up spectroscopy and HASH classification of 31 targets found 16 true, two likely and four possible planetary nebulae, alongside contaminants and a supernova-remnant fragment. This is one validated search-sample result, not 22 equally secure confirmations.
ai_technology: Swin-Transformer deep-learning classifier trained on known planetary nebulae
organization: The University of Hong Kong; Taiyuan University of Technology; Peng Cheng Laboratory

title: Active learning identifies 28 new DFT-validated pressure-induced phase transitions
summary: Across 13 active-learning cycles, a graph neural network screened phase pairs for pressure-induced transitions and selected cases for density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations. DFT confirmed 28 previously unreported transformations; 14 high-pressure phases were dynamically stable at transition pressure, including 10 also predicted dynamically stable at zero pressure. The study also identifies a previously unrecorded dynamically stable monoclinic P2₁/c phase of Cr₂O₃.
ai_technology: MEGNet graph neural network with five-model ensemble and iterative active learning
organization: Purdue University

title: Representation learning uncovers the extragalactic X-ray transient XRT 200515 in Chandra archives
summary: A representation-learning pipeline searched archived Chandra event data and identified XRT 200515, a previously unnoticed extragalactic fast X-ray transient in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Its light curve has a sharp sub-10-second hard burst followed by an approximately 800-second oscillating tail with spectral softening. The paper discusses possible origins including a low-energy giant magnetar flare or a Type I burst from a faint low-mass X-ray binary; the source's physical nature is unresolved.
ai_technology: Unsupervised representation-learning pipeline using sparse autoencoders, dimensionality reduction and density-based clustering
organization: Stanford University; Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics; Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory; collaborators

title: Data-driven equations reveal rainfall-linked North Atlantic decadal variability
summary: Using SINDy equation discovery on monthly observational indices from 1950–2022, researchers derived three linked low-order equations for Atlantic Multidecadal Variability, the North Atlantic Oscillation and North Atlantic precipitation. The model recovered a distinct roughly 20-year component and highlighted precipitation-linked terms as robust components of the learned dynamics; tests against the independent 1900–1939 record found skill for statistics of the variability indices and rainfall. The equations generate hypotheses about ocean-atmosphere feedbacks; they do not establish a single causal mechanism or guarantee forecasts.
ai_technology: Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) equation-discovery algorithm
organization: University of Oxford; UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology; UK Met Office

title: LHCb reports first single-experiment evidence for B⁰ → μ⁺μ⁻ decay
summary: Using 18 fb⁻¹ of Run 3 data and earlier LHCb data, the collaboration reports first single-experiment evidence for the rare B⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ decay, with a combined significance of 3.2σ and measured branching fraction (1.14 +0.42/−0.39 stat. +0.06/−0.05 syst.)×10⁻¹⁰. A boosted decision tree classified candidates and suppressed combinatorial background in the fit. This is evidence below the 5σ discovery threshold; results agree with Standard Model expectations. The date is the original preprint submission; CERN announced the result on 3 November 2026.
ai_technology: LHCb boosted decision tree (BDT) candidate classifier and multivariate trigger classifiers
organization: LHCb Collaboration; CERN

title: Machine learning reveals two previously undetected phases in Rydberg-atom quantum-simulator data
summary: An interpretable hybrid unsupervised/supervised learning analysis of experimental snapshots from a programmable Rydberg-atom array mapped phase regions on a square lattice and identified signatures of two previously undetected phases: boundary-ordered and rhombic. The rhombic pattern had been predicted theoretically, so the result is its experimental-data signature rather than a wholly unanticipated theoretical phase; the boundary-ordered phase was revealed from edge correlations.
ai_technology: Hybrid-correlation convolutional neural network (Hybrid-CCNN) with PCA and clustering
organization: Harvard University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Cornell University; collaborators

title: Deep learning resolves subtle seismic-wave changes across the 2016 Norcia earthquake cycle
summary: A seven-layer convolutional neural network classified raw seismic waveforms recorded near Italy’s 2016 Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake as pre- or post-mainshock and separated time-to-failure intervals with over 90% test accuracy. The authors interpret the model’s performance, frequency dependence and null tests as evidence that local waveforms encode evolving attenuation and elastic properties consistent with progressive fault damage before rupture and postseismic recovery.
ai_technology: Seven-layer convolutional neural network trained on local seismic waveforms
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; Pennsylvania State University

title: Three spectroscopically confirmed z≈6 quasars found through contrastive learning
summary: A self-supervised contrastive-learning search of Dark Energy Survey imaging isolated a group of 11 sources that included seven known z≈6 quasars. Follow-up Gemini-South and archival NTT spectroscopy confirmed three additional quasars at redshifts 5.94–6.07. One source, J0109−5424, shows evidence of a foreground object and is a lensed-quasar candidate, but its multiple-image status requires high-resolution imaging.
ai_technology: Self-supervised contrastive-learning neural network trained on Dark Energy Survey imaging data
organization: University of Cambridge; Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Gemini Observatory/NSF NOIRLab; INAF; collaborators

title: AI-enhanced seismic catalog exposes a ring-fault system at Campi Flegrei
summary: A retrained machine-learning workflow applied to continuous seismic records from 2022–2025 expanded the Campi Flegrei earthquake catalog from about 12,000 to more than 54,000 events. The more complete locations delineated a sharply defined, shallow caldera ring-fault system, illuminated previously unclear northern faults, and identified very shallow hybrid events likely associated with the hydrothermal system. The authors report no direct signature of upward magma migration in the analyzed data.
ai_technology: Retrained machine-learning seismic detection and phase-picking workflow developed at Stanford
organization: Stanford University; Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia – Osservatorio Vesuviano; University of Naples Federico II

title: Machine-learning-guided synthesis confirms superconductivity in Mo20Re6Si4
summary: Researchers used a deep-learning composition model to prioritize a sigma-phase ternary compound, synthesized Mo20Re6Si4, and measured bulk superconductivity with a critical temperature of 5.4 K. Magnetic susceptibility and a specific-heat anomaly support the bulk transition. The paper reports mixed model performance on its small test set and describes the model as guidance alongside chemical intuition.
ai_technology: Deep-learning neural network that classifies compositions as superconducting and predicts critical temperature
organization: Rutgers University; Flatiron Institute; University of South Carolina; Princeton University; Michigan State University

title: Semi-supervised image classifiers lead to confirmation of a new lensed quasar
summary: Semi-supervised image classifiers trained on Pan-STARRS and DESI imagery surfaced five quasar-lens candidates for Keck follow-up. Spectroscopy confirmed GRALJ140833.73+042229.98 as a previously undiscovered gravitationally lensed quasar: a z=2.998 quasar lensed by a z=0.542 early-type galaxy. Three other targets were quasar-plus-star or quasar-plus-galaxy interlopers, and one remained unresolved.
ai_technology: Semi-supervised image-classifier pipeline using a convolutional autoencoder with a classifier, plus a convolutional network trained with virtual adversarial training
organization: University of Sydney; University of California, Irvine; California Institute of Technology; collaborators

title: Self-supervised imaging search identifies 16 spectroscopically confirmed quasars at z≈5.94–6.45
summary: Contrastive learning on DESI Legacy Survey DR10 multiband images, followed by SED-fit prioritization, selected sources for spectroscopy; follow-up confirmed 16 quasars at z=5.94–6.45. Several show uncommon narrow Lyα lines, strong Lyα+N V equivalent widths or mildly red observed-frame NIR slopes, and three lie in regions traditional color cuts would miss. The 16-object reported sample includes 15 new literature discoveries and one independently confirmed DESI DR1 source; the 45% follow-up yield includes previously known quasars among 40 observed targets.
ai_technology: Self-supervised contrastive-learning neural network applied to DESI Legacy Survey DR10 multiband images, with SED-fit prioritization
organization: Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile; Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Universidad Diego Portales; University of Geneva; collaborators

title: Deep learning and spectroscopy confirm four faint quasars at redshift about 5
summary: A deep-learning and Bayesian-information-criterion search of Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam photometry selected four faint high-redshift quasar candidates. Palomar spectroscopy found broad Lyman-alpha emission and breaks in all four, confirming redshifts between 4.7 and 5.6; one object also received a black-hole mass estimate.
ai_technology: Deep-learning photometric classifier combined with Bayesian information criterion
organization: Seoul National University; Kyungpook National University; Kavli Institute for Astronomy and Astrophysics, Peking University

title: The QUBRICS machine-learning survey spectroscopically identifies 224 new bright high-redshift quasars
summary: The QUBRICS survey applied a machine-learning selection pipeline to southern optical and infrared catalogs and followed candidates spectroscopically. The paper reports 224 newly identified bright quasars at z≥2.5, including 15 at z>4, and provides a large southern sample for cosmological observations.
ai_technology: QUBRICS machine-learning photometric selection with Canonical Correlation Analysis redshift regression
organization: INAF Astronomical Observatory of Trieste; INAF Astronomical Observatory of Padova; Las Campanas Observatory; Sapienza University of Rome; other QUBRICS collaboration institutions

title: AI-assisted seismic mapping reveals segmented fault activity at the Discovery transform fault
summary: A machine-learning earthquake-detection and relocation workflow applied to 2008 ocean-bottom seismometer records found that the western Discovery transform-fault strand may comprise seven patches with distinct seismicity. The authors also identify a seismicity-gap zone that they interpret as possibly linked to an active small off-ridge rift.
ai_technology: PhaseNet phase picker, GaMMA phase association, and machine-learning-enhanced seismic event workflow
organization: University of California, Santa Cruz; Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution

title: EqGPT infers a previously unreported equation for steepening surface gravity waves
summary: A knowledge-guided generative model trained on mathematical handbook equations generated candidate PDEs, then evaluated and optimized them against data. In a real-data case study of strongly nonlinear surface gravity waves approaching breaking, the authors report an equation not previously reported for that process.
ai_technology: EqGPT, a generative transformer using equation tokenization and a generation–evaluation–optimization loop
organization: China University of Petroleum (East China); Imperial College London; Southern University of Science and Technology; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of Oxford

title: Autonomous X-ray mapping reveals previously unseen block-copolymer morphologies, including a nanoscale ladder
summary: An autonomous experiment planner selected synchrotron X-ray measurements across a combinatorial block-copolymer blend sample. The resulting map and targeted electron microscopy revealed previously unreported alternating, skew/bilayer, and ladder-like self-assembled morphologies, and the authors infer a general mechanism of local subdomain partitioning.
ai_technology: gpCAM autonomous experimentation framework for selecting high-value measurements
organization: Brookhaven National Laboratory Center for Functional Nanomaterials and National Synchrotron Light Source II; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory CAMERA

title: SMDET-selected ultracool-dwarf candidates include two objects with spectroscopically confirmed T-dwarf types
summary: The SMDET image-level neural network identified 118 previously uncatalogued high-proper-motion ultracool-dwarf candidates in WISE time-series images. Follow-up near-infrared spectra for two selected objects yielded T5 and T3 classifications, confirming their estimated spectral types within one subtype.
ai_technology: SMDET, a convolutional neural network for detecting faint moving sources in WISE time-series coadds
organization: Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 collaboration; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; California Institute of Technology/IPAC; Northern Arizona University

title: Machine-learning tremor catalog reveals Japan Trench spatial and slow-slip relationships
summary: A machine-learning monitoring system applied to eight years of S-net seafloor records detected seven times more tectonic tremors than the previous envelope-correlation catalog. The denser catalog resolved tremor activity extending along strike and dip, tremor patterns synchronized with slow-slip events, higher tremor energy rates near large-earthquake asperities, and a positive relationship between energy rate and recurrence interval; authors interpret the latter as evidence consistent with plate-boundary frictional heterogeneity.
ai_technology: DiET convolutional neural network and GrASP graph-based station association, with hybrid envelope-correlation/energy-ratio hypocenter location
organization: Geological Survey of Japan, National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology; Tohoku University

title: Deep learning reveals a new seismicity distribution along the Kabaw Fault in central Myanmar
summary: A deep-learning-based catalog pipeline processed 18 months of seismic-array data and located 1,891 shallow earthquakes, more than twice the 849 events in the prior manual catalog. The denser catalog shows that shallow Kabaw Fault seismicity disappears south of about 22.8°N while deeper events occur west of the fault, and it fills part of a previously under-sampled seismicity gap; the authors interpret this contrast as potentially reflecting along-strike variation in deformation associated with oblique Indian-plate subduction.
ai_technology: DEPALORE pipeline using Earthquake Transformer, transfer-learned PickNet, REAL association, NonLinLoc location and HypoDD relocation
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Zhejiang Ocean University; collaborators

title: Unsupervised machine learning reveals previously missed hydraulic-fracturing seismicity in Live Oak County
summary: An unsupervised repeating-signal detector, combined with template matching, exposed small earthquake bursts in a region of the Eagle Ford shale where conventional catalogs had detected little seismicity. The authors report that the new events temporally coincided with hydraulic-fracturing activity, and their regional analysis found detectable seismicity began after injection flux exceeded about two million barrels per month despite similar cumulative injection volume; this supports, but does not prove, a causal role for injection rate and is limited by sparse station coverage.
ai_technology: Repeating Signal Detector (RSD), an unsupervised machine-learning waveform-family detector
organization: Miami University; University of Kansas

title: A self-driving laboratory discovers lens-and-grating patterns that steer spontaneous emission
summary: A self-driving nanophotonics experiment discovered that combining lens-like refractive-index curvature with grating-like spatial gradient can steer incoherent light emission from a semiconductor metasurface beyond conventional momentum-matching designs. Across a 74° field of view, optimized patterns produced average peak directivity 2.2 times that of sawtooth-grating controls, reaching 67% peak directivity; a fitted equation learner extracted a compact relationship from the experiments.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder, active-learning experimental planner and neural-network equation learner
organization: Sandia National Laboratories

title: A self-driving lab finds a polymer shell with record energy-absorbing efficiency
summary: A human-supervised self-driving laboratory selected and physically tested more than 25,000 additively manufactured polymer shell designs across an 11-dimensional parameter space. The campaign found a structure with 75.2% energy-absorbing efficiency, exceeding the paper’s previously reported maximum of 71.8% for balsa wood, and the authors derived transferable design heuristics from the resulting dataset. The result is a structural design for specified compression thresholds, not a universal material efficiency ranking.
ai_technology: MAMA BEAR self-driving laboratory with Bayesian optimization and automated additive manufacturing/testing
organization: Boston University; U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Soldier Center

title: Machine learning helps identify 61 new cataclysmic variables in SDSS-V spectroscopy
summary: A convolutional neural network shortlisted cataclysmic-variable candidates from more than two million SDSS-V spectra, reducing the spectra requiring visual inspection to about 2% of the total. Human review and follow-up analysis of the resulting 504-object sample reported 61 previously unreported cataclysmic variables, spectroscopically confirmed 248 candidates and yielded 82 new or improved orbital periods; the article discusses selection biases and the CNN missed 27 spectra later found by human review.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network classifier for SDSS-V/BOSS spectra
organization: SDSS-V collaboration; University of Warwick and collaborating institutions

title: Spectroscopic follow-up revises Gaia machine-learning white-dwarf classifications and reveals a large magnetic and carbon-rich population
summary: Follow-up spectra for 255 Gaia white dwarfs were compared with machine-learning classifications from low-resolution Gaia spectra. The study reports that only 5 of 112 objects classified as massive DBs were genuine DB white dwarfs; most were magnetic white dwarfs or warm DQ stars. Its spectroscopy also catalogued 63 magnetic white dwarfs and 29 warm DQs in the selected sample, while confirming high classification accuracy for major spectral types within the classifier’s training set.
ai_technology: Random-forest spectral classifier applied to Gaia low-resolution spectra
organization: Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya; Universitat de Barcelona and collaborators

title: Unsupervised learning reveals mixed-frequency seismic precursors before Axial Seamount’s 2015 eruption
summary: An analysis of four months of Axial Seamount seismicity combined supervised event discrimination with unsupervised spectral clustering and found a mixed-frequency earthquake class whose counts rose rapidly about 15 hours before the 2015 eruption. The events migrated along mapped eruptive fissures; the authors interpret them as brittle crack opening associated with magma or volatile influx. This is a retrospective single-eruption finding, not an operationally validated forecast.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine-learning spectral clustering, with supervised event discrimination
organization: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, Columbia University; University of Washington; Chinese University of Hong Kong

title: Machine learning identifies regional low-magnitude seismic unrest before the Ridgecrest and Anchorage earthquakes
summary: A random-forest method using statistical features from earthquake catalogs identified abnormal low-magnitude seismicity spreading across roughly 15–25% of Southern California and Southcentral Alaska up to about three months before the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence and 2018 Anchorage M7.1 earthquake. Finite-element mechanics models were used to propose a pore-fluid-pressure explanation. This is a retrospective analysis of two target events, not a demonstrated reliable warning system.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning algorithm with earthquake-catalog statistical features
organization: Institute of Geophysics, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC); University of Edinburgh

title: Weakly supervised deep learning maps seamount morphology patterns associated with tectonic setting
summary: A weakly supervised deep-learning analysis combining satellite-derived gravity and bathymetry produced a global seamount inventory and reported systematic morphology differences: broad edifices along fast-spreading ridges and steeper forms near intraplate hotspots. The authors interpret these differences as reflecting geodynamic controls on volcanic construction. Many detections rely on indirect gravity/bathymetry data rather than shipborne mapping, so individual feature identifications and causal interpretations require further validation.
ai_technology: Weakly supervised deep-learning detector with vision foundation model, iterative pseudo-label refinement, and elliptical Gaussian fitting
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory

title: Machine learning identifies predicted zero- and extreme-thermal-expansion monolayers
summary: High-throughput calculations and symbolic regression identified mechanical descriptors that classify positive- versus negative-thermal-expansion 2D crystals, then used those descriptors to predict monolayers with near-zero thermal expansion (2D Invar) and unusually large positive or negative expansion (anti-Invar). The paper reports multiple specific predicted crystals and explains the phonon/deformation-mode basis. The materials are computational predictions rather than experimentally synthesized monolayers.
ai_technology: High-throughput calculations combined with symbolic regression machine learning
organization: Soochow University; Xi’an Jiaotong University

title: Machine-learning-assisted design predicts Netsene, a 3D carbon nodal-surface semimetal
summary: A theory-guided inverse-design study combined a crystal diffusion variational autoencoder with a Crystal Transformer to propose a body-centered tetragonal C24 allotrope, Netsene. First-principles calculations report dynamical and mechanical stability and a nested nodal-surface semimetal band structure with drumhead surface states. This is a computationally predicted allotrope and electronic phase, not an experimentally synthesized material.
ai_technology: Crystal diffusion variational autoencoder (CDVAE) and Crystal Transformer, guided by symmetry-engineering theory
organization: Authors’ institutions include Nanjing University and associated materials-physics groups (see arXiv record)

title: A radio survey reveals megaparsec-scale diffuse emission around a cosmic-web node
summary: Radio U-Net prompted reanalysis of LOFAR, XMM-Newton, DESI optical/near-infrared and weak-lensing data around cluster PSZ2 G083.29−31.03. The team reports previously unnoticed diffuse radio emission extending about 5 Mpc and aligned with X-ray emission and galaxies; lensing supports a complex mass distribution with two low-mass systems on either side of the cluster. The authors propose that these systems are merging substructures in a massive cosmic-web node, while noting alternative interpretations remain possible.
ai_technology: Radio U-Net, a machine-learning detector for diffuse radio emission
organization: University of Bologna; INAF; University of Milano-Bicocca; National Central University, Taiwan; University of Tokyo; INAF Istituto di Radioastronomia; CINECA

title: Deep-learning tracking of mantle simulations finds continental-margin subduction zones persist longer
summary: A fully convolutional network segmented subduction zones in two-dimensional mantle-convection simulations using temperature, vertical velocity and fineness fields. Across the modeled runs, zones forming near continental margins were generally longer-lived and less sensitive to internal heating than oceanic zones, supporting the hypothesis that continental lithosphere can stabilize subduction during early-Earth-like conditions. This is a computational-model result rather than direct observation of ancient Earth.
ai_technology: Attention-based fully convolutional network with custom segmentation loss
organization: Pennsylvania State University; Georgia Institute of Technology

title: Machine learning maps modeled fault-system CO₂ flux within active tectonic regions worldwide
summary: A stacked ensemble trained on 867 compiled degassing records and geospatial raster predictors generated a continuous 0.10° map of model-estimated CO₂ flux within an active-tectonics applicability mask. The authors report spatially coherent high-flux estimates along the Andes, Pacific Ring of Fire and other active orogens. This is a new model-derived spatial estimate for fault-system flux, rather than a direct global survey or measurement.
ai_technology: Stacked regression ensemble combining support-vector, k-nearest-neighbor, decision-tree, random-forest and gradient-boosting models
organization: Universidad Nacional de Colombia; Academia Colombiana de Ciencias Exactas

title: Deep learning finds comet C/2020 T2 in a single ZTF image
summary: The Tails EfficientDet model identified the extended object C/2020 T2 in one Zwicky Transient Facility Twilight Survey image on 2020 October 7. Follow-up orbital work confirmed it as a long-period comet. The study reports this as the first comet discovery assisted by deep learning; it also recovered a previously known comet, which is not counted as a new discovery here.
ai_technology: Tails, an EfficientDet-based deep-learning comet detector
organization: California Institute of Technology; IPAC; Zwicky Transient Facility collaboration

title: UMAP analysis of DESI spectra surfaces newly recognized inhomogeneous white dwarfs
summary: A machine-learning-guided analysis of DESI multi-epoch spectra used UMAP to identify three systems with strongly varying spectral signatures that were proposed as new ‘double-faced’ white dwarfs with inhomogeneous surface composition. Follow-up phase-resolved time-series spectra verified the interpretation for one system; the other two remain candidates. This is one paper-level result and only the verified system is counted as confirmed.
ai_technology: UMAP dimensionality reduction applied to multi-epoch white-dwarf spectroscopy, alongside a neural-network spectral classifier
organization: University of Warwick; University of Leicester; University of Barcelona; Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias; DESI collaboration

title: Claude-assisted analytic proof establishes a+b=1 for mean-field jamming exponents
summary: Giorgio Parisi and Francesco Zamponi provide an analytic proof that the critical exponents a and b in the full replica-symmetry-breaking scaling solution for infinite-dimensional dense hard spheres obey a+b=1. The identity links gap, contact-force and overlap scaling relations and had previously been known numerically but not analytically. The authors report that Claude Opus 4.7 derived the core proof idea with minimal supervision, with Sonnet 4.6 helping refine it; the authors found and corrected errors in an early draft, then verified and edited the final proof.
ai_technology: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7 and Claude Sonnet 4.6
organization: Sapienza University of Rome; CNR-Nanotec Rome; INFN Sezione di Roma 1; Beihang University

title: AI-assisted transfer-matrix analysis yields an exact solution for the 1D frustrated q-state Potts model
summary: The study exactly solves the one-dimensional J₁–J₂ q-state Potts model for arbitrary q by reducing its q²×q² transfer matrix to a 2×2 maximally symmetric subspace and mapping it to an effective q-state Potts model in a field. OpenAI’s o3-mini-high reasoning model helped derive the q=3 case; the author then generalized the result to arbitrary q and checked the formulas numerically. The solution nontrivially extends an older mapping known for q=2/Ising and yields q-dependent phase and residual-entropy behavior.
ai_technology: OpenAI o3-mini-high reasoning model
organization: Brookhaven National Laboratory

title: Gemini derives an exact analytic solution for the cosmic-string gravitational-radiation power integral
summary: A Gemini Deep Think system, guided by tree search and numerical feedback, derived closed-form spectral coefficients for the integral determining gravitational radiation power from cosmic-string loops, resolving the paper’s stated open calculation. The authors compare the expressions against direct numerical integration over ranges of loop harmonic and geometry parameters, finding close agreement. This is a theoretical/computational result, not a new astronomical detection.
ai_technology: Google Gemini Deep Think integrated with tree search, executable Python evaluation and high-precision numerical feedback
organization: Affiliations are not recorded as an organization claim because the consulted arXiv page did not expose them in the checked abstract.

title: Machine learning identifies disordered twist-angle sequences with strongly reduced thermal conductivity in multilayer graphene
summary: Bayesian optimization and a CNN, coupled to non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, selected two-angle disordered twisted multilayer graphene structures with substantially lower simulated cross-plane thermal conductivity than aligned and periodic stacks. The optimized 14-layer sequence reached 0.095 W m−1 K−1 versus 0.512 W m−1 K−1 in aligned graphene in the reported model; phonon participation ratios and dynamical structure factors support strong partial phonon localization.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization (COMBO) and convolutional neural network coupled to molecular-dynamics simulations
organization: Sun Yat-sen University

title: Machine-learning analysis attributes the apparent pre-Norcia earthquake b-value rise to changing activity across two fault structures
summary: For the 2016–2017 central Italy sequence, a combination of machine-learning techniques resolved two seismicity volumes with distinct fault orientations and Gutenberg–Richter b-values. Each structure retained its own b-value through the sequence; the apparent rise before the Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake emerged when both were combined as their relative activity changed, showing that spatial heterogeneity can create an apparent temporal b-value signal.
ai_technology: Combination of machine-learning techniques for seismicity structure and b-value analysis (paper abstract does not name a single model)
organization: University of Naples Federico II; Scuola Superiore Meridionale

title: Machine-learning phase picks constrain the 2025 Drake Passage earthquake depth and activated fault geometry
summary: For the Mw 7.4 Drake Passage earthquake of 2 May 2025, a trained classifier identified depth-sensitive pP–sP seismic phases used to refine focal depths under sparse station coverage. The authors infer a mainshock depth of about 25 km, consistent with the small tsunami, and report aftershocks on west-dipping faults southeast of the epicenter near the Shackleton Fracture Zone; the paper integrates this with seismic-reflection and previously collected imaging data.
ai_technology: Trained machine-learning classifier for depth-sensitive seismic phase identification
organization: Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale (OGS); CNR-ISMAR; University of Urbino; CONICET–University of Buenos Aires

title: OptPDE identifies new candidate integrable PDE families with nontrivial conserved quantities
summary: Automatic differentiation optimized partial-differential-equation coefficients to increase the number of conserved quantities. The published study reports four PDE families with at least one nontrivial conserved quantity and analytically studies one new candidate, u_t = u_x^3; the work establishes candidate systems and conserved quantities, not that every generated family is fully integrable.
ai_technology: OptPDE coefficient optimization with the CQFinder conserved-quantity search
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: Machine learning identifies sediment-derived granites in the Hadean zircon record, supporting early subduction
summary: A machine-learning classifier trained on trace-element fingerprints identified detrital zircon signatures from sediment-derived S-type granites as old as 4.24 billion years in the Jack Hills record. Across global detrital zircon data, the authors report long-term cyclic changes in S-type granite proportions and infer that exposed, weathered continental crust and subduction operated by about 4.2 Ga. The result bears on early Earth geodynamics, not a direct fossil or biological discovery.
ai_technology: Trace-element Support Vector Machine (TSVM) classifier
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Macau University of Science and Technology; University of California, Davis; Queen’s University

title: Interpretable machine learning finds a perpendicular-spin signature consistent with a spinon Fermi surface
summary: A correlator convolutional neural network trained on projective snapshots from numerical simulations of the Kitaev–Heisenberg model identified a characteristic correlation pattern in the intermediate gapless phase when analyzing spin snapshots perpendicular to the applied field. The authors interpret the learned pattern as Friedel oscillations of gapless spinons forming a Fermi surface, supporting earlier theoretical proposals for this phase and suggesting measurable correlations for future experiments.
ai_technology: Quantum-classical QuCl approach using a correlator convolutional neural network and regularization-path analysis
organization: Cornell University; The Ohio State University; Google Research; Harvard University; Ewha Womans University

title: High-resolution machine-learning catalog outlines a potential unmapped fault in the Weiyuan shale-gas region
summary: A machine-learning event detector combined with waveform cross-correlation produced a high-resolution catalog for injection-induced seismicity in the Weiyuan area, identifying one-third more earthquakes than the routine catalog and improving magnitude completeness. Spatial migration patterns show a pore-pressure diffusion front; a cluster outlines a potential unmapped fault that may have hosted the region’s largest recorded event, the September 2019 Mw 5.2 earthquake.
ai_technology: Machine-learning earthquake detector combined with waveform cross-correlation (the abstract does not name a particular detector architecture)
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Sichuan Earthquake Agency

title: EQTransformer-based catalog reveals a 50-km-deep outer-rise fault at the Southern Mariana trench
summary: Applying EQTransformer phase detection to near-field ocean-bottom seismometer recordings collected near the Challenger Deep yielded more than 1,975 earthquakes. Relocation and waveform-similarity clustering outlined a southern Mariana outer-rise fault extending approximately 20–50 km below the seafloor (about 50 km maximum depth), inferred to be a reactivated normal fault; the depth suggests more incoming-plate water input than prior estimates.
ai_technology: EQTransformer machine-learning seismic phase detector
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Chinese Academy of Sciences; Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology; Southern University of Science and Technology; Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution

title: Deep learning identifies 216 previously unrecognized Green Pea galaxies in DESI Legacy Survey imaging
summary: A MobileMamba-ECA image classifier searched DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys data and surfaced 775 Green Pea galaxy candidates. Cross-matching with DESI DR1 spectroscopy established 216 as previously unreported Green Pea galaxies: although spectra existed, the standard DESI pipeline had classified them only as generic galaxies. The study’s remaining 511 photometric-only objects are follow-up candidates and are not included in the confirmed count.
ai_technology: MobileMamba-ECA deep-learning classifier (Mamba state-space backbone with efficient channel attention)
organization: Shandong University; National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: CNN-guided spectroscopy confirms 28 new extremely metal-poor galaxies
summary: A three-stage convolutional-neural-network pipeline screened more than 7.7 million SDSS DR17 imaging sources lacking SDSS spectra, then selected targets for observation. Follow-up spectra of 45 candidates confirmed all as metal-poor galaxies, including 28 newly discovered extremely metal-poor systems; 18 have weak or undetected [N II] lines and oxygen-abundance upper limits.
ai_technology: Three-stage CNN characterization pipeline (metal-poor galaxy classifier, XMP classifier, and N2-index predictor)
organization: University of California, Davis; Durham University; Isaac Newton Group of Telescopes; Southern Astrophysical Research Telescope

title: MSFA-Net and Balmer-line fitting identify 3,583 new blue horizontal-branch stars
summary: A two-stage deep-learning pipeline searched LAMOST DR12 spectra and retained 27,853 BHB candidate spectra. After removal of previously known objects, stringent Balmer-line-profile fitting, and deduplication, the authors report 3,583 unique newly identified blue horizontal-branch stars. Gaia photometry provides an additional consistency check.
ai_technology: MSFA-Net, a multi-scale and frequency-attention deep neural network, followed by a binary refinement classifier
organization: National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: WDNet-guided DESI follow-up confirms 75 new white dwarfs and 7 cataclysmic variables
summary: WDNet detected candidates in DESI Legacy Surveys DR9 images. The researchers cross-matched 18,242 photometric candidates with DESI DR1 spectra, obtaining 719 candidate spectra; manual visual inspection of those spectra identified 75 new white dwarfs and 7 new cataclysmic variables. These spectroscopic classifications, not the much larger image-candidate list, are the reported verified sample.
ai_technology: WDNet, a deep-learning object-detection network based on YOLOv8 with multi-scale feature fusion
organization: Shandong University; National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Yunding Technology

title: Deep-learning-enhanced Sparta earthquake catalog resolves a shallow multifault rupture
summary: For the 2020 Mw 5.1 Sparta, North Carolina sequence, an EQTransformer-based catalog combined with matched-filter detections and differential-time relocations contains 1,761 high-precision events, about 5.8 times the original NEIC count. The denser locations resolve several shallow clusters and support the authors’ interpretation that the mainshock nucleated near the intersection of a blind strike-slip fault and a reverse fault associated with the surface rupture; moment-tensor inversion places its centroid at about 1.3 km depth.
ai_technology: Earthquake Transformer (EQTransformer) deep-learning phase/event detector, followed by matched-filter detection and differential-time relocation
