organization: Georgia Institute of Technology; University of Science and Technology of China; North Carolina State University; Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Crystal-graph learning and DFT identify 19,512 additional thermodynamically stable materials
summary: The authors trained crystal-graph attention networks on an expanded, composition- and symmetry-balanced dataset and used them to search 2,500 binary and ternary structure prototypes covering about one billion inorganic compounds. Density-functional-theory validation identified 19,512 additional compounds on the calculated thermodynamic convex hull and about 150,000 more within 50 meV/atom of it; the paper also analyzed predicted superconducting and superhard materials and compounds with large gap deformation potentials.
ai_technology: Crystal-graph attention neural networks trained on expanded density-functional-theory materials data
organization: Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg; University of Coimbra; Friedrich Schiller University Jena

title: Unsupervised clustering links deep-earthquake scaling to hydration differences among northwest Pacific slabs
summary: K-means clustering of Japan Meteorological Agency deep-earthquake catalogs separated the northwest Pacific slab segments; Gutenberg–Richter analysis found a magnitude 3.7–3.8 kink in Honshu and Izu seismicity, with b values falling from about 1.4–1.7 to 0.6–0.7. The authors infer that small-event excess and an approximately kilometre-scale metastable-olivine-wedge rim may reflect deep hydration and enhanced transformational faulting.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine-learning clustering (K-means, checked against spectral clustering and Gaussian mixture models)
organization: Michigan State University; Freie Universität Berlin; Université d’Orléans–CNRS; University of California, Los Angeles; Yale University

title: Machine-learning denoising exposes strong size scaling in deep-earthquake rupture parameters
summary: A multitask neural denoiser recovered teleseismic P-wave pulses from deep Mw 5.0+ earthquakes that had previously been too noisy for source analysis. The study found moment–duration scaling M₀ ∼ τ⁴, stress-drop scaling Δσ ∼ M₀⁰·²¹ and radiated-energy scaling Eᵣ ∼ M₀¹·²⁴; deep events had a median radiation efficiency near 5%, weak directivity and few subevents. After accounting for rigidity, no systematic depth trend in duration, stress drop or radiated energy remained across 100–700 km.
ai_technology: DenoTe, a transfer-learned multitask convolutional encoder–decoder neural network
organization: University of Washington, Department of Earth and Space Sciences

title: Machine-learning classification shows rigidity-corrected moment release is similar across earthquake depths
summary: Random-forest classification of source-time-function characteristics for 3,675 global Mw > 5.5 earthquakes showed that depth-dependent rigidity explains much of the differences in rupture duration, length and stress drop between shallow, intermediate and deep earthquakes. Once medium rigidity is corrected, the analyzed events exhibit similar moment-release processes, supporting a constant-strain-drop interpretation across depths and host-rock types.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning classification and feature-importance analysis
organization: University of Science and Technology of China; Mengcheng National Geophysical Observatory

title: CNN-augmented focal mechanisms reveal stress-linked faulting changes around major southern California earthquakes
summary: CNN phase and first-motion pickers supplied additional waveform polarities and arrivals for a 297,478-event southern California focal-mechanism catalog, about 40% larger than the prior catalog. The authors used the expanded catalog to observe systematic post-mainshock faulting-style changes spatially correlated with estimated static stress perturbations from the 2010 El Mayor–Cucapah and 2019 Ridgecrest earthquakes, including changes more than 100 km from the epicentres.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural networks for seismic phase arrival and first-motion polarity picking
organization: University of Southern California; California Institute of Technology; University of Southern California Southern California Earthquake Center

title: Random-forest selection and spectroscopy identify 20 new high-redshift quasars
summary: A supervised random-forest search of Pan-STARRS1 and WISE photometry identified follow-up targets in the difficult redshift range around z≈5.5, where quasars resemble red and brown dwarfs. Spectroscopic observations of 37 candidates confirmed 20 previously unknown high-redshift quasars (18 at z=4.6–5.5 and two around z≈5.7), including a source outside common color-cut selections.
ai_technology: Supervised random-forest classification and regression applied to Pan-STARRS1 and WISE data
organization: Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Steward Observatory, University of Arizona; Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics; European Southern Observatory; other international observatories

title: CNN tracking reveals irradiation-driven nanovoid size fluctuations and shrinkage in copper
summary: A convolutional neural network combined with greedy matching to detect, track and measure pre-existing nanovoids in in-situ TEM videos of irradiated copper. The analysis revealed non-monotonic, random-walk-like size fluctuations and shrinkage during irradiation; phase-field simulations were used to investigate the mechanism. Follow-up manual measurements and additional experiments confirmed the size-fluctuation observation.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network for void detection, with greedy matching for tracking and migration analysis
organization: Purdue University; University of Hong Kong; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen

title: Physics-guided machine learning links Southern Ocean regime shifts to a northward-shifting Antarctic Circumpolar Current
summary: Applying THOR to one eddy-permitting CM4 climate simulation, researchers detected a projected dynamical-regime shift where the Antarctic Circumpolar Current crosses the Pacific–Antarctic Ridge under the SSP5-8.5 scenario. Neural-network explanations and transport analysis attributed the modeled change to stronger wind stress shifting the current northward into less topographically constrained waters, where the flow intensifies. This is a model-based scenario result, not an observed future change.
ai_technology: THOR (Tracking global Heating with Ocean Regimes), using NEMI clustering, an ensemble of 50 multilayer perceptrons, SHAP and layer-wise relevance propagation
organization: University of California, Davis; NOAA Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory; European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts; Institut Pierre-Simon Laplace

title: Machine learning identifies a projected shift from DIC- to alkalinity-dominated ocean CO₂-flux variability
summary: Kernel ridge regression reconstructed present and future air–sea CO₂-flux variability in five Earth-system models. The analysis found dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) and alkalinity to be the main drivers, while DIC’s relative importance generally declines in warming scenarios—especially in the equatorial Pacific, Southern Ocean and North Atlantic—as anthropogenic carbon uptake flattens vertical DIC gradients. This result is conditional on the models and scenarios analyzed.
ai_technology: Kernel ridge regression and machine-learning clustering/classification
organization: NORCE Norwegian Research Centre; Bjerknes Centre for Climate Research

title: Machine-learning classification dates a tectonic transition and probable slab detachment in central Tibet
summary: A random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element data distinguished destructive from constructive plate-boundary signatures, with the paper reporting greater than 98% accuracy on its labeled evaluation set. Applied to basalts from Tibet’s Bangong–Nujiang suture zone, it found mixed signatures before about 108–107 Ma and only destructive-boundary signatures afterward; the authors interpret the transition as likely oceanic-slab detachment, consistent with other geological evidence.
ai_technology: Random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element concentrations

summary: A transformer trained to predict minimum Hamming distance, paired with a genetic algorithm and exact Brouwer–Zimmermann distance checks, found at least six previously unknown champion generalized toric codes over F₈ at dimensions 18, 22 and 38 (length 49). title: GPT-5.6 helps prove an exact mapping between frustrated and field-driven spin chains
summary: A single-author preprint proves that every finite one-dimensional open O(n) spin chain with arbitrary inhomogeneous nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions has an exact, temperature-independent Hamiltonian mapping to a simpler nearest-neighbor chain with axial single-spin potentials. A parallel result for q-state Potts chains yields a closed-form solution for every q ≥ 2 and finite chain length. title: Generative AI designs and experimentally validates an ultrathin broadband ENZ absorber
summary: A generative deep neural network searched multilayer indium-tin-oxide/aluminum-doped-zinc-oxide designs and selected an epsilon-near-zero absorber stack. After the researchers merged two similar adjacent layers for fabrication, the approximately 159-nm device experimentally maintained more than 98% absorption over a 1,077-nm near-infrared bandwidth at 49° p-polarized illumination. title: AI-assisted Hubble asteroid sample extends the shallow size-distribution slope to H≈20
summary: Using 632 serendipitously imaged Hubble Space Telescope asteroids found by the prior AI-assisted Hubble Asteroid Hunter survey, the authors fit trail parallax to estimate distances, absolute magnitudes, and approximate sizes. title: AI-guided CORONA imagery search finds four archaeologically verified tells in Abu Ghraib
summary: A fine-tuned deep-learning model trained with 1960s CORONA satellite images flagged eight previously unrecognized tell candidates in Iraq's Abu Ghraib district. title: Deep-learning ComPACT catalogue adds 116 previously unreported galaxy clusters
summary: Analysis of the CNN-detected ComPACT Sunyaev–Zel’dovich catalogue identified 116 previously unreported galaxy clusters with new redshift estimates, including five massive systems (M500c > 6 × 10^14 solar masses) at z > 0.7. title: PCFNet-guided spectroscopy confirms four protoclusters at redshift 3.3–3.4
summary: Subaru/MOIRCS spectroscopy of four PCFNet-selected candidate regions confirmed four protoclusters at z = 3.316, 3.403, 3.408 and 3.425, across three regions, with galaxy-density peaks more than five times the uniform distribution. title: AI-guided experiments uncover a new polymer polymorph and improve organic transistor performance
summary: An AI-powered advisor in an autonomous fabrication-and-test platform guided 64 trials of mixed ion–electron conducting polymers for organic electrochemical transistors. ai_technology: Adaptive AI decision interface and AI advisor integrated with autonomous electronic-material fabrication and testing
organization: The University of Chicago; Argonne National Laboratory; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of Southern Mississippi

title: Unsupervised learning separates rockfall and glacier-sliding precursors before the Blatten collapse
summary: Unsupervised clustering of 20 days of seismic data before the 28 May 2025 Blatten glacier collapse separated rockfall signals from events associated with basal glacier sliding. Sliding-related event counts accelerated approximately exponentially beginning about five days before collapse, with further acceleration about 1.5 days beforehand; the authors interpret this pattern as consistent with nucleation-like slip weakening.

title: Machine learning reconstructs deep-time crustal thickness and links thickening episodes with porphyry deposits
summary: A machine-learning mohometry model estimated paleo-crustal thickness from 66 geochemical proxies across subduction, collision and intraplate settings, extending chemical reconstruction beyond arc-related rocks. Tested reconstructions for southern Tibet and South China agreed with independently constrained crustal histories (R² = 0.937; RMSE = 4.3 km). title: MACE-guided screening yields three corundum high-entropy oxides and a cation-ordered oxide
summary: MACE-MP-0b2 interatomic-potential calculations screened 462 four- and five-cation trivalent-oxide compositions and selected 16 for synthesis. Experiments produced three phase-pure corundum high-entropy oxides—(Al,Cr,Fe,Ga)₂O₃, (Al,Cr,Fe,Rh,Sc)₂O₃ and (Cr,Fe,Ga,Rh,Sc)₂O₃—and a separate phase-pure cation-ordered (Al,Fe,Ga,Sc)₂O₃ oxide. title: LLM-guided experiments identify three phases unique to the ternary Co–Al–Ge system
summary: Researchers used an LLM to plan iterative composition measurements and experimentally mapped the Co–Al–Ge phase diagram at 900 °C. The domain-specific aLLoyM model directed early measurements into compositionally complex interior regions, enabling the earliest discovery of all three novel phases reported to form only in the ternary system; the general-purpose LLM strategy found more phases in fewer cycles. title: Machine-learning mapping finds broader preservation of pre-glacial landscapes across Arctic Canada and Greenland
summary: A random-forest model using six terrain morphometrics from ArcticDEM classified glacial erosional styles across Arctic Canada and Greenland. The map indicates that regions with little or no glacial erosion, and thus potentially preserved pre-glacial landscape fragments, occur more widely than previous mapping recognized; it also finds distinct morphologies between Greenland and Canada. The authors infer that inherited topography, ice dynamics, latitude and geology help shape these patterns.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning classifier
organization: Durham University; Newcastle University

title: Transformer-based SDSS search identifies two previously unreported optical–UV tidal disruption events
summary: A PCA-enhanced Transformer classifier screened 298,195 SDSS DR7 spectra and selected 14 TDE-like cases for secondary review. The authors report two newly identified TDEs: SDSS J124225.39+642919.0, whose GALEX UV source was present by the spectrum date (before 11 February 2002), and SDSS J152459.70+045423.1, whose TDE-H+He spectrum coincided with a Catalina optical outburst in 2007–08. title: Physics-informed generative learning yields experimentally verified single-phase B2 intermetallic alloys
summary: A conditional variational autoencoder and artificial neural network, using physics-informed descriptors of B2 sublattice ordering, generated and ranked compositions in complex alloy systems. Experimental synthesis and XRD/TEM characterization verified previously unreported single-phase B2 alloys, including three Fe–Co–Ni–Ti–Zr compositions, Co19.9Ni30.5Ti38.1Zr11.5, and Cu4.7Co9.2Ni36.4Ti38.7Zr7.4Hf3.5. title: Deep-learning denoising reveals new short-period seismic observations of known ultra-low-velocity zones
summary: A supervised deep-learning denoising autoencoder exposed previously undocumented short-period S-diffracted wave observations associated with several known ultra-low-velocity zones (ULVZs). It also revealed four Hawaiian-ULVZ S-diff post-cursor records at Japan F-net stations from East Pacific Rise earthquakes, providing ray paths with mean azimuth about 78° from earlier North American paths. title: AI-guided experiments uncover new zeolitic imidazolate framework crystals
summary: AIRES combined probabilistic machine-learning predictions with robotic synthesis, optical crystal screening and single-crystal X-ray diffraction to explore zinc zeolitic imidazolate frameworks. The campaign crystallized new structures using 10 of 48 previously untested linkers, doubling the discovery rate of random exploration (700 versus 1,400 experiments) and increasing the single-linker Zn-ZIF library by about one-third. title: LLM-guided alloy design yields self-limiting oxidation behavior at 900 °C
summary: A knowledge-enhanced AI workflow led to Co22Cr24Fe20Ni25Mo5Mn4, a non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy with experimentally observed single-phase FCC structure and self-limiting oxidation kinetics at 900 °C. After about 50 hours, the study reports a steady-state oxidation-rate constant of 1.41 × 10⁻⁸ mgⁿ cm⁻²ⁿ h⁻¹ (reaction order n = 45.35) and a Cr₂O₃/(Mn,Fe)Cr₂O₄ bilayer oxide scale. ai_technology: Physics-guided ML phase classifiers and LLM-assisted alloy-design workflow
organization: Shanghai University

title: First observation of single-top-quark production with a W and Z boson at CMS
summary: CMS reports the first observation of single-top-quark production in association with a W and Z boson in proton-proton collisions. A Particle Transformer classifier and improved reconstruction separated the rare tWZ signal from major backgrounds in three- and four-lepton events. Combining 13 and 13.6 TeV data (200 fb⁻¹), the measured signal has 5.8σ observed significance (3.5σ expected) and cross sections of 248 ± 52 fb at 13 TeV and 242 ± 77 fb at 13.6 TeV. ai_technology: Particle Transformer (ParT) multiclass classifier
organization: CMS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider

title: OmniFold enables an unbinned 24-dimensional Z+jets cross-section measurement by ATLAS
summary: Using 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, ATLAS simultaneously unfolded 24 correlated Z+jets kinematic observables with the machine-learning method OmniFold and released the particle-level result as an unbinned event dataset. The measured total fiducial cross section is 1,808 ± 42 fb; most illustrative differential bins have 3–5% total uncertainty, rising to about 15% in tails. The measurement is more precise than the compared predictions for many distributions, especially Sherpa. The event-level release also supports derived observables, including an infrared-and-collinear-safe τ₂₁ measurement in a specified fiducial region.

organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider

title: Deep learning expands the Utah FORGE DAS microearthquake catalog and resolves stimulation structure
summary: A ResNet-based DASEventNet model applied to continuous distributed acoustic sensing from the April 2022 Utah FORGE Well 16A (78)-32 stimulation manually verified 5,749 microearthquakes absent from the Silixa STA/LTA catalog; 45 of 5,794 model-positive windows were false detections on manual review. The study reports events down to Mw −1.80 versus −1.14 for STA/LTA and a broader Stage 3 seismicity distribution consistent with fracture geometry seen in an independent deep-borehole geophone catalog. title: XRD-guided learning identifies Li₆AsSe₅I as a room-temperature superionic conductor
summary: XRDMatch, a semi-supervised model using X-ray diffraction patterns as its descriptor, screened unlabeled crystal data and identified 38 lithium superionic-conductor predictions. The paper says 32 were supported by prior literature, six were new candidates assessed with ab initio molecular dynamics, and Li₆AsSe₅I was synthesized and experimentally confirmed as a superionic conductor. The source abstract does not establish that all 38 are new or experimentally validated; this record covers the single reported synthesized material.

title: PhaseNet-TF expands Tonga earthquake catalog and resolves the intermediate-depth double seismic zone
summary: A semi-supervised PhaseNet-TF workflow detected and relocated 13,616 events from a one-year Tonga OBS and land-station record, about 11 times the manually picked reference catalog. The denser catalog delineates the intermediate-depth double seismic zone to about 300 km and indicates that its lower plane is limited to roughly 19°–21°S, rather than continuous along the studied section. The study did not recover a deeper 350–460 km double zone; sparse events and location uncertainties limit inference at those depths.
ai_technology: PhaseNet-TF deep-learning phase picker with semi-supervised iterative retraining
organization: Michigan State University; Stanford University; University of California, Berkeley

title: LHCb observes the doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon with an 8.7σ global significance
summary: Using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton-proton collisions recorded in 2024, LHCb observed an Ωc⁰π⁺ mass peak with 8.7σ global significance and identified it as the weakly decaying doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon. The reported mass is 3725.9 ± 1.0 (stat) ± 0.2 (syst) ± 0.4 (lifetime) ± 0.6 (external) MeV/c². A boosted decision tree suppressed random-track combinatorial background; the result is a preprint submitted to Physical Review Letters.

organization: LHCb Collaboration; CERN

title: LHCb observes CP violation for the first time in baryon decays
summary: Using 9 fb⁻¹ of LHCb Run 1 and Run 2 data, the collaboration measured a phase-space-averaged CP asymmetry of (2.45 ± 0.46 ± 0.10)% in Λb⁰ → pK⁻π⁺π⁻ and its conjugate, a 5.2σ observation. In the resonance-dominated R(pπ⁺π⁻)K⁻ region, the asymmetry was (5.4 ± 0.9 ± 0.1)%, 6.0σ from zero. Machine-learning BDT selection suppressed combinatorial background; neural-network PID variables mitigated particle misidentification.
ai_technology: Boosted decision tree event classifier; neural-network particle-identification variables
organization: LHCb Collaboration; CERN

title: Dense-array seismicity analysis infers a buried fault beneath the Three Gorges Reservoir area
summary: A two-phase dense-array catalog processed with the LOC-FLOW machine-learning workflow revealed microseismicity in three zones and shallow (0–6 km) and deep (6–15 km) layers near the northern Xiannvshan Fault Zone. A steeply dipping seismic band is interpreted as a previously hidden western extension of the Tianyangping Fault; the authors also propose fluid-permeable connections between depth layers. The enhanced catalog detects over an order of magnitude more events than the regional network catalog for the same period.
ai_technology: LOC-FLOW machine-learning seismic catalog workflow
organization: Wuhan University of Technology; Institute of Seismology, China Earthquake Administration; collaborators

title: CMS makes the first hadron-collider observation of boosted Z→cc̄ decay
summary: In 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, CMS observed boosted Z→cc̄ production in association with jets for the first time at a hadron collider. The measured signal strength relative to the Standard Model prediction is 1.00 with combined uncertainty +0.19/−0.17. A deep neural network (DeepDoubleX) identified large-radius jets from charm-quark pairs; the paper also sets a 95% confidence-level upper limit of 47 times the Standard Model prediction on boosted H→cc̄ production.

organization: CMS Collaboration; CERN

title: t-SNE-selected LMC radio source receives a spectroscopic AGN classification at z = 2.80
summary: SALT spectroscopy of the previously unclassified source LMC tSNE b8 (R.A. 06:22:41.86, Dec. −68:59:21.9) identified it as an active galactic nucleus at redshift z = 2.80. The source was selected from the blazar-like sequence in a t-SNE map combining VISTA near-infrared and ASKAP radio survey data with multi-wavelength photometry. This is one specific spectroscopic classification from the paper’s broader follow-up sample.
ai_technology: t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding (t-SNE) applied to multi-wavelength source photometry

title: LHCb makes the first high-significance observation of the rare Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decay
summary: Using 5.4 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data collected in 2016–2018, LHCb observed 237 ± 16 Σ⁺ → pμ⁺μ⁻ decays and measured a branching fraction of (1.08 ± 0.17) × 10⁻⁸. The dimuon spectrum showed no evidence of resonant structures, and the results are compatible with Standard Model expectations. This is the first high-significance observation; earlier HyperCP and LHCb Run 1 results were evidence only.
ai_technology: LHCb boosted decision tree (BDT) classifier
organization: LHCb Collaboration; CERN

title: Spectroscopy validates machine-selected populations of obscured active galaxies
summary: Using a sample selected by unsupervised machine learning on optical and mid-infrared photometry, the team obtained 178 MMT spectra and found the brighter class was 85% Type I active galactic nuclei (AGN), with <3% non-AGN contamination, while a fainter class was 65% Type II AGN with 15% contamination, mainly star-forming galaxies. The follow-up showed that the machine-selected classes recover redder and more obscured AGN populations than typical optical spectroscopic samples.

title: PhaseNet catalog reveals a 2023 injection-linked earthquake cluster in the Raton Basin
summary: Applying PhaseNet-based phase picking to eight years of recordings from eight broadband stations, the study built a roughly 96,000-event Raton Basin catalog (local magnitudes −1 to 4.3) and resolved a previously unreported 2023 cluster with a Mw 4.3 event. Nearby wells had elevated injection volumes for about a year before the cluster; analysis of relocated events and 90 full centroid moment tensors also supports basement-rooted normal faults and possible elevated pore pressure. The authors interpret injection as a likely influence, not a demonstrated sole cause.

title: Graph neural network enables first observation of Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay
summary: Using 4.5 fb⁻¹ of BESIII electron–positron collision data, the collaboration reports the first observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay at greater than 10σ significance. It measures a branching fraction of (3.57 ± 0.34(stat) ± 0.14(syst)) × 10⁻³ and extracts |Vcd| = 0.208 ± 0.011(exp) ± 0.007(LQCD) ± 0.001(lifetime) for the first time from a charmed-baryon decay.

title: Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals scale-dependent fault controls at Gonghe geothermal site
summary: A machine-learning workflow catalogued 7,346 microearthquakes (ML −2.0 to 2.18) recorded during 2021 stimulation and circulation tests at China’s Gonghe enhanced-geothermal-system site. The catalog resolves a ring-shaped distribution with four clusters and varying faulting styles. The authors infer that site-scale seismicity reactivated mapped, pre-existing natural faults; at borehole scale, the principal seismogenic zone coincides with strong SHmax rotation. Stress modeling estimates a low fault-friction coefficient near 0.23 (95% CI 0.19–0.48) and the low-to-moderate fluid overpressure needed for slip.

title: ParticleNet enables first hadron-collider W-boson mass measurement from hadronic decays
summary: Using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton data, CMS reports the first measurement of the W-boson mass in an all-jets final state at a hadron collider: 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV. The result comes from unfolded groomed jet-mass distributions for boosted hadronic W+jets events. The mass-decorrelated ParticleNet graph neural network tagger provides the main result by selecting the W-jet sample and suppressing quark/gluon multijet background; a non-neural N₂ tagger is used as a cross-check.

organization: CMS Collaboration

title: ATLAS graph neural network enables first observation of four-top-quark production
summary: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS observed simultaneous production of four top quarks in same-sign dilepton and multilepton events, with 6.1σ observed (4.3σ expected) significance. The measured cross-section is 22.5⁺⁶·⁶₋₅·₅ fb, consistent with the Standard Model prediction within 1.8σ. A graph neural network separated the four-top signal from dominant backgrounds in the signal extraction.

organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

title: ATLAS boosted decision trees enable first observation of triple-W boson production
summary: In 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV LHC data, ATLAS observed simultaneous WWW production at 8.0σ (5.4σ expected) and measured an inclusive cross-section of 820 ± 100(stat) ± 80(syst) fb. The analysis selected same-sign dilepton-plus-jets and trilepton final states. Two boosted decision trees—one per channel—improved signal/background separation and supplied distributions for the fit. The measured rate is about 2.6σ above the Standard Model prediction, not a significant discrepancy.
ai_technology: Two boosted decision tree classifiers for the dilepton and trilepton channels
organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

title: Deep-learning lens search leads to first confirmed galaxy-scale lensed superluminous supernova
summary: The HOLISMOKES search identified the ZTF transient SN 2025wny at the position of the previously selected lens candidate PS1 J0716+3821. Follow-up imaging resolved multiple supernova images and spectroscopy classified it as a Type I superluminous supernova at z=2.008 ± 0.001; the second deflector galaxy was measured spectroscopically at z=0.375 ± 0.001. This is the first confirmed galaxy-scale strongly lensed supernova with expected time delays of days to weeks, offering a new system for time-delay cosmography.
ai_technology: Deep-learning Pan-STARRS 3π lens-candidate classification and transient-alert cross-matching pipeline
organization: Technical University of Munich; Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics; Technical University of Denmark; HOLISMOKES Collaboration

title: ATLAS graph neural network enables first LHC observation of single-top s-channel production
summary: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS reports the first observation of single-top-quark s-channel production at the LHC, with 5.1σ observed (5.2σ expected) significance. The measured cross-section is 10.8 ± 1.5(stat) ± 1.6(syst) pb, consistent with the Standard Model. A graph neural network discriminant separates the signal from top-pair, W+jets and t-channel single-top backgrounds; the analysis also uses broadened event acceptance, improved b tagging and refined modeling.
ai_technology: Event-level graph neural network; ATLAS GN2 graph-transformer b-jet tagger
organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

title: Boosted decision tree enables first observation of two simultaneously longitudinally polarized Z bosons
summary: Using 164 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton–proton data and a statistical combination with the Run 2 measurement, ATLAS reports the first observation of ZZ production with both Z bosons longitudinally polarized, at 6.5σ observed (5.6σ expected). The combined signal strength is 1.22 ± 0.21; the Run 3 measurement also reports polarization fractions across the fiducial phase space and two four-lepton invariant-mass ranges, consistent with Standard Model predictions.

organization: ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

title: AI-built Baihetan reservoir catalog reveals fault-controlled and depth-dependent seismicity
summary: LOC-FLOW analysis of 55 stations and continuous waveforms from January 2021 to July 2022 identified 53,838 events around China’s Baihetan Reservoir, about four times the manual catalog, with reported relative location errors of tens of metres and recall of about 99% of manual events. The authors infer that post-impoundment seismicity is concentrated along regional structures and fractures, differs across the Jinsha River, and includes migration away from the inundation zone and with depth. They report depth-dependent b-value and water-depth/event-rate patterns consistent with different shallow and deep controls.
ai_technology: LOC-FLOW automated earthquake-detection and location workflow using PhaseNet deep-learning phase picking

title: Machine learning guided discovery of enhanced anomalous Hall resistivity in Fe–Ir–Pt films
summary: A machine-learning screen trained on experimental Fe–heavy-element binary alloys pointed to a ternary Fe–Ir–Pt composition range with enhanced anomalous Hall effect. High-throughput composition-spread measurements experimentally found a peak anomalous Hall resistivity of 6.5 μΩ·cm, above the prior 5.25 μΩ·cm maximum reported for Fe–X binary systems. Scaling analysis attributed the enhancement to an extrinsic contribution.

title: Bayesian optimization experimentally identifies a high-AHE Fe–Co–Ni–Ta–Ir amorphous film
summary: An autonomous closed-loop search combining composition-spread experiments with Bayesian optimization reached a maximum anomalous Hall resistivity of 10.9 μΩ·cm in an amorphous Fe44.9Co27.9Ni12.1Ta3.3Ir11.7 thin film deposited at room temperature. This measured value exceeded the study’s target of 10 μΩ·cm and the values found in the initial random-exploration cycles.

title: AI-assisted work proves a Latin-square imbalance bound, with optimal examples through order 52
summary: A collaborative LLM-plus-symbolic-computation study proved that every n×n Latin square with n ≡ 1 (mod 3) has imbalance at least 4n(n−1)/9. It introduced near-perfect permutations that attain the bound and computationally found independently verified matching examples for every such order from 4 through 52. The universal lower-bound theorem was formally checked in Lean 4.

title: Recurrent neural network reveals near-critical seeding of topological defects in Kibble–Zurek simulations
summary: In numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg phase transition, a recurrent neural network predicted the final locations of topological defects from short sequences of order-parameter fluctuations during the Kibble–Zurek impulse regime, before freeze-out and before the defects were macroscopically visible. Prediction error across quench rates followed power-law scaling consistent with the Kibble–Zurek freeze-out time, indicating that information about the eventual defect pattern is encoded in near-critical fluctuations in this model.

title: Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals transform fault in the Zabargad Fracture Zone
summary: A 12-month network of ocean-bottom and land seismometers yielded a high-resolution catalog of more than 3,900 earthquakes in the northern Red Sea Zabargad Fracture Zone and Mabahiss Deep. The southern cluster’s diffuse seismicity and predominantly left-lateral strike-slip focal mechanisms reveal a NE–SW transform fault, which the authors describe as possibly in an early development stage. A tested PtFeCu formulation showed about 3.1-fold higher specific activity (776 μA cm⁻² Pt) and 3.2-fold higher mass activity (0.67 A mg⁻¹ Pt) than Pt/C at 0.9 V; the authors attribute activity and improved durability to Cu-dependent surface-strain modulation and reduced Fe segregation, supported by calculations and experimental tests.

title: Robot-guided optimization identifies six non-aqueous electrolytes with improved fast-charge performance
summary: A closed-loop platform paired Clio, an automated electrolyte-formulation and conductivity-testing robot, with Dragonfly Bayesian optimization. In 42 experiments over two workdays, it selected six non-aqueous electrolyte formulations from a LiPF₆ and EC/EMC/DMC design space. The team tested these formulations in 220 mAh graphite‖NMC pouch cells; all showed improved fast-charging capability relative to a baseline electrolyte selected in advance from the same design space. The search reached its reported target about six times faster than random search using the same automated setup.

title: Active-learning search experimentally realizes a high-zT Cu₁₋ₓAgₓGaTe₂ thermoelectric
summary: Compressed-sensing symbolic regression and active learning screened the Cu₁₋ₓAgₓGaTe₂ thermoelectric series and guided synthesis of selected compositions. summary: An adaptive-learning design-of-experiments loop guided robotic high-throughput synthesis of Fe–N–C oxygen-reduction electrocatalysts across a six-dimensional process/composition space. title: Machine-learning unmixing links acid rain and subsurface flowpaths to watershed CO₂ drawdown
summary: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was applied to stream-chemistry time series from three watersheds to infer solute endmembers and their changing contributions without predefining endmember chemistry. Combined with geological interpretation and independent geochemical evidence, the model separated shallow acid-rain-affected flow from deeper pyrite-weathering contributions. The analysis found that acid rain can reduce a watershed’s long-timescale CO₂-sequestration capacity and that omitting sulfide oxidation/acid-rain reactions overestimates weathering-driven CO₂ drawdown.

title: CNN-assisted search confirms quadruply lensed quasar PS J2107−1611
summary: A convolutional neural network trained on simulated lens images screened 27,760 preselected quasar candidates with multiple nearby Pan-STARRS detections. summary: A Chain of Symbolic Regression (CoSR) analysis of hypersonic simulation data derived an interpretable non-power-product scaling relation for axial-force coefficient across sharp-cone and blunt-body configurations. It combines angle of attack, Mach number and Reynolds number through a dominant term and a viscous correction; the relation has a shared functional form but geometry-specific fitted constants. title: Active learning discovers three high-entropy thermoelectrics with zT above 2
summary: A Gaussian-process model and Bayesian active-learning loop used an average thermoelectric quality factor as a physics-informed descriptor to search a nine-element chalcogenide composition space of 16,206 candidates. summary: A noise-aware Kriging model with active-learning acquisition selected candidate compositions from a million-composition NiTi-based alloy design space. title: Machine learning derives new idealized ocean-eddy momentum and heat-flux closures
summary: Relevance-vector-machine sparse regression applied to high-resolution idealized ocean simulations produced compact momentum and temperature-flux closures for coarse grids. title: Satellite-image clustering guides discovery of four late Miocene fossil sites in Mozambique’s Urema Rift
summary: Unsupervised k-means clustering of seven Landsat 8 spectral bands highlighted a small set of priority areas for paleontological field survey in Gorongosa National Park. summary: A graph-based machine-learning model and closed-loop active-learning experiments identified a four-metal perovskite oxide with an intrinsic oxygen-evolution overpotential of 391 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²oxide, among the lowest reported for four-metal perovskite oxides. summary: A two-stage 1D CNN pipeline applied to continuous three-component seismic waveforms from one L’Aquila station identified 273 previously uncataloged local earthquake events during a one-month 2009 foreshock period. summary: scDORI inferred enhancer-linked regulatory networks from single-cell multiome data and prioritized regulators for perturbation. summary: The accepted-paper abstract reports that DeltaCata, a geometric graph neural network predicting mutation effects on enzyme kinetics, guided engineering of methyltransferase sGmOMT2. summary: Classifiers and UMAP analyzed 129,676 prenatal-test cfDNA samples, with genotype checks in 169 selected samples. summary: Using actively fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potentials with experimental validation, the authors report that cation disorder improves lithium-path connectivity but broadens site energies, suppressing diffusion in disordered-rocksalt cathodes. summary: GenDIReCT used diffusion-based reconstruction conditioned on calibration-independent closure invariants to analyze EHT observations from 2017, 2018 and 2021. summary: A preprint reports external validation of an ECG-image ensemble for Takotsubo syndrome versus anterior STEMI in 95 participants: accuracy 0.914 and AUC 0.970. summary: The November 13, 2026 paper introduces WenHai-E2E, which generates global eddy-resolving ocean forecasts directly from observations and reports better forecast accuracy than a numerical system. summary: A Dartmouth preprint studied which language-model features predict human neural responses during naturalistic listening. summary: The journal abstract describes CochleaNet, a deep-learning framework for cleared-cochlea light-sheet images, covering hair cells, spiral ganglion neurons, synapses, tonotopy and gene expression. summary: The journal abstract reports that machine-learning-assisted database mining identified 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates.
